News.title: Outrage as monster dad who raped daughter, 18, before she killed herself is FREED after just five months in jail
News.content:
EVIL DAD FREED Outrage as monster dad who raped daughter, 18, before she killed herself is FREED after just five months in jail







Next

A MONSTROUS dad who raped his own teenage daughter before she took her own life has been freed after just five months in jail.

Stephen Vincent Chavez, 41, admitted in May to sexually abusing his biological daughter Makayla, 18, after supplying her with alcohol.



Prosecutors said he acknowledged abusing a position of trust and targeting a vulnerable victim.

Makayla later took her own life in December 2025, just five months after the horrific assault in July that year.



The dad was sentenced to one year in Ventura County Jail in June as well as three years probation.

According to an inmate record for Chavez, he is due to be released on November 9.

READ MORE US NEWS VILE ACT Sick pics of dead student 'sent in texts by man after drugging and raping her'



The case previously sparked outrage after it was revealed that Chavez would only get three years in jail.

Prosecutors said it was the maximum prison sentence they could seek under current law.



The incestuous crimes took place while Makayla was staying with Chavez at his home in Moorpark, Southern California.

The teenager had reportedly relocated from North Carolina to attend college in the hope of beginning a new chapter in her life.

Ventura County DA officials said: “After a day of drinking at a family gathering, Chavez purchased additional alcohol for him and his daughter to drink at home.



“Chavez then engaged in sexual intercourse with her.”

Makayla was hospitalised after the assault, and a rape kit confirmed the presence of Chavez’s DNA.

She then died by suicide months later.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

Ventura County Deputy District Attorney Tessa McCarty said the teen had trusted Chavez to care for her after moving across the country to live with him.



She said: “[Chavez] violated this trust and shattered the father-daughter relationship in an unimaginable way, conduct for which prison is the only appropriate sentence.”

Prosecutors reportedly spent months examining whether additional charges – including rape – could be legally pursued.

The District Attorney’s Office said the investigation included “multiple interviews, additional forensic testing, medical evaluations and an extensive review of electronic evidence”.

“After doing so and convening a team of the office’s top sexual assault prosecutors to review the findings, the District Attorney’s Office is confident that this case was properly charged based upon the law, facts and evidence presented,” it said.

Makayla’s mother, Carolina Sandoval, previously expressed deep frustration at the statutory limits of the case.



She said: “Based on the charges, the most that he can get is three years and 20 years as a registered sex offender.

“It just feels like… my daughter’s life is only worth three years.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The heartbroken mother said Chavez got her daughter intoxicated and took advantage of her physically and mentally.

She said: “So if that’s not rape, I really don’t know what is.”

News.title: UK’s terrifying e-scooter ‘Wild West’ revealed as deaths rise & grieving mum begs: ‘don’t get your kid one at Christmas’
News.content:
KILLER TREND UK’s terrifying e-scooter ‘Wild West’ revealed as deaths rise & grieving mum begs: ‘don’t get your kid one at Christmas’







Next

CHILDREN as young as NINE dying, headteachers being told to “dob in” pupils who arrive on them, and A&E departments battling rapidly increasing casualties.

This is the impact of Britain’s worrying wave of deadly e-scooter incidents, causing police, traumatised parents and senior hospital staff to issue parents a blunt message: do not buy them as toys for your kids this Christmas.



Recent data from the Parliamentary Advisory Council for Transport Safety (PACTS) revealed that, to date, 66 people had died in crashes involving e-scooters – with many more seriously injured including a girl, nine, in Wellingborough, Northants., last month.

It was a different story in 2019 when, before they became mainstream, just one person lost their life.



TV presenter and influencer Emily Hartridge, 35, was Britain’s first e-scooter victim when she was killed after the vehicle she was riding collided with a lorry in Battersea, London.

An inquest subsequently found it had an under-inflated tyre, causing her to lose control.

Fast forward six years to 2025 and there were 12 deaths, including the heartbreaking case of nine-year-old Darcie Casselden.

She was riding an e-scooter when she died alongside her 16-year-old brother Roman in a hit-and-run in Basildon, Essex.



Carly Calland’s son, Jacob, 14, also died that year when, in March, the e-scooter he was a pillion passenger on travelled onto a dual carriageway and through a red light.

“The increase in the number of people dying is terrifying,” the campaigner told The Sun.

“It’s a ‘Wild West’ out there. It’s illegal to ride e-scooters on public land like pavements or roads, but people don’t realise.

“You don’t have to wear protective gear. Helmets aren’t mandatory. There’s no central legislation but these vehicles can hit 28mph.

“It’s so dangerous. We need people to sing from the same hymn sheet regarding legislation but that isn’t currently happening. It shouldn’t take another death for it to.”



Carly had asked Jacob never to go on an e-scooter but he disobeyed her, leaving the house when she was at her mum’s.

By the time she reached him after finding out he had been involved in an accident, he was lying on the road. He was rushed to hospital but went into cardiac arrest and didn’t regain consciousness.

He died in Carly’s arms as she whispered “I love you” to him.



The other boy, who cannot be named for legal reasons, appeared at Manchester Crown Court earlier this year where he admitted causing death by dangerous driving and was given an 18-month youth referral order and a five-year driving ban.

“In the 17 months since Jacob died there have been 14 people killed because of e-scooters – nearly one a month,” said Carly, from Manchester.

“That cannot be allowed to continue. With Christmas coming up, more and more parents will be buying their kids e-scooters – they need to know how dangerous they can be. Please don’t get one for your child.”

Carly, also mum to Jaxley, eight, said her focus was on “education”.

“Jacob is constantly in my thoughts, every day I think about him,” she recalled. “I wish it had not happened to him and he wasn’t dead, but perhaps he was meant to die to save other people.”



She is supported in her campaign by Greater Manchester Police.

DC Steve Pennington, from the force, warned: “E-scooters are not harmless toys and they can lead to horrific consequences when used by inexperienced riders and without the due care required.

“I would urge parents to check what their children are using.”

Just last week, Humberside Police, along with the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner for Humberside, launched a campaign to educate children, parents and guardians about the dangers and legal restrictions surrounding e-scooters ahead of Christmas.

Inspector Pete Musgrave said: “It’s important people understand they are not toys and there are strict laws governing their use.”



Medics have also backed Carly’s campaign after a new report revealed three trauma centres in Liverpool, Manchester, and Sheffield had treated 477 under-16 e-scooter patients since 2019. Before this, the number was fewer than 10.

Similarly, the Royal Hospital for Children in Scotland revealed that the number of children who attended A&E in Greater Glasgow and Clyde due to e-scooter and e-bike accidents shot up by a staggering 600 per cent, with doctors treating kids with injuries as severe as major head trauma and broken legs.

Major Trauma Coordinator at the hospital, Mark Lilley, said the increase was “alarming”.

“We know e-scooters are popular and may feature on many Christmas wish lists, but the risks are significant,” he warned.

“A fall at speed can cause life-changing head or brain injuries. We have seen the trauma these accidents bring to families, and we strongly urge parents to reconsider before buying one for a child.”



Other doctors shared his concerns, adding they had seen kids with head injuries, broken bones and in need of surgery.

Children’s Major Trauma Coordinator at Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital, Caroline Rushmer, said they “weren’t toys”, adding: “They’re dangerous and their high speed makes them unsuitable for children and young people.”

Meanwhile, following the death of 14-year-old Aaron Rowe in Lincoln in September in an e-scooter crash, Lincolnshire County Council wrote to all the county’s schools and asked them to report pupils arriving on e-scooters.



Principal of Lincoln University Technical College, Stuart Hamer, told the BBC it was a necessary move.

“My foremost concern is the welfare of my students and if that’s dobbing them in, because that’s going to get a hard message home, then that’s got to be the way we go.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Referring to Jacob’s death specifically, a Department for Transport spokeswoman told The Sun: “This was a tragic incident, and our thoughts are with Jacob’s family.”

They added: “It remains illegal to use privately owned e-scooters in public spaces, and we’re bringing forward new laws to make their use safe, including consulting on potential requirements like helmets, registration and insurance.”

News.title: Joe Biden, 83, shares heartbreaking cancer update as former President prepares to release memoir
News.content:
Next

FORMER President Joe Biden has shared an emotional update on his cancer battle as he prepares to release his highly anticipated memoir.

The 83-year-old opened up about his health struggles in a candid message to supporters on Sunday, revealing how the disease affected his plans.



Biden admitted his cancer diagnosis has slowed him down, forcing him to scale back public appearances to promote his upcoming book.

The former president, who was diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer last year, said his doctors remain encouraged by his response to treatment.



But he confessed that “some days are better than others” as he continues his health battle.

“While writing the book, I was diagnosed with cancer, a disease known all too well to millions of Americans and their families,” Biden wrote on X.



“Some days are better than others. It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.”

His memoir, Promise Me, America, is set to hit shelves on November 17.

The book will offer Biden’s account of his four years in the White House, including the challenges he faced and the decisions that shaped his presidency.

“It covers my years as President. The challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them. It’s about who we are as a nation,” Biden said.



“What we stand for. And America’s role in the world. More than anything, it’s about my faith in the American people and the great American experiment in self-governance and democracy.”

Biden’s latest admission comes just weeks after he issued a deeply personal warning to men about the importance of early cancer detection.

Marking Prostate Awareness Month in October, the former president revealed that the disease had already spread by the time doctors discovered it.

“By the time we found it, it had already spread to my bones,” Biden wrote on social media.

“When prostate cancer is caught early, the five-year survival is close to 100%.”



Biden completed a course of radiation treatment in October 2025 after being diagnosed with stage four prostate cancer earlier that year.

He later praised the medical professionals caring for him, saying the treatment had worked as intended.

“Their skill, dedication, and compassion mean so much. The radiation treatment from last fall worked as intended, and I continue to do the things I care about, like finishing my memoir,” he said.

However, his son Hunter Biden previously painted a grim picture of the former president’s condition.

Speaking in August, Hunter described his father’s cancer as “very debilitating” and revealed the toll it had taken on him.



“The cancer has spread, metastasized into his bones and further,” Hunter said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s very painful, and it’s very debilitating in many respects.”

Biden’s upcoming memoir follows the release of his wife Jill Biden’s book, A View from the East Wing, which was published in June.

News.title: Plan to spy on benefit cheats’ bank accounts SCRAPPED by Chancellor in blow to taxpayer
News.content:
SNOOP-U-TURN Plan to spy on benefit cheats’ bank accounts SCRAPPED by Chancellor in blow to taxpayer







Next

CHANCELLOR John Healey has scrapped plans to crack down on benefit fraud by snooping on claimants’ bank accounts.

The proposal would have enabled officials at the Department of Work and Pensions (DWP) to pry on the savings of people claiming benefits.



Under the current criteria, anyone with more than £16,000 in savings is ineligible for Universal Credit.

It follows former chancellor Rachel Reeves‘ assertions last spring that claimaints would have their bank accounts scrutinised to ensure they weren’t playing the system.



Benefit fraud currently costs the Treasury nearly £10bn a year.

Mrs Reeves insisted the policy would help tackle these enormous losses.

But now, DWP ministers have asked banks to scan accounts after they have received Universal Credit, then submit findings to the Government.

These delayed checks could lead to a surge in benefit scams from first-time claimaints, experts have warned.

Mr Healey’s plans to U-turn on the original snooping policy will cost taxpayers £5m this year and another £10m next year.

Reports by The Telegraph expect the welfare bill to balloon by 2032, from £352bn to £431bn.



While state pension will account for around half of this figure, the increase will also be partly driven by youth unemployment reforms, analysts claim.

Youth work schemes, recommended by former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn, will resemble Germany and Denmark’s mobility models, which cost around 0.3 of the GDP annually.

An equivalent increase in the UK would come to around £6bn, according to the Telegraph.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is expected to respond to these policy reforms early next year – as well as a separate probe into health-related benefits.

Tories criticised Mr Healey’s abandonment of the welfare claims probe, accusing Labour of a “complete surrender” on the pressing topic.



Helen Whatley, the shadow work and pensions secretary, said: “There will be no savings in this Parliament and they don’t even want to make savings over the next decade.

“Millions of people are trapped on benefits and hardworking taxpayers are being forced to foot an ever-growing bill.

“We desperately need a Government with the backbone to tackle our broken welfare system.”

Despite the Chancellor backtracking on bank account inspections, energy companies have been given the green light to examine their customers’ incomes, tax records and property valuations.

A spokesperson for DWP said: “This Government is determined to crack down on fraud and error and protect taxpayers’ money.



“The previous Open Banking proposal relied on claimant consent and could not be used in every Universal Credit claim.

“We are instead introducing the Eligibility Verification Measure (EVM), which will require banks and financial institutions to provide information where accounts meet specified criteria, giving DWP a more consistent way to identify incorrect payments and tackle fraud and error.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This is just one part of a comprehensive programme to tackle fraud, error and debt and EVM is expected to save £1.2bn by 2030-31.”

News.title: Missing schoolgirl, 13, found dead in abandoned farmhouse in Germany after neighbours ‘ignored repeated cries for help’
News.content:
CRIES IGNORED Missing schoolgirl, 13, found dead in abandoned farmhouse in Germany after neighbours ‘ignored repeated cries for help’







Next

A MISSING schoolgirl has been found dead in an abandoned farmhouse after neighbours reportedly ignored her cries for help.

Cops discovered the suspect critically injured beside 13-year-old Lisa Ta’s body at a remote property five days after she vanished in Berlin, Germany.



The tragic find was made when the owner of the abandoned property in Altglietzen arrived to find the door open and the two individuals inside, prompting an urgent call to police.

It is unclear how long she had been dead following the grim discovery near the Polish border, more than 31 miles from her home, around midday on Sunday.



Neighbours reportedly told investigators they heard cries for help coming from the abandoned farmhouse in the days prior to Sunday.

Lisa was last seen on Tuesday after she left her apartment in the German capital and headed to her school in Sella-Hasse-Strasse but she never arrievd.

Her 17-year-old sister Linda told local media: “She didn’t reply anymore.”

Linda had insisted that her younger sister would never have disappeared voluntarily.



She said: “She wouldn’t run away, that’s not like her.

“We’re extremely worried.”

A huge police operation was launched to find the missing teen, including around 220 officers, specialist search teams, sniffer dogs and a police helicopter.

The investigation was taken over by Berlin’s homicide squad on Friday after prosecutors said there were indications that a serious crime had been committed.

When police eventually found her body, the suspect was discovered injured beside her after a suspected botched suicide attempt.



He was taken to hospital in a critical condition and it is not clear if he will survive his self-inflicted injuries.

One resident told local media that a suspicious vehicle had been parked outside the farmhouse for hours on the day of her disappearance.

She said: “A car with Berlin registration plates stood outside the property for hours with its hazard lights on.

“That struck me as strange. It was gold-coloured, not an estate car, I think an Opel. The next day the car was gone.”

Other residents also reported hearing cries for help in recent days, although it remains unclear why nobody contacted police at the time.



The suspected killer’s identity has not yet been established.

An autopsy is planned to establish Lisa’s cause of death and investigators are also examining whether a sexual offence may have been committed.

Lisa’s mother, Nguyen Hoai Xoan, had previously appealed to the Vietnamese community in Germany to help spread information about her daughter’s disappearance.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She said: “Mum only hopes that you come home safe and healthy. Mum misses you so much.”

Police from Berlin and Brandenburg are continuing their investigation into the circumstances of Lisa’s death, including the events leading up to her disappearance and the identity of the suspected perpetrator.

News.title: Boy, 5, ‘killed by cousin to harvest organs for quick cash’ as mutilated body found wrapped in blanket in shallow grave
News.content:
PURE EVIL Boy, 5, ‘killed by cousin to harvest organs for quick cash’ as mutilated body found wrapped in blanket in shallow grave







Next

A FIVE-year-old boy has allegedly been murdered by his cousin in a twisted plot to harvest the child’s organs for quick cash.

Accused killer Basudev, known as Tangnu, was arrested by police in Jashpur district, India in connection with the horrific slaying.

He is suspected of luring Jitendra Ram, 5, away with alcohol, before killing him, removing several organs and dumping his body in a shallow grave.



The horror case emerged after Jitendra’s dad, Ramjit Ram, reported his son missing from their home in Sanna village on November 7.



The family, who had moved there around a year earlier for work, lived in a temporary hut near a dam.

Basudev, a relative from a nearby village, was reportedly known to visit them occasionally.

He arrived at the family’s hut on the morning of November 5 and invited Ramjit and another man to drink alcohol, according to the complaint.



After Basudev left for the bus later that day, Ramjit returned home to find his son missing.

The family immediately launched a search.

During their efforts, locals reportedly told them Jitendra had last been seen with Basudev.

Relatives then searched nearby villages, fields and surrounding areas but could not find the boy.



Two days later, on the morning of November 7, a villager spotted a suspicious sack inside a water-filled pit near a field.

When it was opened, the body of the missing child was allegedly found wrapped in a blanket and quilt and partially covered with soil.

Police were called to the scene and launched a murder investigation.

Basudev was swiftly detained and questioned, allegedly confessing that he led Jitendra to a hut in a field after leaving the family’s home.

Police claim he bought alcohol and a chicken, returned to the hut, prepared food and gave the child alcohol.



Jitendra eventually fell asleep, according to investigators.

Police allege the suspect then used a knife to kill him before removing organs from the body.

Officers said Basudev told them he removed the child’s kidneys, lungs and eyes and placed them in a plastic bucket.

He allegedly wrapped the body, put it inside a sack and concealed it in a pit.

Police further claim the suspect buried the knife, a shovel and the bucket near a bamboo grove in an attempt to destroy evidence.



Following a search, investigators said they recovered the child’s body, the alleged murder weapon, the shovel, the bucket and the suspect’s mobile phone.

Police believe the suspect had been searching social media for ways to make money quickly and had become fixated on the idea of selling human organs.

Senior Superintendent Lal Umed Singh: “Preliminary investigations reveal that the accused had been searching for ways to earn quick money on social media.

“During [this time] the idea occurred to him to harvest and sell human organs from children.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The investigation is ongoing.



Authorities have not announced any evidence that the organs were successfully sold, and the allegations against the accused remain subject to legal proceedings.

News.title: Eerie handwritten ‘911’ note with ‘sad faces’ found pinned to front door by postman before cops make horror discovery
News.content:
GRUESOME FIND Eerie handwritten ‘911’ note with ‘sad faces’ found pinned to front door by postman before cops make horror discovery







Next

A POSTMAN made a grim discovery after noticing a creepy “911” note plastered to the entrance of a ramshackle home.

USPS worker Dom Clements was working his normal route in New Jersey on Friday when he spotted the eerie message taped to the front door.



The chilling sign read, “9-1-1 Inside,” above two sad cartoon faces with ominous X’s drawn over their eyes.

The eagle-eyed postie immediately dialled emergency services, prompting police officers to rush to the crumbling property in Mount Holly.



Once inside, cops uncovered a bloody scene and located the bodies of three “elderly” individuals, officials said.

Clements told The New York Post: “I thought it was weird, because the only person that would have been able to see that sign would have been me, ‘cause I’m the only one that goes to that house every day.

“And it’s just like, nobody else can, you can’t see that sign from the outside.”

The mailman also noticed the letterbox taped up with clear wrapping tape – matching the strips used to fix the sign to the door.

Clements added: “The only person who goes up to the door is the mail carrier. It’s weird. The whole situation was weird. Definitely don’t want it to happen again.

“That sign is so bizarre. It just felt weird. I was like, ooh, that doesn’t…That’s not like that happens every day, you know?



“It’s just, this is the first time I’ve ever, ever seen something like that.”

The identities of the three victims and their causes of death have not yet been released pending post-mortem examinations, Burlington County prosecutors confirmed.

But neighbours on Winding Way said a reclusive family of brothers and sisters lived at the decaying home, which had peeling paint and rotted window frames.



A neighbour, who wished to remain anonymous, said: “I mean, we’ve been here 50 some years. They were here before us, but they pretty much stayed by themselves.

“I do know that one sister was a crossing guard for years. My kids knew her and everything like that. And so she worked parades and other things as a crossing guard here in town.

“The one brother, he was like clockwork. He would always walk down to 7-Eleven around 2.30, 3 and walk on back.

“I think he would get lottery tickets and something to drink. But other than that, they would barely leave their house.”

The local resident said she heard no signs of violence ahead of the horror discovery – but did notice something unusual earlier in the week.



She said: “Tuesday is our trash day. And I saw someone coming out of the house.

“All the years I’ve been here, I’ve never seen anybody come in, go out of the house [except for the man who walks to 7-Eleven each day].

“But it was trash day. He had a bag in his hands, took it down to the curb, dropped it next to another container. It was just a little bag. He put it down and walked away.”

Police chief Clifford Spencer said: “I want to reassure our residents that, based on the preliminary investigation, there is no ongoing threat to public safety.

“The Mount Holly Police Department is working closely with and fully cooperating with the Burlington County Prosecutor’s Office as this investigation continues.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I understand that an incident of this nature is deeply concerning to our community. As your Chief of Police, I want to assure you that the safety and security of our residents remain my highest priority.

“My thoughts and prayers are with the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives in this tragic incident.”

News.title: Mystery as woman’s body found stuffed in suitcase with feet tied on road in Athens just mile from where Brit was killed
News.content:
Next

A WOMAN has been found dead stuffed inside a suitcase in Athens – in a chilling echo of a female Brit volunteer’s death earlier this year.

The victim was found on a road in the Greek capital with her feet tied up – about one mile from where tragic Elisabeth Jane Ross, 38, was also discovered inside a bag in July.



On Sunday, local cops were alerted to a suitcase left on a road by a passerby who noticed a strong smell around it in Agios Panteleimonas.

Cops rushed to the scene and found a woman of African descent, believed to be between 17 and 25, inside the luggage bag, reports say.



She was wearing shorts, a sports bra and a blouse, according to local media.

Her body was in a state of advanced decomposition but showed no obvious injuries, authorities said.

The unidentified woman’s cause of death is now being investigated.

The grim ordeal has drawn comparison to the death of Elisabeth earlier this year.



Sunday’s discovery was just one mile from where Elisabeth was similarly found inside a suitcase at an abandoned building in Kypseli on July 18.

Afghan boxer Sharif Ahmadzai is being held in a Greek prison in connection with the Brit aid worker’s death.

The Brit, from Edinburgh, had initially been staying with Greek friends in the Keratsini district, having arrived in Athens on June 26.



She moved to Rethymnou Street in the centre of the capital on July 2, police have confirmed, where she was volunteering with a Christian-based NGO, working with refugees.

Her body was discovered in an abandoned building two weeks later.

Ahmadzai, 26, has been accused of manslaughter, robbery and illegal gun possession.



He has not entered a plea while authorities await toxicological test results.

Ahmadzai’s US-born wife Alaina Hall allegedly reported her husband to cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.

She told cops that she had met Elisabeth through volunteer work in Athens and had last seen her on July 12, after a Bible study meeting, according to Greek news outlet Protothema.

Days later, she heard reports of a body being found stuffed in a suitcase in an abandoned building in Athens.

Later that night, Alaina recalled waking up with a “terrible” feeling.



In the morning she then texted Elisabeth and got two replies which made her suspicious.

Alaina said: “These messages were not in Lisa’s style, both in terms of her level of English and the use of emojis that she never used.”

When she tried calling Elisabeth she didn’t get a reply.

Alaina also told police she had grown suspicious of her husband after she woke to find him missing on the evening of July 15.

When she checked his shared location, she saw he was in Elisabeth’s flat.



Having later confronted him, he told her he had been watching a football match but had gone to Elisabeth’s apartment to use the toilet.

She told police: “I don’t know what to tell you, but all of the above made me feel strange.

“Especially combining the dates, the messages and my husband’s behaviour, I have various thoughts that make me feel uncomfortable.”

Investigating officers also found CCTV footage which allegedly shows him leaving Elizabeth’s apartment with a suitcase and dropping it where her remains were discovered on July 16.

News outlet Protothema reported that Ahmadzai had told police he did not kill Elisabeth, saying he found her dead before panicking.



In his testimony he reportedly said: “I never did harm to anyone. I want you to understand me and believe me. I was just in a panic.”

He is said to have claimed he had visited the house where she was staying and found her lying on the bathroom floor.

Ahmadzai said: “[She] was spitting something like water out of her mouth. I spoke to her two or three times, but she didn’t respond. I froze. My legs went numb.”

The 26-year-old then claimed he panicked and fled and then encountered an elderly man near a bus stop.

He reportedly asked the man what he should do after finding a dead body.



Ahmadzai said: “[The old man] told me that he worked with hospitals and he knows about them and what I should do is remove it from the house, or I will get into trouble.

“I sat and thought about what he told me for a few hours.”

He then said he had returned to the apartment the following day and placed Elisabeth’s body in a black suitcase, before placing it in the boot of the red Peugeot he drove.

Ahmadzai said: “I started the Peugeot, arrived near my house and parked it.

“I got out of the car, took the suitcase out of the boot and walked to an abandoned building across from the Panhellenic University.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“There I found the old man I told you about who gave me the advice. He told me to leave the suitcase with him, and he would take care of it.”

He also admitted to the cops he had taken Elisabeth’s phone and bank cards.
