News.title: 'In a rut after only three years and need more fun'
News.content:
Dear Coleen,

I feel like I’m in a relationship rut with my partner of three years. We moved in together this time last year and things have gone downhill. We used to do a lot together – dinners, drinks, the cinema, going on trips – now we come home after work, have dinner, watch telly and go to bed. Sex has become less frequent, too, and feels like it’s a special occasion.

We’re in our early-30s, but it feels like we’re an old married couple and that we’ve been together for decades instead of just three years. When we met, there was so much sexual chemistry and the relationship was fun, but now it’s dull and predictable and I don’t know how to get out of the rut.

I know things need to change for us to survive, but I find it very hard to initiate the conversation where we acknowledge that. We love each other, so there’s no doubts on that score, but I know that’s not enough.

View 2 Images The reader says: "I need more joy in my life." (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

‌



I need some things to look forward to in our future instead of this apathy and I need more joy in my life. Can you help?

Coleen says,

The only way to get any movement forward is to have that discussion. Don’t overthink it – start with the positives, then say you need to be mindful of not slipping into “not-making-an-effort mode” now you’re living together.

When you love someone and trust them, it’s easy to start to take each other for granted, but relationships at all stages take work. I’ve always found it can help to talk about when you started dating and remembering how you felt during those first heady days, and then do something about it.

Make the time for each other, plan things to do together, then intimacy and sexual chemistry should start to flourish again. If you want more romance, then initiate it – book a dinner or a night away, or send that flirty text. You don’t have to wait for him to do it – lead by example and get the ball rolling.

‌



Maybe it’s also time to talk about the future – where do you see yourselves in two years or five years and what are your hopes and dreams? Get excited about the possibilities. You don’t have to come home every night and sit in front of the telly. You can change the narrative.

Coleen’s words of wisdom

It’s important to try as many things as you can in your life. None of it is a waste of time because it all leads to finding what you truly love and who you were meant to be all along.

News.title: Blood pressure and cholesterol can be lowered by cutting out one drink a day say scientists
News.content:
Blood pressure and cholesterol can be lowered by cutting out one drink a day say scientists

Routinely drinking alcohol, even in small quantities, can increase a person's blood pressure

View Image Blood pressure is raised by having even small amounts of alcohol, a study revealed (Image: Getty)

Research suggests that even one alcoholic drink a day could raise an individual's blood pressure and cholesterol levels. The research team was surprised to find that even moderate drinking could have a notable impact, despite the most substantial increases being seen amongst heavy drinkers.

‌



‌



High blood pressure places extra strain on the heart, blood vessels, and vital organs such as the brain, kidneys, and eyes, potentially triggering serious health complications including heart attacks, strokes, and vascular dementia. While medication is available, lifestyle adjustments such as regular exercise, weight loss, and cutting back on caffeine, alcohol, and salt can also help keep blood pressure in check.

‌



The study, published in Hypertension – an American Heart Association journal, examined data from seven international studies involving more than 19,548 participants from the US, Korea, and Japan, who were monitored for a minimum of five years. The findings were based on the grams of alcohol consumed rather than the number of drinks.

‌



Researchers identified a clear link between the number of alcoholic drinks consumed daily and a rise in systolic blood pressure, which measures the force of the heart pumping blood around the body. Strikingly, this connection was apparent even amongst those who had just one drink per day, compared with those who abstained from alcohol altogether.

The study also recorded a rise in diastolic blood pressure - which measures the resistance to blood flow within vessels during the periods between heartbeats - in men, though not in women.

Lead researcher Professor Marco Vinceti from the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia, and an adjunct professor at Boston University's School of Public Health, said: "We found no beneficial effects in adults who drank a low level of alcohol compared to those who did not drink alcohol."

‌



He went on to express his mild surprise, noting, "We were somewhat surprised to see that consuming an already-low level of alcohol was also linked to higher blood pressure changes over time compared to no consumption – although far less than the blood pressure increase seen in heavy drinkers."

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



Professor Vinceti clarified that while alcohol isn't the sole factor raising blood pressure, the evidence strongly highlights its considerable role. He therefore recommends: "Limiting alcohol intake is advised, and avoiding it is even better."

Paul Whelton from Tulane University's school of public health and tropical medicine, and president of the World Hypertension League, weighing in on the research, disclosed: "We found participants with higher starting blood pressure readings, had a stronger link between alcohol intake and blood pressure changes over time."

‌



He added, "This suggests that people with a trend towards increased – although still not 'high' – blood pressure may benefit the most from low to no alcohol consumption."

According to nhs.uk, for the average adult, high blood pressure is typically considered starting from 140/90mmHg. The study revealed a rise in systolic blood pressure – the top number – of 1.25 millimetres of mercury (mm Hg) for those consuming an average of 12 grams of alcohol daily.

‌



Night-time habit could be early warning for stroke or heart failure READ MORE :

For those drinking 48 grams of alcohol each day, an average increase in blood pressure of 4.9 mm Hg was observed. Furthermore, men consuming 48 grams of alcohol daily experienced an average rise in their diastolic (bottom number) blood pressure of 3.1 mm Hg.

Regina Giblin, senior cardiac nurse at the British Heart Foundation, commented on the results: "This large analysis shows that even a low alcohol intake is associated with an increase in blood pressure over time."

‌



She noted, "However, this analysis can only show an association – it can't prove cause and effect – so further research is needed."

Giblin also emphasised, "If you do drink alcohol, it's important to always keep within the guidelines of up to 14 units of alcohol each week.

‌



"Regularly drinking more than this can be harmful, leading to health problems including high blood pressure. You should also try to have several alcohol-free days each week.

"However, alcohol isn't the only factor that can affect blood pressure and increase your risk of heart and circulatory diseases.

Article continues below

"Adopting a healthy lifestyle – including eating well-balanced meals, exercising regularly, stopping smoking, keeping your cholesterol at a healthy level, and controlling your weight – can all help to reduce your risk of heart attacks and strokes."

News.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued by fishermen nine hours after going overboard in the Pacific Ocean
News.content:
Cruise ship pianist rescued by fishermen nine hours after going overboard in the Pacific Ocean

Two fishermen came across the Royal Caribbean pianist nine who fell overboard from the 14-deck Ovation of the Seas ship and had survived in the sea for around nine hours

View Image The pianist went overboard the Royal Caribbean Ovation of The Seas (Image: Getty Images)

A cruise ship pianist survived nine hours treading water in the sea until he was rescued by chance after being spotted by two fishermen.

‌



‌



The Royal Caribbean employee is understood to have fallen from the 14-deck Ovation of the Seas ship and was found around 20 miles off the coast of California in the Pacific Ocean.

‌



Two Newport Beach fishermen reportedly saw the unnamed man treading water, with the cruise ship having docked in Los Angeles on Friday morning around 7am with a missing crew member.

‌



Fishermen Sean Norton and Grant Garrett have told of their surprise at seeing the man as they returned to Newport Beach having been fishing for marlin near Catalina Island.

UK weather maps show just two areas above 0C in England after Polar Vortex warning READ MORE :

Newport Beach lifeguards believe that the man probably went overboard at around 2.30am and was found by the fishermen at about midday.

“I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,'” Mr Garrett told CBS News.

‌



Mr Norton added: “Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up. He was in total shock. The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die.'”

The US coastguard was called and the man was taken to hospital in a stable condition. “It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean,” Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda reportedly said.

‌



How the man came to be in the sea in the first place is unclear at the moment and Mr Norton believes that he was only able to survive due to the unusually warm weather at the moment. A super El Niño has been affecting global temperature this year and the fisherman believes this was a factor.

"You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water's 76 degrees. A different year — no way he makes it,” he said.

Article continues below

A spokesperson for Royal Caribbean Group reportedly said following the incident: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”

The Mirror has contacted Royal Caribbean for comment.

News.title: Pharmacist warns one drink makes sore throats 'worse' and 'last longer'
News.content:
Pharmacist warns one drink makes sore throats 'worse' and 'last longer'

People should avoid making this common mistake with their sore throats

View 2 Images Sore throats are common from winter illnesses, like a cold or flu (Image: Halfpoint Images via Getty Images)

A pharmacist has said there are several things that can speed up recovery from a sore throat. However, she also warned that one common mistake could make the pain and irritation "last longer" and delay recovery further.

‌



‌



Sore throats are a common symptom of many winter illnesses, such as colds and the flu. The irritating feeling can be impossible to ignore at times - and an expert claims that some of the most "overlooked" remedies could be more helpful than people assume.

‌



Anum Ahmed (@Pharmacist.anum on TikTok) said that people can avoid the temptation to buy many over-the-counter medications when sickness strikes. Instead, some simple at-home solutions may help speed up recovery.

‌



She said: "[Standard] paracetamol can be a really effective painkiller when it comes to relieving the pain from a sore throat. You could also consider something like ibuprofen, if ibuprofen is suitable for you, because it is an anti-inflammatory, which can also help to soothe that sore throat pain."

For localised relief, many people would typically reach for a pack of medicated lozenges. Anum claims that some of these contain a form of local anaesthetic, as well as others with "anti-inflammatory ingredients".

‌



The medical expert said: "Now, with these, it's important to remember that the impact can be quite small, so don't expect a miracle. Speak with your pharmacist, and they can let you know which ones are available and which ones are suitable for you."

Something that people may neglect when they're feeling under the weather is proper hydration. Anum claims this is "key" to soothing a sore throat, but she says people often grab the wrong types of drinks for it.

‌



Ensure our latest health headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings

View 2 Images Boiling hot drinks could make your throat feel worse (Image: ljubaphoto via Getty Images)

‌



She said: "Most people will reach for warm drinks when they have a sore throat, which can be really helpful, especially with a little bit of honey. It can be really soothing for your sore throat.

"Did you know that cold drinks and cold foods such as ice lollies can provide a numbing effect to your sore throat, which can also help to relieve the pain? So don't be sleeping on cold drinks as well."

‌



As for the one drink the health specialist says can make a sore throat 'last longer' and potentially get 'worse', Anum warns: "You want to avoid boiling hot drinks straight out of the kettle. Boiling hot drinks can actually irritate your throat more and make the pain worse."

Article continues below

According to health experts, boiling hot drinks can make a sore throat worse by causing thermal irritation and mild burns to the already sensitive, inflamed lining of your throat. While comfortably warm liquids like tea or broth are excellent for soothing irritation and loosening mucus, scalding liquids increase pain, inflammation, and swelling.

According to the NHS website, a sore throat normally gets better on its own "within a week" but heals faster with proven treatments and remedies. Anum claims: "If you are concerned you're getting severe symptoms, and they're not improving. Please always speak with your pharmacist or your GP."

News.title: Electric vehicles sales target 'set to be cut' in blow for climate campaigners
News.content:
Electric vehicles sales target 'set to be cut' in blow for climate campaigners

Under existing plans around 80% of new cars sold by 2030 must be electric - but this could be slashed by 20% under proposals reportedly being discussed by ministers

View 2 Images Under existing plans around 80% of new cars sold by 2030 must be electric (Image: Getty Images)

Cuts to the government’s electric vehicle targets will reportedly be announced in a move opposed by climate campaigners.

‌



‌



Under existing plans around 80% of new cars sold by 2030 must be electric - but this could be slashed by 20% under proposals being discussed by ministers. The 2035 zero-emissions target for 100% of car and vans sales is not expected to change.

‌



Andy Burnham’s deputy, Louise Haigh, will finalise the plan at a meeting in Downing Street on Wednesday, according to the Guardian.

‌



The Prime Minister recused himself from decisions on electric car sales due to his wife Marie-France van Heel’s ties with the industry through her work.

A government spokesperson told The Mirror: “The Government is united in its commitment to the ZEV Mandate, and no decisions have been taken.

"We are committed to the phase out of all new cars relying solely on petrol and diesel engines by 2030, and to 100% of new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, and our legally binding net zero targets.

‌



"Our consultation on the mandate will not change this, and will ensure we are taking a pragmatic and balanced approach to the ZEV transition.”

Andy Burnham to unveil GP boost to support up to 300,000 vulnerable patients this winter including home visits READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham’s deputy, Louise Haigh, will finalise the plan at a meeting in Downing Street on Wednesday (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

‌



It comes after the government launched a review of the EV mandate in the summer.

They said at the time: “In the context of challenging and complex global economic conditions, including supply chain disruption and tariff and trade uncertainty, the UK is reviewing targets to ensure they remain pro-business and grounded in the real world.”

‌



Carmakers have also argued higher inflation in recent years has pushed the interim 2030 target for EV sales out of reach.

But Green Party MP Sian Berry said: “Putting the brakes on EV targets would be yet another indication that corporations are in the driving seat when it comes to climate policy. Such a move would seriously weaken the government’s climate commitments, but also put investment in charging infrastructure and associated jobs at risk.

‌



“The switch to EVs has the potential to create greater emissions savings than any other energy transition policy, while providing drivers with vehicles that can be significantly cheaper to run."

Paul McNamee, the director of the Labour Climate and Environment Forum, also told the Guardian: “Significant weakening of the ZEV mandate from the current 80% targets will be seen as a rowing back on climate leadership.

‌



“If the government does this, it must provide assurance that the mandate will not be weakened again in the coming years, the 2035 target for EVs remains in place, and it delivers a robust industrial strategy to build a strong EV manufacturing base in the UK that will protect jobs in the long term.”

Health minister Karin Smyth insisted no decision had been made during a series of interviews on Monday.

‌



Appearing on BBC Breakfast, the minister was asked whether climate change was no longer a big priority. She replied: “No, we are committed to our emissions targets and climate change is important to this government, obviously.

“The reports you are talking about this morning - the government hasn’t made any decisions.”

‌



Asked whether it would be embarrassing for Andy Burnham to head to the Cop climate change summit in Antalya, Turkey, later this week after watering down EV targets at home, she added: “Well as I said no particular decision has been made on those targets.

“When he goes to Cop this country is doing great work in terms of our transition, looking at renewables, that’s a key part of growth.

Article continues below

“I’m sure the Prime Minister will have a good story to tell working with our partners across the world in Cop.”

News.title: M40 closed: Drivers face huge 90 min delays after crash
News.content:
M40 closed: Drivers face huge 90 min delays after crash

National Highways has warned drivers that the M40 is closed southbound between Junction 1a (M25) and J1 (Denham) with tailbacks of four miles due a "police-led incident"

View 2 Images Motorists are facing long delays on the M40

Drivers are facing delays of 90 minutes on a major motorway after a crash involving four vehicles early this morning.

‌



‌



National Highways warned drivers that the M40 was closed southbound between Junction 1a (M25) and J1 (Denham) with tailbacks of four miles - and it has since reopened but severe congestion remains.

‌



Four vehicles were involved in a crash stated Thames Valley Police which led to "minor injury" after they received reports of the incident at 5.45am.

‌



A spokesperson for Thames Valley Police told The Mirror: "This was a minor injury collision involving four vehicles. The road has just re-opened and the backlog is clearing."

View 2 Images There are four miles of congestion on the motorway (Image: Motorwaycameras)

UK weather maps show just two areas above 0C in England after Polar Vortex warning READ MORE :

"#M40 southbound near #GerrardsCross within J1A Road remains closed due to a @ThamesVP incident," earlier stated National Highways. "Traffic caught within the closure is being released from rear of the incident. Delays building, currently 90 mins, 4 miles of congestion."

‌



It also stated: "The M40 is closed southbound between Junction 1a (M25) and J1 (Denham) due to an ongoing Thames Valley police led incident that was reported at 05:45. Traffic Officers are on scene to assist with strategic closures on the approach.

Images from the motorway show long queues amid foggy conditions although it is not known if that had anything to do with the collision.

‌



A yellow warning for fog is in place from the Met Office which until 11am today and covers most of England and parts of eastern Wales.

The national weather agency states: " Fog leading to difficult travel conditions and possible delays."

‌



And it continues: "Fog patches will form readily again during Sunday evening and overnight becoming extensive by Monday morning. Some dense patches of fog are expected with visibility down to around 50 metres or less in some places. Fog thinning slowly later on Monday morning."

Last night National Highways said the M4 was blocked in west London, near Heathrow Airport, after a two vehicle crash. It caused three miles of congestion before clearing in the early hours of Monday morning.

‌



The agency said at 11:30pm on Sunday (November 8): "M4 westbound in Greater London between J3 Harrow and J4 Heathrow Airport. Road is blocked due a collision between two cars. Police are on scene and vehicle recovery crews are en route. Current delays of 30 minutes on approach to the incident, with three miles of congestion.”

Heathrow Airport then took to social media to warn passengers to allow extra time to get to the terminal. A spokesperson said: “Overnight fog has affected visibility on roads around Heathrow and conditions may continue into this morning (Monday November 9).

Article continues below

“If you're travelling to the airport, please allow extra time for your journey. We advise passengers to check with their airline before leaving home and to drive with care.”

News.title: Electricals retailer Comet makes its comeback, 14 years after chain's collapse
News.content:
Electricals retailer Comet makes its comeback, 14 years after chain's collapse

EXCLUSIVE: Gadget and electricals firm Comet went to the wall in 2012 but has been revived with a new marketplace website that has gone live

View 3 Images Electricals giant Comet has 236 branches when it collapsed in 2012 (Image: PA)

Comet will make its comeback today - 14 years after the electrical chain’s collapse.

‌



‌



The retailer has been revived as an online only business - complete with its original branding - with the hope of taking on the might of Amazon and others. More than a million electrical products will be available from the start, ranging from TVs and mobile phones, to washing machines and kettles.

‌



The launch comes after online marketplace OnBuy.com bought the Comet brand in May last year. Onbuy had originally said the Comet website would go live by last Christmas, but that was delayed.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Comet is making a comeback - but only online (Image: PA)

Comet was founded in Hull in 1933 and started out selling batteries and radios, and grew to become a high street giant. But in what was one of the biggest high street casualties of recent years, the 236-store chain went to the wall in 2012, with 7,000 job losses, after racking up heavy losses.

‌



The relaunched Comet won’t sell its own stock but instead operate as an online shop window where big name retailers and electricals goods makers can advertise and sell their products.

A confident Cas Paton, founder of OnBuy, said: “We have got Comet so well placed for the launch that we know that the site is going to be a success.

‌



“There’s never been an electronics and gadgets marketplace in the UK. There has been in the US and Europe. We think there is a big gap in the market for consumers to compare different retailers and different brands.”

View 3 Images New Comet owner Cas Paton says: "It’s a resurgence of something that is quite dear to people"

‌



He claimed Comet’s website would display far more products than retailer rivals, with over one million products and accessories.

Mr Paton, who started his first business aged 21 with £80 after leaving the Royal Navy, insists the strength of the Comet brand can prove a winner.

‌



“We’ve done some testing and paid a lot of money for the brand,” he said. “We think it’s such a good, positive story that something is actually coming back, rather than collapsing. It’s a resurgence of something that is quite dear to people, and positive nostalgia.”

Remembering how he used to go into Comet stores, he said: “There were only two places to buy your gadgets and electricals, Dixons and Comet. People felt deary about Comet but it lost its way.”

Article continues below

While there won’t be a return of Comet stores, he said they were looking at tying up with a retailer to offer a click-and-collect option for customers.

News.title: Woman says Al Fayed's brother drugged and sexually abused her at Highland estate
News.content:
A woman has told BBC Scotland how she was trafficked to the Highlands, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner by Salah Fayed, the brother of former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed.

Jill, whose name has been changed for legal reasons, said she was a young Harrods employee when she was recruited to what she believed was an executive training scheme in the 1990s.

Speaking for the first time about the abuse that took place in Scotland, Jill said she was flown on the Fayed family's private jet to Balnagown, their estate in Easter Ross, where she was repeatedly assaulted.

She is one of hundreds of women who have alleged abuse by the Fayed brothers.

Since Mohamed Al Fayed's death in 2023, hundreds of women and girls have alleged they were sexually abused by him.

His brother Salah, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2010, has also been accused of abuse by numerous women.

News.title: Thick fog disrupts morning travel as yellow weather warnings in effect
News.content:
Yellow weather warnings for dense fog remain in effect across parts of the UK as low visibility disrupts travel.

A Met Office warning is in place across much of England and eastern Wales and runs until 11:00 GMT on Monday. An additional fog warning has been issued for Northern Ireland running until 10:00 GMT.

The larger warning covers an area of England and Wales stretching from Canterbury to Cardiff, Hull to St Asaph and Southampton to York, and includes London, Birmingham and parts of Greater Manchester.

The Met Office has issued a further warning for fog from Monday evening into Tuesday morning.

News.title: Scientists predict 2026 hottest year on record as climate talks begin
News.content:
The world is on course for its hottest year on record as the planet is hit with warming from climate change and El NiÃ±o, scientists have told BBC News.

The warning comes as world leaders and negotiators gather in Turkey on Monday for the opening of COP31, the latest UN climate summit.

Berkeley Earth, the independent US research group behind the forecast, said that even with two months of the year left it is 95% confident that 2026 will surpass the previous record set in 2024.

The impact of rising heat has been felt acutely in recent months by countries attending COP, with extensive wildfires across Europe and the sudden glacier collapse in Nepal which killed more than 1,000 people.

"We have had a run of record warm years," said Dr Robert Rohde, of Berkeley Earth. "That is what we expect as global warming progressesâ¦ glaciers collapsing, record-breaking heatwaves and droughts."

On Friday, the EU's Copernicus climate service, external confirmed that October was the hottest on record.

But Rohde warned this was just the start. "There is potential for much larger and much more dramatic changes down the line," he said.

The main driver of rising global temperatures has been the increasing concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, largely caused by burning fossil fuels.

The UN's World Meteorological Organization (WMO) published its own report on Monday, external, and although more cautious than Berkeley, it has forecast that 2026 will be among the four warmest years on record.

It said that 2027 will provide no let-up, as an unusually powerful El NiÃ±o will continue into next year, pushing temperatures higher.

WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said it "gives new meaning to the phrase off the charts".

News.title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
News.content:
The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.

Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief".

New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.

But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.

The government has been consulting on reducing its 80% rule and a significant reduction is now expected.

Downing Street has insisted no decision has been made.

A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.

If ministers do decide on a steeper watering-down of the rules, it will arguably be interpreted by some - alongside the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea - as the government prioritising economic considerations over environmental ones.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has recused himself from this issue due to his wife's links to an electric vehicle company.

The key meetings on the subject will instead be chaired by Cabinet Office minister Louise Haigh.

Sustainability groups say any weakening of the 2030 target will threaten the UK's long-term electrification and climate goals.

It could undermine the UK's claim to be providing leadership on climate just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.

Energy UK, the trade association for the energy industry, has also opposed the move.

Last month, it said, external reducing targets could damage "the investment certainty needed to deliver the infrastructure, innovation and services required for the transition to zero-emission transport".

Asked if climate change was no longer a big priority, Health Minister Karin Smyth said the government was committed to its emissions targets.

"This country is doing great work in terms of our transition and looking at renewables â that's a key part of growth in different parts of the country," she told BBC Breakfast.

She added that the prime minister would have "a good story to tell" when meeting other leaders at COP31.

A government spokesperson said: "We are committed to the phase out of all new cars relying solely on petrol and diesel engines by 2030, and to 100% of new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, and our legally binding net zero targets."

News.title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says
News.content:
Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said.

The inquiry's first report, published this summer, concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children".

The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "backing" the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back".

Inquiry co-chair and former education secretary Baroness Morris said the next phase of the inquiry's work will consider "what needs to be done".

"This isn't just the responsibility of schools but calls for action from across society," she said.

The Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes, external was commissioned by the multi-academy trust Star Academies, and is supported by the Department for Education.

It spoke to thousands of young people and their parents, as well as hundreds of teachers.

Education data about white working class pupils was also analysed as part of the year-long review, looking at the 1.25 million young people in England who are white British and in receipt of free school meals.

News.title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?
News.content:
I'm "words of affirmation", and so is my husband. This is supposedly our shared love language.

But, while we do like receiving compliments, they make us both feel a bit awkward.

Despite this, our result was confidently defined when we took the original Love Languages Quiz online, a personality test published by US pastor Gary Chapman who first came up with the five types of expressing and receiving love in 1992.

I'm sceptical. Does the theory really know more about us than our own lived experience of a 10-year marriage?

The five love languages are: Quality Time, Acts of Service, Words of Affirmation, Receiving Gifts, and Physical Touch - and they feel more ubiquitous than ever.

Contestants on dating shows ask each other their love languages; "My love language isâ¦" is a common prompt on dating apps.

News.title: The Silicon Valley superstar engulfed by personal scandal
News.content:
Jensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures.

He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies.

As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China.

The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US.

He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.

He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine - a biography on Huang, tells the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

Huang has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang.

Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.

"I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".

News.title: Doing these things now will help you save money at Christmas
News.content:
How soon is too soon when it comes to thinking about Christmas and your finances?

The answer, of course, is that it is never too soon. Save early and the cost becomes more manageable.

The squeeze is harder for some than others, with charity Barnardo's warning that some parents will skip meals so their kids get a Christmas dinner with the trimmings.

But, debt advice charity StepChange is offering tips to everyone, to avoid Christmas spending leading to a financially painful new year.

News.title: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island
News.content:
Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.

The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram alongside a highlights reel of her on the programme that it was "time to throw myself into something new".

"While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I'll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever," the TV and radio presenter said.

Jama's announcement comes hot on the heels of an appearance as a contestant on Celebrity Traitors that won her praise and speculation in the Times, external that she could "get Â£1m per deal" thanks to her success.

Thanking fans and the production team on Love Island, she said she had an "unforgettable time" on the programme.

"I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I've loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show.

But she added: "I've always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then."

Jama landed her biggest presenting role to date as the host of the reality TV show in 2023, taking over from Laura Whitmore.

The programme couples contestants together who then complete a range of tasks and keep swapping in the hope of meeting the love of their life.

An ITV spokesperson said: "Maya has been a fantastic and much loved host on Love Island - we thank her for everything she has brought to the show over the last three years and wish her every continued success."

Love Island is one of the most popular reality TV shows in the UK but the series has polarised viewers, with some arguing the show is misogynistic and raising concerns about the welfare of contestants.

News.title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse
News.content:
Dormouse numbers may be recovering in England and Wales after years of decline, offering a rare piece of good news for one of our best-loved mammals.

The animal has disappeared from much of the countryside with conservationists warning of a long-term collapse in its population.

However, new data suggests dormouse numbers increased between 2020-2025, a period that coincided with warmer springs and summers.

Scientists believe these conditions may help dormice survive, by boosting food supplies and reducing the time they spend asleep.

That gives the animals more opportunity to breed and build up fat reserves ahead of winter.

News.title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row
News.content:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has rejected accusations of politicising Remembrance Sunday after being criticised for linking the event to the UK rejoining the European Union's Erasmus scheme.

Her department announced on Saturday night that "as we mark Remembrance Sunday, Erasmus+ will give a new generation the chance to build connections across Europe".

That sparked a backlash from the Conservatives, who said "veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme" and accused her of making an "EU membership pitch".

Nandy said she was "horrified" by the Tory response and insisted that the expanded EU scheme for study and work would help young Britons recognise wartime sacrifice.

The UK is rejoining the scheme in January, six years after leaving it as part of the Brexit deal.

On Saturday, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport drew comparisons between that scheme and events on Sunday to commemorate veterans who had died in conflict.

Referring to the scheme, Nandy said in her department's press release: "As we remember the immense courage of those who served our country, we honour them by building the best opportunities for the next generation through closeness and collaboration with our allies."

Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake described her comments as "tone deaf and frankly shameful" and called on Nandy to apologise.

He said the bonds that veterans forged "run far deeper" than Erasmus.

"It is not a day for a Labour minister to try to make an EU membership pitch," he added.

Reform leader Nigel Farage told the BBC: "For Lisa Nandy to use Remembrance Sunday to announce this and say it's all about peace, it's all about the war - I find that very, very poor taste."

Peter Sharples, chief executive of the Veterans Institute, told the Telegraph that people should "just honour the fallen" on Remembrance Sunday rather than discussing "party political matters".

Asked about the criticism on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, Nandy stood by her initial remarks.

"It was Winston Churchill after the Second World War who talked about extending the hand of friendship across Europe and making sure that we honoured the legacy of that generation," she said.

She said that after Brexit "we closed off opportunities for young people from this country to understand not just the impact that generation made here in the UK, but the way in which they went off and fought for the freedom of people across Europe".

Asked to respond to accusations she had chosen Remembrance Sunday to "promote part of the new deal the government has done with the EU", Nandy said she was "not choosing today or any day actually to promote a deal with the EU".

Pressed about linking the day to what the government believes are the cultural benefits of the scheme, Nandy said: "There was a time where that wouldn't have even raised an eyebrow as somehow political, it was just common sense - and it is common sense."

News.title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
News.content:
Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.

Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".

The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.

In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.

Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."

It came after the Sunday Times reported, external that the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.

The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.

Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".

Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.

The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.

A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".

"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.

An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".

"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.

News.title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built
News.content:
An off-grid hut that produces its own heating and electricity can continue to be the home of the man who built it, a council has decided.

Geoffrey Finnimore, a self-employed architectural designer, erected the structure in Glandwr, near Crymych, in 2020, but never told authorities or asked for permission.

Pembrokeshire council told him he must apply for retrospective permission for the home that is self-sufficient, and also collects rain water.

However, the local authority found that because it has now been occupied as a home for more than four years, it is immune from prosecution action.

"Without my home, which I created to solve my own problems without state assistance, having to pay for other accommodation would be catastrophic for my finances and well-being," Finnimore said.

The council asked him to apply for a lawful development certificate, external for the property.

This is a formal legal document confirming the development is lawful.

But as he had lived there for more than four years, it meant he could not be prosecuted, so his application was accepted, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.

News.title: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
News.content:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.

On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.

That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".

Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.

And for the first time, the leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.

News.title: Briton among six killed in 'far-right' shooting in Krakow
News.content:
A gunman believed to have been inspired by far-right ideology has killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in an attack in the busy centre of Poland's second largest city.

Police said the attacker drove on to Main Market Square in Krakow, a popular tourist attraction, on Saturday afternoon and fired randomly at people.

Four women and two men were killed. Three were Polish, one was British and two have not been identified.

Among the 16 injured are five foreign nationals from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain.

Another three bodies were found when counter-terrorism police searched the suspect's home around 125 miles (200km) away, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said.

A massive armed police presence was deployed across Krakow on Saturday evening, as security measures were ramped up in the capital Warsaw and elsewhere.

A period of mourning has been declared in Krakow until 11 November.

Two police officers are also among those injured, one critically.

The suspect, who was equipped with military-style weapons and attire, is a 24-year-old Polish man - described by a minister as "ultra-nationalist".

Police shot and arrested him and he remains in hospital having undergone surgery.

Tusk said there were "strong indications" the two women and one man found dead at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec ÅwiÄtokrzyski were his immediate family members.

He said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism... that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'm shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in KrakÃ³w today."

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added.

The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in the historic centre of Krakow, an ornate square which has long been a draw for tourists.

Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out.

The glass front of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes.

Images from the scene show overturned tables and scattered belongings left behind as people ran for their lives.

Armed police officers pursued the attacker's car until it crashed, at which point they engaged him in a firefight.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify captured the moment a police officer confronted the suspect as he lay on the ground.

The officer, who is visibly injured, can then be seen falling to the ground.

News.title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10
News.content:
Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught.

The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.

The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.

Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.

He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.

These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell said: "The early years of secondary school should be a time when children are excited to go to school and engage in the specialist and much broader teaching on offer, and where they find their passion and develop a love of learning."

She added that ringfencing Key Stage 3 studies would allow for "more time to develop deeper understanding, as well as a richer experience that will engage more young people in their passions".

The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.

It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9, from 13% to 15%.

The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.

"The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said. "I'm putting a stop to that."

A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.

However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.

Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.

She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".

News.title: Christmas pudding isn’t for everyone. Here are three festive alternatives
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The festive season is fast approaching, and with it the need to start planning a Christmas feast for the whole family.

While crisp potatoes and gravy-filled Yorkshires are bound to please all, the classic Christmas pudding isn’t for everyone.

So, if you’re looking for something different to serve after your festive roast, here are three showstopping dessert alternatives.

Lucy Brazier’s chestnut and chocolate cake

“This is one of my family’s favourite chocolate ‘pudding’ cakes, and I make it at least once every Christmas (and not infrequently for birthdays and other celebrations too),” says River Cottage’s Lucy Brazier.

“It’s delectably tender, fudgy and chocolatey – and not too sweet or over-rich. You can serve it warm from the oven, with a dollop of whipped cream or ice cream, but it’s also good made a day or two ahead and served cold or at room temperature.”

open image in gallery Lucy Brazier’s chestnut and chocolate cake ( Charlotte Bland/Press Association )

Ingredients (Serves 10–12):

250g peeled cooked chestnuts (vacuum-packed or tinned are fine)

250ml milk

250g dark chocolate (at least 70% cocoa solids), broken up

250g unsalted butter, roughly cut up

4 medium eggs, separated

100g caster sugar

You will also need:

A 25cm springform cake tin

Method:

1. Preheat the oven to 170°C/Fan 150°C/Gas 3, and grease and line your 25cm springform cake tin.

2. Put the chestnuts and milk into a pan and heat until just boiling. Take off the heat and mash well with a potato masher – you are aiming for a creamy purée, with just a few crumbly bits of chestnut. Set aside.

3. Put the chocolate and butter into a second pan and place over a very low heat. Keeping a close eye, to ensure that the chocolate doesn’t get too hot, melt them gently together, stirring now and then. Allow to cool a little.

4. Whisk the egg yolks and sugar together in a large bowl until blended and creamy (they don’t need to reach a ‘moussey’ stage). Stir in the warm (not hot) chocolate mixture and then the chestnut purée, to create a well-blended batter.

open image in gallery Christmas At River Cottage by Lucy Brazier and Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall ( Bloomsbury/Press Association )

5. Whisk the egg whites in a clean bowl until they hold stiff peaks. Take one spoonful of egg white and mix it into the batter to loosen it, then fold the rest in lightly, trying not to knock out too much air. Carefully transfer the mixture to the prepared tin. Bake for 25–30 minutes until the cake is just set but with a slight wobble still in the centre.

6. To serve warm, leave to cool a little then release the cake from the tin. Slice carefully – it will be very soft and moussey. Alternatively, leave the cake to go cold, when it will have set a bit firmer

Extract from Christmas at River Cottage by Lucy Brazier and Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall, published in hardback by Bloomsbury Publishing, priced £25. Photography by Charlotte Bland.

Skye McAlpine’s Christmas pavlova

“The happy muddle of shades of festive red, from the cheery Santa-bright of the berries to the rich, deep scarlet of the sour cherries in syrup, as well as the pleasing resemblance of this dish to a holiday wreath, add a good dash of ‘Christmas’, in my book, to the whole affair,” says cookbook author Skye McAlpine.

Hands-on time: 20 minutes

Hands-off time: 2 hours baking and cooling

open image in gallery Skye McAlpine's Christmas pavlova ( Skye McAlpine/Press Association )

Ingredients (Serves 6-8):

3 egg whites

⅓tsp cream of tartar

150g caster sugar

450ml double cream

250g amarena cherries

100g fresh redcurrants

40g pomegranate seeds

Method:

1. Heat the oven to 140˚C / 120˚C fan / Gas 1. Line a baking tray with baking paper. Draw a wreath shape in pencil on the baking paper (I use a plate and a mug to create the outer and inner outline for this, respectively, but you can also do it by eye).

2. In a spotlessly clean bowl, whisk the egg whites and cream of tartar until frothy, then add the sugar, 1 spoonful at a time, whisking all the while, until stiff, glossy peaks form. Spoon the soft meringue on to the template to create a wreath shape, then use the back of your spoon to create a gentle hollow channel within the walls of the meringue, where the cream and fruit will sit later. Bake in the oven for 1 hour, then switch the oven off without opening its door and leave the meringue in there to cool completely for a further hour.

open image in gallery The Christmas Companion by Skye McAlpine ( PA )

3. You can bake the meringue up to 4 days ahead of when you plan to serve it and keep it in an airtight container at room temperature.

4. To serve, gently lift the meringue ring off the baking tray, peeling away the baking paper, and place on a serving dish. Whip the cream in a mixing bowl until soft peaks form, taking care not to over-whip it. Spoon the cream into the channel you created over the meringue wreath and top with the fruit. Store in the fridge for up to 8 hours before serving.

Extract from The Christmas Companion by Skye McAlpine, published in hardback by Bloomsbury Publishing, priced £28. Photography by Skye McAlpine.

Rachel Morgan’s tiramisu

“We’ve made this a lot for parties,” notes Rachel Morgan, owner of Twelve Triangles bakery in Edinburgh. “I always think it’s a good example of how something fairly simple can be greater than the sum of its parts. If you want to go the extra mile I can absolutely vouch for making your own mascarpone, which really does take it to the next level.

“This makes enough for 4–6 people in a 20cm x 40cm deep dish, but the quantities are very easy to scale up.”

open image in gallery Rachel Morgan's tiramisu ( Laura Edwards/Press Association )

Ingredients (Serves 4-6):

350ml espresso

4tbsp panela sugar

200ml coffee liqueur

4 eggs

80g caster sugar

400g mascarpone (homemade if possible)

Salt

About 36 sponge fingers

Cocoa powder

Mascarpone (makes about 500g)

740g double cream

20g lemon juice

Method:

1. To make the mascarpone, put the cream into a saucepan that has a lid and heat it until it reaches 82–84°C, stirring occasionally so that it heats evenly. Once it has hit that temperature, take it off the heat, add the lemon juice and stir until it thickens

2. Once it has thickened up, put the lid on and let it sit for an hour. Then strain it through a muslin or clean j-cloth and leave it for about 5 hours.

3. Brew your espresso and mix in your panela and coffee liqueur, then set aside to cool in a shallow bowl.

4. Separate the eggs and whisk the yolks and caster sugar together until they are very pale, thick and creamy, then whisk in your mascarpone – make sure your mascarpone is at room temperature and has been properly beaten/softened or it will be lumpy when you add to the egg yolks. This is especially important if you have made your own mascarpone, since it will be much thicker set than the shop-bought stuff.

open image in gallery Kitchen Table: Simple Things Made Well, by Emily Cuddeford and Rachel Morgan ( HarperCollins/Press Association )

5. Whisk your egg whites with a pinch of salt to a stiff peak and fold through your egg yolk/sugar/mascarpone mix.

6. Dip the sponge fingers one by one into your now cooled coffee mix and lay them in an even layer on the bottom of your dish. Cover with a layer of the mascarpone/egg mix. Repeat with another layer, dipping the sponge fingers into the coffee, and covering with the remainder of the mascarpone/egg mix.

7. Finish with a heavy dusting of sieved cocoa powder and allow to rest in the fridge for at least 6 hours before serving.

Extract from Kitchen Table: Simple Things Made Well by Emily Cuddeford and Rachel Morgan, published in hardback by HarperCollins, priced £25. Photography by Laura Edwards.

News.title: Lorraine Kelly misses live ITV show after crash on M40
News.content:
Lorraine Kelly has issued an update to fans after she was forced to miss her Monday morning show today (9 November).

The presenter shared a video on Instagram and revealed she missed the ITV show following an accident on the M40.

She captioned the post: “I’ve actually had genuine nightmares about not being able to get to work - today it was true. Sadly an accident on the M40 shut the motorway and I was stuck for an hour and a half.

“All OK now and hopefully no injuries but live TV means you can’t be late. See you tomorrow, so sorry!”

News.title: At least 14 dead after fire rips through high-rise China apartment block
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

At least 14 people have died following a fire at a high-rise building in Taiyuan, the capital of Shanxi province in northern China, official news agency Xinhua reported on Monday.

State media said 25 people remain in hospital, nine with severe injuries, citing authorities after the blaze broke out on Sunday evening in a property located on a busy downtown main road.

Smoke billowed over the 40-storey structure as firefighters using external cranes fought flames spreading upward from a lower annex, video footage verified by Reuters showed.

The fire appears to have started around the annex's fourth floor before reaching the eighth and ninth floors, which house a hotel, according to the state broadcaster.

Smoke billowed over the 40-storey structure as firefighters poised on cranes outside fought flames that spread upward from a lower annex, video images circulated online and verified by Reuters showed ( Reuters )

The property is a mixed-use commercial and residential building containing several hotels, short-term rental apartments, smaller commercial venues and tutoring centres, the report said.

The blaze was extinguished after about two hours and rescue operations concluded by 8.30pm on Sunday night, with 38 people taken to hospital, authorities said.

An investigation into the cause of the fire in the northern manufacturing hub remains ongoing, state media added.

Russell Brand faces a “signficant” prison term when he is sentenced later today after being convicted of raping one of his fans and sexually assaulting three women.

The former comedian, now 51, spent the weekend in a cell after he was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court of raping a woman in 2009, as well as sexually assaulting female TV and radio workers between 2004 and 2009.

His victims told the court he had forced them into sexual activity, sometimes within seconds of them first meeting, using his immense fame to pursue a goal of sex with 5,000 women.

Mr Justice Bennathan will pass sentence today, after telling the shamed star to expect a “significant” jail term following the jury’s verdict last week.

In the wake of Brand’s convictions, the Metropolitan Police revealed that more allegations against the former TV and radio host are being investigated.

On Sunday, culture secretary Lisa Nandy suggested Brand’s crimes were unlikely to be an isolated incident within the entertainment industry. She told Sky News: “I would wager that this is probably happening today, and I don’t think that the industry is doing enough to tackle it.”

News.title: Moment Tommy Robinson is attacked by influencer at Kilkenny boxing event sparking a mass brawl
News.content:
A mass brawl broke out at at Kilkenny boxing event after Tommy Robinson was attacked by an influencer who launched himself from the ring.

Footage shows Mo Deen leaping over the ropes at the ‘Unhinged 300’ event and onto the commentator’s table where Robinson was sitting, causing a chaotic pile-on.

Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, the retaliates, throwing a punch back at Deen on stage, igniting violent clashes around the venue.

Irish police confirmed two arrests were made following the chaos with a man in his 30s taken to hospital after being assaulted and one teenager charged with violent disorder.

Robinson was attending on bail after being found guilty for harrassing two journalists and causing them to fear violence.

News.title: Man Utd are in relegation trouble and Carrick must be sacked
News.content:
Michael Carrick says he has been given no assurances about his future beyond this afternoon’s crucial game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford.



United are searching for only their second Premier League win of the season and first in 70 days after the club’s worst start to a campaign for 40 years piled the pressure on Carrick.



They dropped into the relegation zone last night following Nottingham Forest’s victory over Manchester City and will be bottom by the end of the weekend if they lose to Villa and Crystal Palace and Sunderland both win.



The Old Trafford hierarchy opted to give Carrick more time to try to turn their season around following a 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth and 4-1 drubbing in Como, since when United have been beaten 2-0 by Chelsea and recovered from two goals down to overcome Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.



Asked if he had been told outright he would still be in charge next week, Carrick said: “No - no. Just carry on as absolute normal.”



Pressed on when he felt his future was uncertain, the head coach added: “No, no. Whatever happens and what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game, we’ve got to prepare right.



“I’m really looking forward to playing at home on the back of the other night. The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see and we’ve got to repay that.”



Another defeat would leave the United board with a big decision to make around Carrick’s future at a time when they are under severe attack from the fanbase.



United’s game against Roma was briefly interrupted when tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch in the first half of a game notable for more furious protests against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Three people were arrested by Greater Manchester Police for throwing items on to the pitch and are understood to have been hit with automatic three-year football banning orders as a consequence.



More in-stadium demonstrations are expected today with regular match going fans encouraged not to buy alcohol or drinks inside Old Trafford and again release green and gold balloons before kick-off.



Green and gold were the club’s original colours as Newton Heath and have become a symbol of protest against the ownership.



Asked why there had been such a big drop-off from last season, Carrick added: “It’s just inconsistency, that’s within games,” he said.



“It can be a number of things, it’s never just one thing: a bit of decision-making, a bit of concentration, things going against us in certain points, sometimes we haven’t helped ourselves. So there’s no excuses for it, it is what it is. The great thing is we can do something about it.”

News.title: Energised England deliver statement win to take heat off Borthwick
News.content:
England’s players delivered on their self-created ultimatum to “do it for Steve” by annihilating an abysmal Australia. Barring an extraordinary sequence of events, Borthwick will now remain as head coach through to the World Cup.

Even if Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney’s vote of confidence in the head coach last week was delivered without caveats, he would still have been forced to play the role of reluctant Caesar if the crowd turned mutinous, as they did four years ago. That resulted in Sweeney delivering the thumbs down on Eddie Jones’s reign.

Yet this did not come to pass, as England showed plenty of fire and fury on behalf of their head coach after his control of the dressing room was questioned last week. With 14 minutes to go the crowd, who had been muted on Remembrance Sunday, broke into a rendition of Swing Low, indicating their own approval.

It was not perfect. Attack coach Lee Blackett will be hugely frustrated that they only scored seven tries from a staggering 22 entries into the Australia 22. They also took their foot off the Wallabies’ throats in the final quarter, although they did surpass their highest points total against the visitors. Probably the biggest disappointment was the injuries suffered by wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and centre Seb Atkinson, who had both enjoyed strong games until that point.

News.title: Lando Norris wins chaotic Sao Paulo Grand Prix but F1 season is fizzling out
News.content:
Lando Norris will start today’s Sao Paulo Grand Prix on pole position after a chaotic qualifying session at Interlagos yesterday. A red flag was thrown a matter of moments into qualifying, which led to a lengthy delay of around an hour and a half. When racing did resume, the conditions were treacherous but it was the 2025 world champion Norris who coped best by claiming his third straight pole at Interlagos.

“It has been a long day,” Norris said after taking pole. “It has been a great qualifying. To be on pole again here, two years in a row, different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. It is not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it is going to rain a lot more. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that is exactly what we did, so it has been a very good day.

“This was my first time driving the car in the wet, so I think I figured it out pretty quick. It is tough because you are wet, intermediates, all different tyres, and it was very windy the last couple of laps. It was certainly a good day for learning for me and good to take into tomorrow [today]. These guys [Mercedes] are also very quick. Just happy. Today [yesterday] is about getting on pole. It does not really matter how you do it, so very pleased with that.”

News.title: Chelsea bullied by Brian Brobbey and Sunderland
News.content:
Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

The hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume said.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”
