News.title: Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed
News.content:
Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

Sports.title: Forest Green owner explains why they failed to commemorate Remembrance Day as English football falls silent
Sports.content:
Next

FOREST GREEN owner Dale Vince has apologised after the club failed to mark Remembrance Day.

The National League club’s final home game before Remembrance Sunday was a 2-2 draw against Harrogate Town last weekend, but no commemoration was held.



Forest Green were beaten 2-0 by Luton Town in the FA Cup at Kenilworth Road this weekend and both teams observed a minute’s silence before kick-off.

And club chief Vince has now admitted their failure to mark Remembrance Day against Harrogate the week before was a “simple mistake”.



Fans had questioned why no special measures were in place at The New Lawn Stadium.

Vince responded on the club’s Fan Advisory Board, saying: “The lack of Remembrance at a home game is simply down to a human error/mistake on the club.

“It didn’t help that we had a sizable number of games in a small time frame (including the FA Cup replay) beforehand; albeit that isn’t an excuse, we should have got this right.

“This was a simple error/mistake.”

Vince has made headlines at Forest Green after bringing in vegan menus to the stadium, banning red meat and installing organic pitches.

He also became the first chairman to appoint a female boss at a men’s team in English football after appointing Hannah Dingley as interim boss in 2023.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And Vince raised eyebrows last month after refusing to replace Robbie Savage after he was poached by Peterborough.

The club announced their strategy for the season was “see what happens”.

Club owner Vince insisted at the time that he believes in the remaining coaching staff – made up of coaching trio Jonathan Gould, Josh Bowen and Yan Klukowski.

He told BBC Radio Gloucestershire: “We’re in a situation where we’re not in a hurry. We’re not actually having any conversations.



“We haven’t spoken to anybody about the role. We like where we are, we’re going to see how it goes — maybe for a few games, maybe for a month.

“The coaching team have been doing the heavy lifting anyway; they know the team inside out.

“I think the three of them make very balanced, rational decisions.

“We aren’t talking to anybody. I promise you we haven’t had a single conversation.

Sports.title: BBC make major change to SPOTY as two new awards are introduced for first time
Sports.content:
Next

THE BBC has made a major change to their iconic annual Sports Personality of the Year awards.

There will be two new awards at this year’s ceremony on December 13.



For the first time ever, there will be two football awards at SPOTY which will become the only sport-specific awards on the night.

Men’s Footballer of the Year and BBC World Service Women’s Footballer of the Year will be awarded this time around.



The latter has been a BBC World Service award since 2015 but will now be presented as part of the BBC Sports Personality of the Year awards for the first time.

Five of the nine awards to be presented on the night will be decided by public vote.

The two footballers of the year will both be decided by the public.

The Men’s Footballer of the Year will be decided by a UK vote whilst the Women’s Footballer of the Year award will be done via a global vote, reflecting its heritage as a BBC World Service award.

Harry Kane, who has stormed into hot favouritism for the main award, is surely nailed on to win the new footballer award after he took home the Ballon d’Or just weeks ago.

The Bayern Munich star had an incredible year for club and country last season, scoring 61 times in 51 appearances for the German giants alone.

FANS have urged Manchester United to appoint Javier Hernandez following his passionate speech before the club’s Premier League clash with Aston Villa.

Hernandez – also known as ‘Chicharito’ – was at Old Trafford to watch the match on Sunday.



The 38-year-old, who spent five years at United earlier in his career, spoke to Sky Sports ahead of kick-off and gave his view on the club’s ongoing struggles.

While the heat is on head coach Michael Carrick and the board, Hernandez argued that the players need to be taking more responsibility.



He said: “I’m still a current football player, but I was a Manchester United player.

“There was a time that even in tough moments it wasn’t about if Sir Alex Ferguson did good or did bad in strategy or in tactics.

“It was more of the players need to perform over there. After this white line when the whistle blows there is nothing much more the manager can do.

“They can tell you to defend more, run more or whatever, but putting on the Manchester United shirt you shouldn’t be looking at what is lacking.

“You need to give your life for this club, because it can be the best chapter in your career.

“For a lot of us, for example, and for a lot of players. You have to give everything.

“I think we need to be a little bit more critical with players, regardless of the tactics and how management and ownership can be, I understand a lot of how that’s part of something.

“But players, if you’re here you need to prove why you’re here, regardless of which position you play and regardless of which position your manager is putting to you.”

Sports.title: Unseen footage shows furious Mikel Arteta kicking chair after Arsenal star’s ‘nonchalant casual play’ against Hull
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA was filmed kicking a chair in the Arsenal dugout following some “nonchalant” play from his team against Hull City.

The 44-year-old was visibly furious when the Gunners lost the ball multiple times in the late stages.

And he appeared to crack when Eberechi Eze fouled a Hull player.



Arteta quickly turned around before storming over to his chair.



He then kicked it before walking back to the edge of his technical area.

The fan who shared the clip on social media commented: “Mikel Arteta kicked the chair in FURIOUS RAGE at Eze’s nonchalant casual play at the end of the game. He’s had enough!”

Another wrote: “We see Havertz do the same every single game without that reaction.”

While a third said: “It gets frustrating sometimes.”

However, some Arsenal supporters argued that Arteta was just frustrated at the referee.

The Gunners went on to win the match 1-0 thanks to a second-half strike from Martin Odegaard.

Sports.title: Man Utd’s catastrophic defence needs open-heart surgery as Carrick faces back-four crisis before trip to Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

THE chaos that comes with Manchester United surpassed all expectations as the final whistle blew in their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Alysson and Nicolas Jackson launched a brutal attack on the Red Devils, putting them two behind inside the first four minutes.



Bruno Fernandes’ spot-kick and Youri Tielemans‘ first United goal dragged the hosts level before another two-goal lead was imposed less than ten minutes later.

And if that was not enough, Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu found the back of the net in injury time to help them take a point back to their digs in 18th.



SunSport’s Manchester United reporter Katherine Walsh talked through the three big points from the messy fixture.

FAN PROTESTS

Each Manchester United game just cranks up the heat on the club’s under-fire hierarchy.



New signs, chants, banners, failed walkout plans and tennis balls thrown on to the pitch.

Yesterday, there was a new sign on show that read, “We don’t want a new stadium, we want new owners”.

That was unfurled in the Stretford End, where Red Devils fans still sang boss Michael Carrick’s song.

SunSport was also sent pictures of “F*** the Glazers” spread across gold and green balloons — the colours of the original Newton Heath club.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Several balloons made their way over to the directors’ box in the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand, where director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada tried to ignore the hate.

Frustrated fans made their feelings clear with anti-Glazer hatred aimed at the missing American family, who are seemingly preoccupied with their Tampa Bay NFL team.

And minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe — who has his eyes set on a new ‘Wembley of the North’ to replace Old Trafford by 2035 — also faced flak.

How about fixing the issues on the pitch to avoid relegation?



The demonstrations reflected the growing unrest surrounding the club’s direction, with supporters demanding accountability and a clear plan to save the Red Devils from the dreaded drop.

For many supporters, a change in fortunes will not be enough.

LEAKY DEFENCE

United’s entire backline is a total shambles and the club now needs open-heart surgery to fix it.

The Red Devils have shipped 30 goals in all competitions this season — only Lens with 31 have a worse record across Europe’s top five leagues. It is a ­defensive crisis.



Their frontline showed admirable fight to haul them back into the contest against Aston Villa, but it was like trying to win a boxing match with both hands tied behind your back.

Whatever Carrick’s side produce going forward, their defenders look capable of throwing it all away.

They have now conceded 15 goals in their last five games — including a 4-1 humiliation in Como — with a trip to Liverpool now looming after the international break.

A defensive rebuild is promised for summer 2027 and I would struggle to find many who deserve to survive next season.



Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez are all out of contract, while Diogo Dalot has reached the point of no return amid a Joshua Zirkzee-style humiliation.

There were huge, mocking cheers when the Portuguese full-back was replaced by Patrick Dorgu on 66 ­minutes — the Old Trafford reaction was reminiscent of the savage reception handed out to Zirkzee when he was hooked against Newcastle back in 2024.

Dalot was all at sea for Villa’s opener before gifting them a daft penalty shortly after the break.

Yet making him the fall guy misses the bigger picture. Changes are needed across the back, who are without a clean sheet in the league this season.

Manchester United Defensive Record ACROSS all competitive fixtures, Manchester United have conceded 30 goals in 15 matches: Premier League (19 goals in 10 matches): Hull City 2–0 Manchester United Manchester United 5–2 Ipswich Town Everton 2–2 Manchester United Manchester United 0–1 Manchester City Fulham 1–1 Manchester United Manchester United 1–1 Tottenham Hotspur Leeds United 1–1 Manchester United Manchester United 0–3 AFC Bournemouth Chelsea 2–0 Manchester United Manchester United 4–4 Aston Villa Champions League (8 goals in 4 matches): Manchester United 4–0 Sabah Atlético Madrid 2–0 Manchester United Como 4–1 Manchester United Manchester United 3–2 AS Roma EFL Cup (3 goals in 1 match): Manchester United 2–3 Brighton & Hove Albion



LACK OF LEADERS

Carrick’s struggling side play off moments, which is unsustainable in the Prem.

It is the hallmark of a side desperately short of structure, leadership and control.

It also explains why the fallen giants have found themselves in the relegation places.

Their attack has stepped up, with Matheus Cunha almost a one-man band, trying to inject the energy and urgency required.

And who would have predicted Danish wideman Dorgu becoming the unlikely saviour?



His goal and assist helped rescue a point and handed Carrick an eight-point haul from ten games.

Bruno Fernandes looked furious at the final whistle despite the comeback, which told its own story.

Even Cunha and Amad Diallo had the audacity to gesture towards the crowd for more noise, despite the wreck unfolding in front of them.

Old Trafford has shown it can roar when given something to believe in — and the players feed off that energy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But it should not be the supporters’ job to drag the team over the line.

United need to give their fans something to shout about — not keep demanding they help bail them out.



It was Villa who threw this one away.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace ready to sack Pierre Sage after woeful start to season with two immediate frontrunners to replace him

CRYSTAL PALACE are ready to SACK manager Pierre Sage after just 16 games in charge.

The Frenchman’s future is hanging by a thread following today’s 3-1 defeat to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.



The latest humiliation left the Eagles rock bottom of the Premier League table after a disastrous start to the campaign.

Palace are set to part company with Sage, 47, just five months after appointing him as manager.



SunSport understands Thomas Frank and Sean Dyche are the two leading contenders to take over at Selhurst Park.

Frank has been out of work since being dismissed by Spurs in February, having previously earned widespread praise for establishing Brentford as a Premier League club.

Sage arrived at Selhurst Park in June to replace Oliver Glasner, who had guided Palace to historic FA Cup and Europa Conference League triumphs.

But the former Lens boss has endured a nightmare opening to life in English football, with Palace winning just twice in their opening ten league matches.

Sunday’s defeat was their fourth consecutive Premier League loss, while their leaky defence has conceded a staggering 24 goals – the worst record in the division.

Sports.title: ‘This just can’t go on’ – Gary Neville fears Man Utd ‘causing themselves emotional damage’ with post-match antics
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE revealed his brutal worries concerning Michael Carrick’s Manchester United after their 4-4 thriller with Aston Villa.

The Red Devils trailed the Villans by two goals after just four minutes in their box office clash.



Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans dragged the hosts level, only for a quickfire Villa double after half-time to have them 4-2 down once more.

While two goals from United in injury time meant that both sides took away a point apiece, Neville is concerned about the “emotional damage” they are causing themselves.



After the final whistle blew, Carrick & Co. sauntered around the pitch, clapping the home fans – but the former Prem skipper is not convinced.

The 51-year-old said: “You have got to admire their persistence. They kept going.

“Their defensive errors were shocking.

“I played for Manchester United 602 times. I always appreciated the fans after the game.”

Neville admitted that the post-match “lap of honour”, particularly after the 3-0 Bournemouth result too, was “painful to watch”.

He said: “It’s almost like they’re causing themselves emotional damage.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“This just can’t go on, can it? It’s absolutely desperate.

“Michael will be proud of them.

“The fans are singing his name because they love him, but this is a really sorry situation.”



Before the game, the clash was viewed as a make or break for Carrick, but the draw just might be enough for him to survive the international break.

During the Villa game, Diogo Dalot was booed off by the United fans, but the boss insisted that he’s “giving everything” he’s got.

Carrick said: “We’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that.

“Diogo, he gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions, he’s played left back, he’s played really well at times.

“He gives a penalty away today, he knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better, all right, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake, but he cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.



“So I like what he brings to the team, I like what he brings to the group, I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

“Picking a team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision, but it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.”

United still only have one Premier League win to their name this season from a 5-2 home victory over Ipswich on August 30.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

They now lie 18th in the rankings, knowing that when they return, Liverpool will be waiting.

Following the Anfield fixture, United will travel to Sporting in the Champions League, where they currently sit in the middle of the play-off qualifiers spots after four games.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick future LIVE: Man Utd sack latest as Mauricio Pochettino becomes fifth target
Sports.content:
Head Coach Michael Carrick of Manchester United walks off after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford

Manchester United go into the international break in the Premier League relegation zone after a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has swerved the gallows for now after his side fought back to draw 4-4 against Aston Villa. But with the international break arriving, if he is going to be relieved of his duties, now would be the time to do it.

United are still wallowing in the relegation places, sitting 18th. Although they trailed by two goals on two separate occasions at Old Trafford against Unai Emery's Villa, a late Patrick Dorgu equaliser rescued a much-needed point on Sunday.

But unrest is still rife and with 10 matches played in the top flight, only eight points have been collected. United are next in action against Liverpool on November 22, 13 days away.

Although it appears Carrick's post is safe for the time being, the international break could give the club the perfect opportunity to bring in a new regime and reports suggest five names are on the shortlist - with USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino now emerging as a surprise fifth option.

Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Stuttgart boss Sebastian Hoeness have also been mentioned as possible targets.

So stick around as Mirror Football brings you the latest on the ever-changing situation at the Theatre of Dreams.

Sports.title: Roy Keane calls out 'casual' Michael Carrick as he questions Man Utd's honesty in epic rant
Sports.content:
Roy Keane calls out 'casual' Michael Carrick as he questions Man Utd's honesty in epic rant

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane slammed Michael Carrick and his players for their response to the chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, which left them in the relegation zone

View 3 Images Roy Keane went on a classic rant after Manchester United's draw against Aston Villa (Image: Sky Sports)

Roy Keane has accused Michael Carrick of being too "casual" and Manchester United's players of lying to themselves after being disgusted by their post-match interviews on Sunday.

‌



United drew 4-4 with Aston Villa at Old Trafford in a chaotic game which left Carrick's future in doubt going into the international break. The home side were shambolic in defence, with individual errors helping Villa, but they showed fight to come back from two goals down on two occasions.

Goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu in injury time earned a point, but United are 18th in the table having gone eight Premier League matches without a win. Carrick gave a spiky post-match interview in which he said he expected to continue as manager, while Dorgu and Matheus Cunha insisted they could turn things around.

Their words did not impress former United captain Keane, who responded with a trademark rant on Sky Sports. "The challenge for any manager who group of coaches and players is you've got to work with what you've got in front of you," he began.

"We see the Villa manager chopping and changing all summer and his hands are tied a little bit but when he gets a group of players to work with he works with them, he tries to make them better and generally speaking he does that. Villa over the last few years have come good towards the end of the season.

"What's the sign of insanity? Doing the same thing over and over and expecting something different. We come here and we knew they'd give up loads of chances. It's up to the manager and group of players to do something about it. You listen to the players talking about the mentality and we're disappointed, well you've got to do something about it.

"It's very hard for us to listen to the messages coming out of the United camp when I'm thinking, I'm not even sure you're being honest with yourselves, so how can we believe a word you're saying?

"What we're seeing most weeks is chaotic defending, people not organised, people not putting their bodies on the line. Then they give interviews and the manager will go we need to tighten up. It's just words, isn't it?

"We're waiting for a reaction from the United team, whether it be after the big defeat from Bournemouth or Como."

Keane then turned his attention to Carrick, whose measured style isn't to his taste. "I admire people who are maybe casual like that," he said. "I wish I was casual like that! I see Carrick and he's like, 'we just have to tighten up'. I'm going, 'tighten up? You should be banging heads!'

"We're all different. But put it this way: they're going to Liverpool in a few weeks. How many chances are Liverpool going to get? I don't think this is a top Liverpool team but do you believe United are going to roll their sleeves up and get a clean sheet? Dig in deep? Be hard to beat? Start quick? Well, good luck with that one..."

He then added: "It's obviously difficult for the manager. Under pressure, no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn't say much. I don't know if that's a tactic. Like a politician.

"He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there's things we need to work on. But they better get moving on that. It's the worst start in how many years, all these stats aren't very good. If you keep giving up goals and chances, it's just going to continue.

‌



‌



United drew 4-4 with Aston Villa in a drama-filled Premier League game on Sunday afternoon. Michael Carrick's side came from two goals down twice, with their attack showing fight to cancel out their shambolic defence.

‌



The home side were 2-0 down after four minutes after mistakes by Senne Lammens allowed Alysson and Nicolas Jackson to score. They fought back through Bruno Fernandes' penalty and Youri Tielemans' goal, but their good work was undermined early in the second half.

‌



Diogo Dalot's foul on Alysson saw John McGinn score from the spot before Leon Goretzka netted from close range after a mistake by Leny Yoro. Substitutes Joshua Zirzkee and Patrick Dorgu then both scored in injury time to claim a point in a chaotic finish.

After the full-time whistle, United's players wandered around the pitch to applaud the fans, who chanted Carrick's name in support of their under-fire boss, whose side sit 18th in the Premier League after an eighth match without a win. "You got to admire their persistence, they kept going," Neville said. "The defensive errors were shocking and we'll discuss that shortly. But this lap around the pitch...

Sports.content:

Andoni Iraola was "very upset" after a controversial penalty decision cost Liverpool a clean sheet in victory at Crystal Palace.

‌



Liverpool head into the international break fourth in the Premier League thanks to a 3-1 win at Selhurst Park. Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak made sure of the points before Eddie Nketiah netted from the spot in injury time.

The consolation goal for Palace came after Milos Kerkez was penalised following a clash of heads with Dario Osorio in the box. Referee Tony Harrington pointed to the spot after the clash which occurred while both players tried to head a bouncing ball.

‌



His call was confirmed by VAR Michael Salisbury and Nketiah beat Alisson from 12 yards to get on the scoresheet. Iraola was furious last weekend after Isak was not given a penalty in the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal for a clear shirt-pull by Jurrien Timber and he made his case once again on Sunday.

Sports.title: Liverpool's patience with Alexander Isak pays off as win puts Pierre Sage on the brink
Sports.content:
This season will probably be more about securing Champions League football rather than a full-on title race.

But after results like this, you can see why Liverpool fans have bought into Andoni Iraola’s exciting vision because they were ruthless, clinical and determined as they climbed up into the top four.

Their patience with Alexander Isak has reaped rewards because the Liverpool striker now looks unstoppable after his eighth goal in all competitions sealed the win.

The Liverpool faithful are also still enthusiastically singing Bradley Barcola’s name even though the £123million signing has yet to score in the Premier League since his summer arrival. And, frankly, under-pressure Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage had better hope he gets as much understanding and sees out the forthcoming international break (also known as the sacking window).

‌

This was so much better from Palace and, if it had not been for Liverpool keeper Alisson Becker’s heroics, then the score line could have been very different. Instead, Palace have sunk to the bottom of the Premier League table, have the worst defensive record in the division - they have conceded 24 goals - and you suspect Sage will be waiting by the phone in the next fortnight.

It will be a tough decision for Palace chairman Steve Parish because he rarely gets it wrong and he will have seen from the directors’ box the score line was harsh on his team. Yes, there were familiar mistakes and hard luck stories but Palace showed real heart this time and they deserved more than just substitute Eddie Nketiah’s injury-time consolation from the penalty spot.

‌



But the question now for Parish is whether an improved performance is enough or if they should press the panic button and get on the phone to Sean Dyche in the next fortnight. It will probably be the latter.

Palace do not have Liverpool’s resources but even big-money talent like Barcola, Isak and Florian Wirtz take time to settle. It was far from a flowing Liverpool performance, but they got the job done.

‌



It seems bizarre to make the keeper from the winning side the best player on the pitch but they would have lost without Alisson. The Brazil keeper still probably does not get the credit he deserves.

Liverpool’s goal lived a charmed life early on as Yeremy Pino crashed a shot against the bar with one of those efforts where the commentator says he “almost hit it too well.” What on earth does that mean?

Jorgen Strand Larsen had the ball in the Liverpool net but was very clearly offside. Palace midfielder Daichi Kamada’s powerful volley forced another brilliant save from the Liverpool keeper who also denied Adam Wharton.

At the other end, Liverpool had plenty of possession but their finishing was wayward as Barcola skied over with a volley which cleared the stand and the crossbar.

‌



View 3 Images Florian Wirtz scored on the break for Liverpool (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

But finally, Liverpool got their breakthrough after a moment of controversy. Referee Tony Harrington gave a free kick when it looked as if Cody Gakpo had just run into Jefferson Lerma. It looked so harsh.

Dominik Szoboszlai whipped in a near post free kick and there was Alexis Mac Allister to glance home past Palace keeper Dean Henderson. Unsurprisingly, the Palace fans vented their anger at the officials. Parish had his head in his hands in the directors’ box.

The trouble is, once Liverpool got themselves in front, there was only ever going to be one outcome. And maybe that is the most damning thing for Sage. Liverpool’s second came nine minutes after the restart.

‌



Barcola’s low cross evaded the Palace defence and Florian Wirtz swept home from inside the box. Wirtz then set up Isak to score in the 89th minute.

There was still time for Palace to get a consolation. Milos Kerkez jumped into Dario Osorio and it was a clear penalty which Nketiah converted. You fear it may not be enough to save Sage.

Sports.title: Gary Neville makes bizarre confession about brother Phil on live TV
Sports.content:
Gary Neville makes bizarre confession about brother Phil on live TV

The two defenders played alongside each other for Manchester United and England before their careers took different turns

View 2 Images Gary Neville had to ask his brother Phil where he lived. (Image: NBC Sports/YouTube.)

Gary Neville has admitted that he doesn’t know specifically where his brother Phil lives in America. The pair were reunited for the first time in three years as they both appeared on NBC Sports' Premier League coverage.

‌



‌



Since they both retired from playing, their careers have taken different paths. Phil has taken more of a coaching role, having previously managed England Women before moving to the USA to manage Inter Miami in 2021.

‌



His most recent position saw him spend just over two years as manager of Portland Timbers. He left the job back in May after 95 matches in charge.

‌



Arsenal rivals put on notice as 'worrying' title claim made after Hull City win READ MORE :

Gary, meanwhile, has made his name in punditry. He makes regular appearances on Sky Sports’ coverage of the Premier League, as well as the Overlap Podcast.

But this weekend has seen both brothers working together again. They were both part of NBC Sports’ coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City.

Opening the programme, presenter Rebecca Lowe said: “How about this? A little bit of television history about to be made. Phil Neville and Gary Neville on television together on a show for the first time ever, am I right?”

‌



Gary then responded with: "Absolutely. We've not seen each other for three years either."

Phil, then said: "He doesn't know where I live." It's something that Lowe confirmed. "Correct. He actually doesn't," she added.

‌



"He actually asked Phil, 'Whereabouts do you live?' before we came on air. As you sit here together for the first time ever on television, how does it feel?"

Phil answered: "Well, it's just nice to see him. We obviously spent a lot of time together in our careers.

‌



"I live in America, he lives in England, and hopefully tonight we can have a nice glass of wine."

Gary then added: "It's brilliant. We don't see each other, obviously, that much anymore.

‌



View 2 Images Phil Neville was brother Gary's assistant manager at Valencia. (Image: Manuel Queimadelos Alonso/Getty Images)

‌



"Phil's been in America with Miami and Portland for the last four or five years, and now he's living in Florida, apparently. Very nice place! It beats Manchester. I wish I was there."

The two brothers played together as teammates for both Man United and England 287 times. The duo lifted six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and the Champions League together.

‌



They also worked together briefly during Gary’s stint as Valencia manager in 2015, when Phil joined as assistant. They, however, only lasted 16 league games, winning just three of those.

Speaking in November last year, Phil spoke about his relationship with his brother, amid his induction into the Premier League Hall of Fame. "We are best friends," he told the Premier League.

Sports.title: Warner: Khawaja's Australia Sandpapergate claims '100 per cent accurate'
Sports.content:
David Warner has thrown his full support behind former Australia opener Usman Khawaja, who claimed that the side's entire dressing room knew about the ball-tampering scheme in Cape Town in 2018.

Khawaja has claimed in recent days that players and coaching staff were aware of the ball-tampering that occurred in South Africa eight years ago, stating: "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us," the 39-year-old told the Sydney Morning Herald, which is serialising the book.

Warner also claimed the investigation held by Cricket Australia in the aftermath of the ball-tampering controversy was "rushed and botched".

Warner and fellow batters ‌Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were banned over the plan to rough up the ball with sandpaper ​during the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Khawaja has claimed that the side's entire dressing room knew about the ball-tampering incident in Cape Town in 2018

In an excerpt of his autobiography released on Saturday, Khawaja said "open, lighthearted discussions" about tampering were ​not confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.

On ‌Sunday, he added that he had chosen to speak about the 'Sandpapergate' scandal now after promising childhood friend Warner that ​he would share his side of the story.

Until now, nobody else involved in the tour has ever admitted culpability.

The bowling unit of Pat Cummins - now Australia captain - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon even released a statement in 2021 denying they knew anything about the tactic.

Warner said in a video statement on Instagram: "People wanted to know it, you've come out and said it, and now people are saying, 'Why eight years on?' and talking about selling a book.

"This is Usman's story. This is what Usman believes. Uzzi wrote down every single thing from that day on. Uzzi, thank you.

"Now, this whole interview process was rushed and botched. Uzzi was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft. Uzzi was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me.

"We're not here to point fingers and we're not opening old wounds. It's about accountability, transparency and ensuring that the truth is properly examined."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Samuel explains what impact Khawaja's claims that the entire Australia team were aware of the ball-tampering scheme in South Africa in 2018 could have on next summer's Ashes series in England

Warner, who retired from cricket's traditional format in 2024 with 112 Test caps, said he decided to comment now after talking to his young daughters over recent days about what transpired in that match and later.

"Perhaps it's time people stop scrutinising the person asking for accountability and start asking those responsible for the investigation to provide it," he continued.

"Now, there have been a lot of statements and inaccuracies over the last eight years that were out in the media by people and there were a lot of people who stayed silent.

"The last couple of days I've been talking to my daughters and that's why it's taken me a couple of days to get this out, because I've had to tell them exactly what happened.

"Especially my 12-year-old Ivy, who wanted to know why we were holding her, why there were so many cameras and why we were crying on TV. That was a hard thing to do.

"But one thing I did say was, 'Girls, tell the truth, because lies will eventually come out'. It's a very tough time.

"This is for everyone in Australia. It's been the question that everyone's been asking. Uzzi, you said it how it is. It's 100 per cent accurate.

"It's been a tough time for my family, Steven and Cameron, no doubt, but this is what needed to come out. I fully support that, Uzzi."

Sports.title: Los Angeles Golf Club make history by winning inaugural WTGL match
Sports.content:
Los Angeles Golf Club sealed a 3-1 victory over New York in an historic first WTGL match at SoFi Center.

Lydia Ko and Michelle Wie West were among the six players in action who treated an audience of 1,500 fans at the indoor venue in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida to some spectacular shot-making, several dramatic near-misses and pure entertainment between the mic'd-up players.

Wie West, Alison Lee and Gaby Lopez eventually out-duelled Rose Zhang and her team-mates in Linn Grant and Ko.

New York's Zhang broke new ground as she hit the first tee shot, one that she blasted 301 yards into the fairway on Cut The Sails.

Wie West came agonisingly close to registering a hole-in-in-one at the par-three seventh as Los Angeles built a narrow 2-1 lead over New York after the first nine holes of team play. New York took number 5, and Lee took down Grant on number 11

In the closing holes, New York had chances, but Zhang missed two short putts on the 13th hole and Grant missed a 10-foot putt on the 14th.

That secured the win for Los Angeles, 3-1, before the teams tied the final hole.

"Our purses are growing up, and we get to play the most amazing golf courses we've ever played," Lee said. "For people to experience and see us play in a different setting, in a more intimate and personal setting, is very different, and hopefully it can bring more eyeballs to the game."

Los Angeles will have a chance to build a verifiable winning streak on Tuesday as the inaugural season begins to ramp up.

Wie West and co will take on Motor City Golf Club, who boast a line-up led by Lexi Thompson and Brooke Henderson.

What is the WTGL?

The WTGL follows on from the success of the Tomorrow's Golf League (TGL), founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy's TMRW Sports, in partnership with the PGA Tour.

The women's edition of the tech-infused golf league will see LPGA Tour stars feature in a unique team format, with five teams (representing five different cities) of five-player rosters confirmed for the inaugural season.

The season-long competition takes place across November and December at the SoFi Center in Florida, a purpose-built indoor venue, with every shot live and all the players mic'd up for the made-for-TV format.

How can I watch the WTGL on Sky Sports?

Both the 2026 and 2027 editions of WTGL will be broadcast exclusively on Sky Sports as part of an expansion of its golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi.

Every match will be exclusively live on Sky Sports Golf, Sky Sports+ or Sky Sports Mix, while repeats will be available the following day on Sky Sports Golf. You can also download the Sky Sports App for news, highlights, scores and reports.

Sports.title: Brown becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
Sports.content:
Blades Brown has become the youngest PGA Tour winner since 1931 after the 19-year-old came back from a deficit of seven shots with a nine-under 63 to defeat Ben James in the World Wide Technology Championship.

At 19 years and 171 days old, Brown became the youngest victor since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.

James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his nerve by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-five 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the play-off.

But he missed an eight-foot putt on the second play-off hole as Brown made his three-footer.

"I just go back to five-year-old Blades that was watching the TV and watching Tiger Woods and all those great players win major championships, and to think that I'm now in a similar spot with having won a PGA Tour event is mind-blowing."

Sports.title: Gauff survives Pegula test to win all-American thriller at WTA Finals
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff shredded her shoes but stayed one step ahead of Jessica Pegula to defeat her compatriot ‌6-4 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 on the opening day of the WTA Finals at Indian Wells, while Czech Linda Noskova got the better of Marta Kostyuk 6-2 6-4.

Gauff ‌had beaten Pegula three months ago in Cincinnati and had the right formula once again, as the 2024 winner showed superb versatility in ​a round-robin clash between the top two Americans in the season-ending championship.

World No 4 Gauff took the opener and recovered from 5-1 down in the second to come within a point of winning in straight sets.

But it was Pegula's turn to dig in from 5-6, saving a match point and then playing a terrific tie-break to extend the contest at Indian Wells.

Gauff took charge of the match in the third set, breaking to lead 3-0 before earning her sixth win against Pegula after two hours and 39 minutes.

Pegula would probably have been grateful to get the tennis under way after her viral and awkward 'hot mic' moment when disparaging comments she made about fellow player Mirra Andreeva to her coach during a training session were picked up on a livestream.

That prompted a grovelling apology from the WTA, which admitted it had not told players the microphones were on, and damage control behind the scenes from Pegula.

The world No 5 had compared Andreeva's mentality unfavourably with Gauff's in her indiscreet comments, and the two-time Grand Slam champion set about showing her competitive grit, clawing her way back with five games in a row, including saving three set points.

Sometime doubles partners Gauff and Pegula had shared their 10 previous meetings, while this was the fourth year in a row they were meeting at the WTA Finals.

"Honestly, ‌I was having a lot of fun today. I took a little break, it was my first match in a month," said Gauff, who was last in action at the China Open in early October.

"To play a tournament like this ‌with no preparation is something I've never done in my career. I'm just really happy to get through today. It was a tough match."

The 22-year-old said she had to be aggressive to deal with Pegula's game.

"I also had to run a lot," she added. "My shoes are pretty torn up now. Some of my shoes are like somewhere on the court there, ⁠so I'm going to have to change shoes tomorrow."

Noskova keen for another accolade

Kostyuk is standing in for No 1 seed Elena Rybakina after the Kazakh withdrew a day before the tournament citing a medical issue, and got off to an understandably slow start, as Noskova broke her serve at the second time of asking before winning four of the next five games in a dominant first-set performance.

Kostyuk made a stronger start in the second set, wining her first two games on serve, but a Noskova break put the No 8 seed ahead 4-2, and her Ukranian opponent's missed opportunity to break back at 4-3 down proved costly, with the Czech winning her next two service games and securing the straight-sets victory.

Sports.title: Rugby League World Cup 2030 to be staged in Pacific-USA
Sports.content:
It has been proposed that Tonga and Samoa will be given Tier 1 status thanks to their on-field performances; the RLWC 2030 will take place across the Pacific and USA; it will have a 'Magic Round' format that will see the tournament descend on a new host city each week

Tonga and Samoa will be given Tier 1 status thanks to their sensational on-field performance

International Rugby League has announced the Rugby League World Cup 2030 men's and women's tournaments will be staged in cities across the Pacific and United States of America with more teams to be involved.

The competitions will be played with a 'Magic Round' format that will see the teams arrive in a host city for a round of the tournaments before moving on.

The IRL board has also approved changes to international eligibility rules to increase the pool of players available to nations and they have endorsed the elevation of Tonga and Samoa to Men's Tier 1 status, subject to consultation with both teams.

The elevation of Samoa and Tonga as Tier 1 nations would be in recognition of their performances on and off the field, with both nations reaching the semi-finals of RLWC26. Samoa became the first Pacific nation to play in a World Cup final in 2022, while Tonga are the only Tier 2 nation to have defeated Australia, England and New Zealand.

Sports.title: Euro Debrief: Kane has become the king of assists
Sports.content:
Welcome to The Euro Debrief, the Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week:

Kane is the assist king

Barcelona win in Madrid

Inter close gap on Lazio

Eleven in a row for PSG

Weghorst denies Ajax

Bundesliga: Kane is assist king

Whisper it but Harry Kane has gone four games without scoring a goal. That has only happened once before in his Bayern Munich career and in that sequence he went off at half-time in one game and came on as a second-half substitute in another. Drought!

It is not an issue for Kane or club because the England captain laid on both goals for his team-mates in a 2-1 win at Mainz that maintains Bayern's place at the top of the Bundesliga table. The Ballon d'Or winner has become the competition's king of assists this season.

LaLiga: Big moment in title race

Atletico Madrid were heading to top spot in LaLiga when Julian Alvarez set up Giuliano Simeone for the opening goal against leaders Barcelona at the Metropolitano on Sunday evening. But two goals from Fermin Lopez turned the game around to secure a big win.

It was a typically competitive start by Diego Simeone's side, enough to fuel the argument that Hansi Flick's Barca have an issue asserting themselves against the strongest sides after those back-to-back losses against Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain recently.

But Flick will be massively encouraged by the response from his side. It is well worth checking out the winner, wonderfully set up by Lamine Yamal, but the control with which Barca saw it out was significant. Instead of Atletico leapfrogging them, they are five points ahead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the LaLiga match between Atletico Madrid and Barcelona

Real Madrid are up to second and back ahead of their city neighbours in the table after a convincing 3-0 win away to Valencia, whose struggles continue. Kylian Mbappe scored again despite being booed by the home fans but Arda Guler impressed most.

This column mentioned last week that Yan Diomande has taken Vinicius Junior's spot on the left while the Brazilian is out but it is the Turkish playmaker from wide who is bringing such balance to Madrid's attack and is the reason why Vini now has a problem.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the LaLiga match between Valencia and Real Madrid

Arda Guler, who scored one and assisted Mbappe's goal, brings such creativity cutting inside that pairing two flyers down the flanks would see Madrid lose a dimension to their game. With Fede Valverde, who scored one of his now trademark stunners from right-back, there are promising signs for Jose Mourinho.

It is also worth mentioning newly-promoted Racing Santander who won at Malaga and might be the most fun team in LaLiga. They have conceded more goals than anyone but Racing are still in the top half for possession - and crucially points. Their positivity is paying off.

LaLiga results: Sevilla 0-0 Alaves, Malaga 1-2 Racing Santander, Espanyol 0-0 Deportivo A Coruna, Osasuna 1-1 Athletic Club, Valencia 0-3 Real Madrid, Elche 0-2 Real Betis, Real Sociedad 1-0 Rayo Vallecano, Celta Vigo 0-0 Levante, Villarreal 2-0 Getafe, Atletico Madrid 1-2 Barcelona.

Serie A: Inter close gap on Lazio

Lazio's run of six consecutive wins in Serie A came to an end as they had to settle for a draw away to Napoli. It was still a good result for Gennaro Gattuso's surprise leaders in Italy given that it was Kevin De Bruyne who came the closest to winning it for the hosts.

Even so, the result means Inter were able to close the gap to just one point with a 2-0 win over Como at San Siro. Cesc Fabregas' side had plenty of possession but lacked the cutting edge of the reigning champions who scored twice early to control the game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Serie A match between Inter Milan and Como

Roma closed the gap too, extending their lead as Italy's top scorers and maintaining their unbeaten record with a 3-0 win over Sassuolo. Rodrigo Mora, subbed with Roma two up at Old Trafford on Tuesday, was involved in all the goals, scoring the last himself.

The Portuguese teenager is a tremendous talent. Could he drive Roma on to the title? "Inter are best placed to win," said his coach Gian Piero Gasperini afterwards. "For the rest, all of us are in the mix, us included." It is beautifully poised going into the break.

Elsewhere, Torino and Lecce traded own goals, while Milan picked up three points at Genoa to put that alarming European defeat to Ferencvaros behind them. Juventus came from behind twice to draw at Fiorentina but stay six points adrift of the top four.

Ligue 1: Eleven in a row for PSG

Paris Saint-Germain followed up their six-goal demolition of Villarreal in the Champions League with a more underwhelming 1-0 victory at home to Troyes but their run continues. Luis Enrique's side have now won 11 games in a row in all competitions.

The European champions stay two points clear at the top because Lille and Paris FC both earned away wins. Lassine Sinayoko scored the only goal of the game away to Auxerre to take his tally for the season in Ligue 1 to nine, two clear of anyone else.

Elsewhere, Monaco dropped points late on against Le Mans, while Lyon, who are between coaches with Carlos Vicens set to replace Paulo Fonseca, lost at Brest. All of which has allowed Marseille to rise to fourth as they continue their climb up the table.

Having beaten Bayer Leverkusen on Thursday, Marseille saw off Lens to make it five consecutive wins domestically for Bruno Genesio's side. They are much improved since the window closed and things have settled down at a club where things are never calm.

It helped that Lens were the opposition. That second-place finish under Pierre Sage already feels an age ago for club and coach. Sage's successor Dino Toppmoller is long gone. It was Yannick Cahuzac who oversaw that 9-1 beating by Como in midweek.

A response was required. Instead, Lens gifted Marseille the opener after 90 seconds as a result of an awful defensive mix-up. Even when they levelled, Lens contrived to lose late on. The shame of that 9-1 will take longer than an international break to go away.

Elsewhere: Weghorst denies Ajax

It was a strange Sunday in the Eredivisie as the big three not only all had different results away from home but all had spells on top of the table. Once it was over, it was reigning champions PSV, who had started the day in third place, who finished it back on top.

Feyenoord had been two up at Heerenveen but lost 5-3 to present Ajax with the chance to move top and confirm their improvement under Michel. Instead, Twente came from two down to snatch a point thanks to Wout Weghorst's 95th-minute penalty leveller.

Weghorst left Ajax in the summer and his replacement Tolu Arokodare, who opened the scoring, has done well. But it is nine in 12 for him at Twente now. Strong work. With PSV making no mistake in beating Cambuur 5-2 it is all set up for an exciting title race.

Whether that will be the case in Portugal is not so clear. Benfica did manage a 95th-minute goal of their own through Vangelis Pavlidis but Marco Silva's side are still five points behind perfect Porto who won late again to make it 11 wins from 11 for them.

Sports.title: Baumgardner targets Dubois after outclassing Turhan
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner, an undisputed world champion at super-featherweight, moved up to lightweight to capture the IBF world title when she shut out Elif Tur Nurhan in Texas.

Baumgardner won a unanimous decision after 10 rounds as she overcame Nurhan at College Park Center in Arlington.

The American won 100-90 on all three cards, beating a hard puncher who had never lost before.

Baumgardner hurt Turhan at times, shaking her up in the third and seventh rounds.

Image: Baumgardner outclassed a hard puncher

Turhan was under real pressure at the end of the third, when a mistake granted her a fortunate reprieve. The action was briefly halted when the 10-second clapper was mistaken for the bell.

"I hit her, I've seen her legs wobble, [I thought:] 'We got her' and then the bell rang or something happened," Baumgardner said.

"Back to business though. Those moments can happen in a fight. It's about staying composed."

Baumgardner poured in punches, with Nurhan feeling the weight of those attacks too in the ninth round. Nurhan went the distance but, despite her punch power, could not threaten Baumgardner.

Now the IBF champion, Baumgardner looks to be on a collision course with Caroline Dubois, who fights Stephanie Han for the WBA, WBC and WBO 135lb titles on February 20, live on Sky Sports.

Image: Baumgardner reacts as she becomes a two-weight world champion

Baumgardner and Dubois have clashed before and the Briton was ringside in Texas. Their war of words continued after the American's latest win.

"Are we going to fight?" Dubois demanded.

"You've got a champ right there in front of you," Baumgardner warned.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player WBC lightweight champion Caroline Dubois calls out Baumgardner for a unification fight

Ramla Ali took a contentious split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps to win the WBO and IBF super-bantamweight titles.

Ali started sharply and knocked Kreps down with a right hook right on the chin in the third round. From then on, though, Kreps maintained real pressure on Ali and the two finished trading punches before the final bell.

Kreps won widely, 98-91, for one judge but Ali took it 96-93 and 97-92 on the other two cards.

It was an emotional victory for Ali, whose family had to flee Somalia when she was a child and settled in London. She dedicated the victory to the memory of her father who passed away earlier this year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO and IBF super-bantamweight world title fight between Ramla Ali and Mikiah Kreps

Skye Nicolson defended the WBC super-bantamweight title, beating Japan's Miyo Yoshida, winning a unanimous decision on a dominant display.

Nicolson took the victory 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92.

Yoshida found moments of success on the inside, landing right hands in the sixth and eighth rounds, but Nicolson continued to counter effectively with straight lefts and rights. Nicolson closed out her commanding performance with sharp uppercuts and a three-punch combination in the 10th round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBC super-bantamweight title fight between Skye Nicolson and Miyo Yoshida

Unbeaten prospect Albina Moldazhanova knocked out former European champion Kirstie Bavington, subjecting her to heavy punishment before landing a right hook in the fourth round to finish it inside the distance. Moldazhanova has a 100 per cent knockout ratio after six pro fights.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 Delap serves up possible Kane solution

It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. Jonathan Wilson

2 Alysson gives Dalot the runaround

Amid the chaotic blur of proceedings at Old Trafford, there was one outstanding performance. Alysson had only one goal to his name in his Premier League career at Aston Villa, but he scored one and helped set up another two in the first 48 minutes against Manchester United. The 20-year-old winger, who has represented Brazil only at under-16 level, was signed from Grêmio for an initial £8.7m last January. His only goal in 18 previous appearances was against Nottingham Forest in September – it took less than a minute to open the scoring at United and less than four for his saved shot to rebound out to Nicolas Jackson for Villa’s second. United’s right-back, Diogo Dalot, was too slow to close Alysson down for his opener and did not have any complaints when his trip on the Brazilian conceded a penalty at the start of the second half. Dalot, often the face of United’s struggles, was booed off when substituted in the second half – Alysson was applauded off by the away end. Billy Munday

3 Gómez’s eye for the spectacular

Diego Gómez is the latest example of a slow-burning Brighton player given the chance and space to bed in before then flourishing. His current status is as an overnight sensation, though a taste for the spectacular and an eye for goal have been obvious since two goals against Leeds in November 2025. Gómez had signed from Inter Miami that January. The inside-right position from which he drilled his left-foot sidewinder to open the scoring against Brentford brings the best from his shooting prowess with both feet. His October halfway line strike against Crystal Palace came with his right foot. As with a number of Brighton’s purchases, Gómez can play in other positions, variously defensive midfielder, attacking midfielder, even on the wing. Within Fabian Hürzeler’s stringent tactical setup, he is asked to work hard for the ball. Such high pressing created the opportunity Charalampos Kostoulas should have done better with in the moments after the opening goal. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Pick that one out: Diego Gómez shows his potency again with a blistering strike against Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

4 Arsenal could do with creating chaos

There is nothing wrong with Arsenal’s habit of winning games by a single goal: Mikel Arteta’s side did it 15 times on their way to the title last season and the latest against Hull was their fourth this season. Yet despite being six points clear of Manchester City heading into the international break, Arteta will have some concerns about the lack of goals so far. With only 15 from their first 10 matches, Arsenal are on course to break Manchester United’s record of 67 for the fewest by a team being crowned champions in 1993 – the Premier League’s first season. They have also been struggling to score in the first half of games, having gone six matches in all competitions without doing so last month, and Arteta has called on his players to be more ruthless. “Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game,” he said. Ed Aarons

5 Brobbey’s masterclass torments Chelsea

All hail Brian Brobbey. It is fascinating that a player sometimes derided for his supposed lack of technical quality while at Ajax has developed into one of the Premier League’s most potent and difficult-to-play centre-forwards in little more than a year in England. His new contract, announced last Wednesday, is richly deserved. There is, as Régis Le Bris acknowledged after the win over Chelsea in which he bullied the visitors, no one quite like him. “Against a team that wants to press like that it’s so important to have a target man,” said the Sunderland manager, and Brobbey was that and then some. Much has been made of how Chelsea miss João Pedro but the Mackems are a different team with their flying Dutchman. Andy Brassell

6 Leeds find support for Calvert-Lewin

It was a tale of two benches at Elland Road. The big question hanging over Leeds is whether they have the support for Dominic Calvert-Lewin to make a concerted push for Europe this season; a question that went some way to being answered when the substitutes Harry Wilson and Noah Okafor combined for the latter to score the winner against Tottenham. In contrast, Roberto De Zerbi’s attacking options let him down in a game that felt there for the taking. Dominic Solanke struggled after replacing Mathys Tel, Omar Marmoush looked limited in the central striker role and their brightest performer was the 18-year-old Lucá Williams-Barnett, who, you would suspect, is now not far from a deserved start. Having won three straight games before their defeat in West Yorkshire, Spurs suddenly go into the international break with more questions than answers over their attacking credentials once again. Aaron Bower

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Noah Okafor and Harry Wilson proved their value as subs for Leeds against Tottenham. Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/Reuters

7 Iraola braced for nervy international break

Andoni Iraola had one wish as he signed off for the international window with the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace – that he does not lose any players to injury before Liverpool are back in action against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday week. The manager is scarred by the previous round of international fixtures: Dominik Szoboszlai, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak all picked up problems. The trio were missed as Liverpool lost to Manchester City in the first game back. Szoboszlai’s injury was the most concerning: he was only able to return as a substitute in the defeat against Arsenal on 1 November and Iraola said after the win at Palace tat the Hungary midfielder was not 100%, that a knee problem required management. “Let’s see if Dom can play with the national team or not,” Iraola said. “I know what I want! But I have to understand the national teams. Also I’m sure Dom will want to go. I’m not sure if it’s going to be fine.” David Hytner

8 Cherries and their ‘magician’ on a streak

Bournemouth are really getting to grips with the Thursday-Sunday grind in their first season in Europe. Marco Rose has been working hard to ensure his team are in the right shape to start Premier League games quickly after a Europa League assignment three days earlier. After Thursday’s trip to face Sparta Prague, Bournemouth were quick out of the traps at Ipswich on Sunday, taking the lead through Evanilson after five minutes. “Last week [against Leeds] I said we start slow and this week we start quite quick and score an early goal – I am a magician,” said the head coach, after their eighth consecutive win in all competitions. That equalled a club record set under Eddie Howe in League One. Evanilson is himself on a streak – he’s scored in five in a row in the league – and only Nicolas Jackson has scored as many in the top flight since the last international break. The Brazilian did not need Christian Walton’s helping hand with this goal. BM

9 Newcastle need more in attack

Newcastle delivered one of their more convincing performances of the season at Fulham, but one area remains a headache for Matthias Jaissle. Efforts to replace Alexander Isak in attack have not been good enough. Nick Woltemade was loaned to Juventus after an inconsistent debut season in England and there was not much encouragement to take from how Yoane Wissa and William Osula played at Craven Cottage. Wissa, who has struggled since his £55m move from Brentford last summer, has four goals in 41 appearances and did not put himself about enough before being taken off after 61 minutes, while Osula did not manage a touch in Fulham’s area and lost possession before Rodrigo Muniz’s late equaliser for the hosts. Jaissle needs more from his forwards on and off the ball. Otherwise Newcastle are going to need to find different players to lead their attack. Jacob Steinberg

View image in fullscreen Yoane Wissa endured another frustrating afternoon for Newcastle at Fulham. Photograph: John Walton/PA

10 What’s the punishment for hair-pulling?

The laws on hair-pulling were changed for this season after the red cards that were issued to Michael Keane, Lisandro Martínez and Dan Ballard in 2025-26. They are undoubtedly an improvement but, as James Tarkowski’s pull on Caleb Yirenkyi’s hair demonstrated in Everton’s comeback against Coventry, grey areas remain. Frank Lampard and David Moyes agreed the Everton captain should not have been sent off as there was no excessive force involved. But was it “a clear action without excessive force” that should have resulted in a yellow card for unsporting behaviour and a penalty to Coventry? Or “negligible, accidental or inadvertent contact” that is not usually considered an offence? Moyes offered up one solution – scrap the law altogether. “I think it is still ridiculous that is even categorised in the rules of the game,” the Everton manager said. “I can’t understand why they don’t fix this completely because I don’t see it as a good rule at all.” Andy Hunter

Sports.title: Crystal Palace poised to sack Pierre Sage and target Frank after Liverpool defeat
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging as the main candidate to succeed him.

The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats.

Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches.

He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford.

The former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche also has his backers at Palace and would be seen as a safe pair of hands given his vast experience in the Premier League. Vítor Pereira, another former Forest manager, could be an alternative.

Sage signed a three-year contract in south London after leaving Lens, where he won the Coupe de France and qualified for the Champions League in his final season. Palace have lost their two main central defenders this year, Marc Guéhi moving to Manchester City in January and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea in the summer. Two loan players – Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor – were signed as replacements. Palace did not land one of Sage’s top targets, Malick Fofana.
