Sports.title: Alycia Baumgardner Sweeps Elif Nur Turhan to Win IBF Title
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner took away Elif Nur Turhan’s unbeaten record and her IBF lightweight title on Sunday night, using a sharp jab and quick counters to win all 10 rounds on each judge’s card. All three scored it 100-90 for Baumgardner, who became a two-division world champion in her lightweight debut.

Turhan (14-1, 8 KOs) spent much of the early going trying to get close enough to throw her looping right hand. Baumgardner’s jab made her start those attacks from farther out than she wanted. When Turhan committed to the overhand anyway, Baumgardner (19-1, 7 KOs) could step clear and catch her before she was set to punch again. Turhan kept bringing the fight to her, but Baumgardner landed the cleaner shots while giving the champion few chances to follow up.

The pattern held through the middle rounds. Turhan stayed busy and found openings with hooks and uppercuts when she shortened her punches. Baumgardner took those shots and went back to the jab, making Turhan, 31, work her way inside again. Turhan’s best punches came once she was close enough to throw without reaching. Too often, she had to risk a wide shot just to get there.

Turhan landed clean uppercuts in the ninth and kept pressing in the tenth, still looking for a big shot after spending much of the night behind. Baumgardner, 32, kept her composure and continued to make Turhan miss and pay for coming forward. The three shutout cards gave Baumgardner every round, even with Turhan landing some of her best punches late.

The win gives Baumgardner a belt at 135 pounds after her undisputed run at 130 and puts a potential unification with Caroline Dubois in play. Turhan gave her an immediate test at the new weight. She kept coming for 30 minutes, landed cleanly when she got inside, and made Baumgardner keep working to regain her distance. Baumgardner did it often enough that none of the three judges found a round to give the defending champion.

The fight headlined Most Valuable Promotions at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas. It was contested over 10 three-minute rounds at the 135-pound limit.

Earlier on the card, Ramla Ali won the vacant IBF and WBO super bantamweight titles by split decision over Mikiah Kreps, and Skye Nicolson retained her WBC belt at the same weight by unanimous decision over Miyo Yoshida.

Sports.title: Skye Nicolson Outboxes Miyo Yoshida to Retain WBC Title
Sports.content:
Skye Nicolson kept Miyo Yoshida chasing for 10 rounds, using her longer reach and lead right hand to win a unanimous decision and retain her WBC super bantamweight title Sunday night at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

The judges scored it 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92 for Nicolson in her first defense as full champion at 122 pounds. Neither fighter went down on the ESPN card headlined by Elif Turhan and Alycia Baumgardner.

Less than a pound separated the fighters at the weigh-in, but Nicolson had about five inches of reach on Yoshida. That advantage showed each time Yoshida had to step in to throw. The challenger landed several rights in the opening round, but Nicolson answered with left hands and body shots. By the third, Nicolson (17-1, 3 KOs) was catching Yoshida with the lead right as she came forward.

Yoshida (19-6, 1 KO) had one of her better spells in the fourth, backing Nicolson up with a flurry. Nicolson countered with a right and tied her up before she could build on it. In the fifth, Nicolson went from circling away to pressing Yoshida, 38, toward the ropes, where she landed a right hook. Yoshida had to stay ready for Nicolson to come forward even as she tried to cut off the ring.

The Japanese challenger kept finding short rights in the clinches in the sixth and seventh and landed on the way in during the eighth. The trouble came whenever Nicolson got clear. Yoshida had to start her approach again, and Nicolson, 31, could get back to scoring with both hands from outside. Yoshida put combinations together in the ninth, but Nicolson caught her with a counter left and an uppercut. The champion worked quick uppercuts into her combinations in the tenth as Yoshida pursued her to the final bell.

Yoshida was trying to win a world title in a third weight class after holding belts at 115 and 118 pounds. She showed she could make Nicolson uncomfortable once she got close, particularly when she led with more than one punch. She spent too much of the fight trying to get back there.

For Nicolson, the result was her first successful defense since being elevated from interim to full champion in May. The former WBC featherweight champion had been due to face Yoshida in Britain in August before an injury delayed the bout. She made her MVP debut in Arlington and came away with the belt still in hand and a possible unification ahead.

Sports.title: Hearn Wants Shakur Stevenson. Who Can He Deliver?
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn wants to work with Shakur Stevenson after the unbeaten champion parted ways with Zuffa Boxing without ever entering the ring for the venture. Matchroom holds viable options at 135 and 140 pounds, yet the most lucrative fight on the board remains Gervonta Davis, which demands an agreement with Premier Boxing Champions.

“We’d love to work with him. He can work with anybody he wants,” Hearn said in an interview with by Fighthub. “He’s one of the best fighters in the world.”

Dalton Smith stands as the most accessible internal option if Stevenson remains at 140 pounds. Hearn handles Smith’s career directly, allowing Matchroom to stage a UK event and bank on strong arena attendance to cover fighter compensation. Andy Cruz represents another route at 135 pounds should Stevenson drop back down. Cruz brings elite technical skill, yet matching two defensive purists creates promotional hurdles regarding broad commercial appeal. Hearn cited neither boxer as a firm candidate.

William Zepeda highlights the strengths and limits of DAZN’s network ecosystem. The streaming service handled Stevenson’s 2025 meeting with the Golden Boy contender, proving cross-promotional business can function smoothly on that feed. Stevenson dominated that encounter by wide unanimous decision, blunting the public appetite for a second run.

Davis presents a much larger commercial target. The Baltimore native headlined on Prime Video via PBC against Lamont Roach, establishing where his primary broadcast loyalties sit. Staging Davis against Stevenson forces Hearn to iron out carriage rights and profit sharing with PBC. A third-party financial backer like Riyadh Season could cover enormous purse guarantees, yet distribution rights would remain a contested negotiation.

The contrast between Smith and Davis exposes modern boxing economics. Hearn can finalize terms with Smith quickly. Still, he has to determine whether live gate numbers and British ticket buyers justify Stevenson’s lofty minimum guarantee. Matchroom absorbs the deficit if the venue fails to sell out. Davis brings bona fide pay-per-view muscle, though Premier Boxing Champions holds broadcast control and will demand most of the revenue pie.

A multi-fight contract gives Stevenson guaranteed ring dates along with locked paydays. A bout-by-bout arrangement lets him hunt massive paydays with complete freedom, but leaves him open to long stretches of inactivity while rivals sort out their own schedules.Waiting months for a marquee rival leaves an elite boxer covering ongoing training costs without incoming revenue.

Hearn labeled Stevenson’s brief run with Zuffa an absolute catastrophe while taking aim at Dana White’s promotional output. The most effective recruiting tool Matchroom possesses is an actionable contract. Smith shows what Hearn can deliver in-house, while Davis proves whether he can overcome stubborn industry boundaries.

Hearn omitting Cruz speaks volumes about Matchroom’s true priorities. Promoting that matchup would be commercial suicide. Cruz versus Stevenson is a purist’s dream, but casual fans run from pure chess matches. Staging it requires massive guarantees for both men with virtually zero pay-per-view upside and a dismal gate outside of a niche venue. DAZN would essentially foot the bill for an expensive technical exhibition that drives no new subscriptions.

Beyond the financials, the matchmaking logic falls apart for Hearn. If he shells out heavy money to sign Stevenson, the objective is cashing in on blockbuster dates or building toward Gervonta Davis. Throwing Stevenson directly in with Cruz risks ruining the asset immediately. Stevenson could easily get outpointed or dragged into an unwatchable snoozer that completely kills his market value.

Even if Stevenson wins, beating Cruz does almost nothing to build his crossover profile. Casuals do not know Cruz, so Stevenson gains little public credit while taking maximum technical risk.

From Hearn’s seat, keeping those two far apart is self-preservation. You protect the newly acquired name with high-visibility, lower-risk domestic dates like Dalton Smith, or you swing for the fences with established commercial giants where the reward justifies the danger. Cruz offers all the poison with none of the prize.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu Defends His Right Hand Before Lara Fight
Sports.content:
Tim Tszyu rejected the notion that he was too cautious with his right hand against Errol Spence Jr. last July. For Tszyu, getting his hand raised put that debate to bed. Taking on WBA middleweight champion Erislandy Lara presents a far trickier tactical puzzle: how to release that signature power punch without walking directly into a counter straight left.

Tszyu insists he damaged Spence and felt entirely comfortable with the performance. Turning his attention to Lara, he pointed directly to the Cuban veteran’s deceptive lead hand, footwork reads, and sudden left hand deliveries.

“This fight is a game of inches. You really can’t make one mistake at that high level. It’s hard to go and throw 100 punches carelessly in a round because there’s 100 different opportunities that you can get caught,” Tszyu said to The Punch podcast.

Tszyu suggested he anticipates an aggressive Lara hunting for a stoppage, but the veteran can inflict equal devastation by simply giving up an inch of canvas. Southpaws of Lara’s caliber thrive on the classic half step pull counter. If Tszyu overextends with the right hand while searching for Lara’s chin, his momentum leaves his weight trapped over his front knee. That leaves him completely exposed to a sharp left counter while his feet remain stuck. A pawing, noncommittal jab from Lara often serves as bait, coaxing aggressive fighters into lunging from outside range.

Winning the lead foot battle will dictate Tszyu’s success. He cannot allow Lara to consistently step outside his front foot, which forces the orthodox right hand to travel at a wide angle while opening a clean lane down the center for Lara. Tszyu must establish his jab to the chest to measure range, mixing in level changes and double feints to freeze Lara’s back foot before unloading. Targeting the body early with heavy rights will also slow the veteran down and pull his elbows in, unlocking paths to the head.

Patience carries its own severe penalties against a master boxer. Spending entire rounds looking for an ideal opening allows Lara to steal minutes with a flickering jab and isolated straight shots. Tszyu settled for minimal right hands against Spence, but dealing with Lara on the Gold Coast demands far more offensive initiative.

Sports.title: James Toney’s Haney Knockout Pick Ignores Seven Years
Sports.content:
James Toney expects Devin Haney to knock out Liam Paro, but that forecast demands a style Haney abandoned long ago. At 27, Haney has collected world titles for seven consecutive years without a single stoppage victory. Transforming into a finisher against a gritty southpaw means embracing the precise physical exposure his entire system is engineered to avoid.

Toney’s endorsement carries weight after their recent work together in the gym. When asked about the matchup, the Hall of Famer did not mince words.

“You see power. He knock him out,” Toney said to Fighthype.

Gym mitts, however, tell only part of the story. Training equipment offers a compliant target where a puncher can generate torque with settled feet. Real competition forces a different arithmetic entirely. Ripping a leveraged right hand on the pads comes without the immediate threat of eating a live southpaw right hook over the top.

That reality shapes Haney’s actual punching mechanics. Sitting down on a shot requires planting the back foot and committing hip rotation, anchoring him in place for an extra beat. Mobility has always been Haney’s primary defensive insurance policy. Abandoning that fluid perimeter control to load up on heavier leather would compromise his balance, alter his recovery timing, and accelerate fatigue in the late rounds.

The footwork battle against Paro sharpens those stakes. Securing dominant outside position with the lead left foot creates an angle for Haney’s straight right. At the same time, stepping outside is never risk-free. If Haney overreaches to establish that angle or lingers to admire his work, Paro can easily pivot and fire a short counter left down the pipe. For Haney, a clean exit after throwing matters far more than maximum thud.

His 2023 performance against Regis Prograis proved that distinction clearly. Haney dropped the heavy-hitting southpaw with a laser straight right in round three. Instead of swarming to produce a finish, he collected the points, reset the perimeter, and coasted to a wide decision win. A knockdown proved his timing, but it did not change his operational instincts.

Stopping Paro demands sustained combinations. Scoring with a lead punch is simple enough; staying in range to deliver the second, third, and fourth punches is where the peril starts. Paro proved against Subriel Matias that he knows how to survive inside exchanges. He smothered Matias’s offense with smart lateral movement, timely clinches, and sharp counter bursts. If Matias could not break Paro’s defensive resolve on the ropes, Haney will hardly do it with one-off punches.

Toney spent his career thriving in the pocket, rolling with shots on the inside, and returning venomous fire at close range. It makes sense that he sees the game through that aggressive lens. Haney, by contrast, treats close-range trades as an avoidable liability.

Haney might possess sufficient force to stun opponents, but producing an actual stoppage requires living in the pocket. Until Haney shows a genuine appetite for sustained infighting, Toney’s knockout prediction remains completely detached from the fighter Haney chooses to be.

Sports.title: Canelo Payday Would Reward Sheeraz’s Janibek Duck
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz might pull off the slickest business move in boxing by tossing his WBO belt in the trash. Dan Canobbio called out the absurdity of the whole setup: Sheeraz walks away from a dangerous night against Janibek Alimkhanuly, and his reward could be the richest payday in the sport against Canelo Alvarez.

Canobbio revealed the reason behind the split. It was never about old testing drama with Janibek. It came down to cash, exposing the massive gap between heavily subsidized guarantees and what the open market actually pays for a real fight.

“He didn’t like the money. He went to purse bid and he saw his true value out there, not the inflated purses that he’s been getting from Turki,” Canobbio said to Ariel Helwani. “I’m not fighting Janibek, who’s very good, for what he considers low money. So he vacates the belt.”

The purse bid told the whole story. Janibek is a stylistic nightmare with zero commercial juice, and nobody stepped up with silly money to save Sheeraz from the risk.

From a pure survival standpoint, Sheeraz made the smart business play. Getting beaten by Janibek kills his career progress and ends his Canelo lottery ticket before he ever touches the check. Getting beaten by Canelo still pays him millions and puts him on the biggest stage in the game. Both bouts bring real danger, but only one leaves him set for life.

The WBO belt stopped being an asset and turned into a snare. Titles are supposed to give a fighter leverage. The moment this one forced a low-dollar dogfight, Sheeraz dumped it to keep the fast lane to Canelo open.

Canelo certainly does not care about Sheeraz’s vacated strap. Sheeraz brings the height, reach, and punching power to cut a flashy promo video, while Canelo brings the buying public. When the backers want the pairing, the sanctioning bodies lose all their juice the second the fighter surrenders the belt.

The ugly part is what this does to the sport. Surrendering a title is supposed to carry a penalty. Instead, Sheeraz gets an upgrade. Every contender watching gets the exact same signal: taking on a terrifying mandatory is for suckers when ducking the assignment lets you jump straight to the cash cow.

Canobbio still likes the matchup because Sheeraz has size and punch, but that angle needs a cold reality check. Height has never bothered Canelo. Callum Smith brought the exact same size, only to spend twelve rounds getting his arms tenderized and his body battered along the ropes.

Towering over Canelo means nothing if you cannot stop him from walking through the front door. Destroying Edgar Berlanga did not prove Sheeraz can control distance against an elite counterpuncher, and taking the bigger payday certainly does not mean he picked an easy night.

This move does Canelo no favors either. For a superstar who built his reputation chasing undisputed status, taking on a fighter who just ditched his hardware looks cheap, especially with active champions like Osleys Iglesias sitting right there.

The fight will sell, but putting it together next turns the sport on its head. It tells every fighter in the division that real tests are optional as long as the promoters want you in the main event anyway.

Sports.title: Tony Yoka’s Five-Win Rebuild Has Taken Him Nowhere
Sports.content:
Tony Yoka has put together five consecutive wins, yet his heavyweight rebuild is chewing through critical years without showing that he has resolved the flaws exposed in his three career defeats. Saturday’s 59-55 points win over Kostiantyn Dovbyshchenko in Manchester kept the streak alive, but against opposition well below the standard required of a serious contender.

Six rounds against a durable Ukrainian journeyman on the Buatsi–Hutchinson undercard told us nothing new about the 2016 Olympic gold medalist Yoka. Over the past three years, the former Olympic champion has merely padded out his record while keeping his true ceiling carefully hidden from view.

Yoka controlled the range behind his jab and timed the Ukrainian with rear-hand uppercuts on the way in. What he failed to do was capitalize on that control. His corner repeatedly called for more spite, but Yoka settled for single shots instead of putting together sustained flurries.

Dovbyshchenko has never been stopped, so a decision win is not an embarrassment on paper. The red flag was Yoka’s refusal to turn up the heat on a fighter offering minimal return fire. That hesitation points to an uncomfortable reality: this run has not restored his confidence, it has simply matched him with opposition he can outpoint without evolving.

Yoka still left the ring with a bloody nose and a cut above his eye. Those marks are not catastrophic, but they highlight the danger of letting an aggressive target march forward unpunished. Against punchers with real stopping power, landing early leads means nothing if he cannot survive the inside exchanges that follow.

Scrapped bouts with Lawrence Okolie and Murat Gassiev account for the layoff, and taking Saturday’s contest on a few hours’ notice showed professionalism. Neither factor alters the urgency of his situation.

At 34, padding the record with routine six-round assignments brings zero value. A sink-or-swim test against someone like Frazer Clarke would finally answer whether Yoka can stand firm when an opponent walks straight through his jab.

Queensberry can keep finding him rounds. Finding a win that restores his credibility is the real challenge, and after five tune-ups, that test is long overdue.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Riding Fast Track To The Exit Door At Zuffa
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is acting like he just hit the jackpot with Zuffa, but scraping past Shane Mosley Jr. should bring him right back down to earth. At 31, Bentley does not have a massive fan base to protect him when things go wrong. If he thinks a busy media schedule guarantees loyalty, he is in for a rude awakening.

Bentley bragged that he received more publicity in two weeks with Zuffa than during his entire run with Queensberry. That is basic promotional launch hype, not a lifetime commitment. Every promoter rolls out the red carpet for a fresh signing. The real test is what happens to that promotional push the minute you take an L.

“I just felt undervalued there. Over here, I feel really valued. I feel like they want to push me and move me forward,” Bentley said after the fight. “I’ve had more press in the last two weeks than I’ve had my whole career at Queensberry. And that’s not a dig at no one. They have their priorities, and that’s who they want to move, and I didn’t think I was a priority over there. So I went where I was appreciated, and I feel appreciated here.”

Most of that early noise came from the controversy of Bentley ditching his promoter and getting stripped of his WBO belt. It gave writers an easy angle before he even laced up gloves. Once that headline gets stale, hype will not carry him.

Frank Warren gave Bentley plenty of patience. Bentley took losses against Felix Cash, Janibek Alimkhanuly, and Nathan Heaney. Queensberry did not toss him in the trash. They kept finding him dates, kept him active, and rebuilt him.

After the Heaney loss, Bentley ran through Danny Dignum, Derrick Osaze, Brad Pauls, and Endry Saavedra. That was a tidy domestic recovery run that fixed his ranking without matching him against the division’s monsters. Bentley might have wanted more spotlight, but Warren kept his career alive.

The mandatory defense against Yoenli Hernandez was supposed to prove whether Bentley had actually improved. Instead of facing the dangerous Cuban, Bentley opted for Mosley, lost his belt, and threw away his best bargaining chip. Now he is calling out Carlos Adames and Aaron McKenna with empty hands. Without a belt, you do not dictate terms to anybody.

Saturday night hardly helped his stock. Bentley dropped Mosley in the second round, got greedy looking for a quick knockout, and let Mosley drag him into deep water. Bentley admitted he ignored his corner because he thought the stoppage was right there.

Bentley claimed he did not gas out, which actually makes it worse. It means once Mosley shook off the knockdown and turned up the heat, Bentley simply lacked the ring generalship to stay in control. That kind of tactical drift gets you knocked out against punchers like Adames or Janibek.

A cash cow can afford an ugly night because ticket sales keep promoters hooked. Bentley does not have that luxury.

Zuffa comes from the UFC mindset where rosters get trimmed fast. If Bentley loses, they are far more likely to cut him loose than spend two years quietly rebuilding him at small domestic venues. Warren gave Bentley second and third chances. Bentley has yet to find out whether Zuffa has any interest in picking up the pieces when he gets beat.

For academics, it is publish or perish; under the Zuffa banner, it is produce or hit the pavement.

Bentley is walking around grinning about media scrums and spotlight time, completely blind to the fact that every camera pointed at him right now is a record entry. Dana White and company do not run a charity. The UFC promotional machine operates on an aggressive ROI formula: you either deliver explosive highlight-reel finishes that generate viral clips, or you pack the house with rabid, ticket-buying fans.

Bentley brings neither to the table. He is not a powerful one-punch artist who guarantees fireworks, and he certainly does not move tickets in the United States.

When you fight under a traditional boxing boss like Frank Warren, you can afford an ugly night or a bad loss because the promotional structure includes patience, domestic dates, and long rebuilding cycles. In the Zuffa ecosystem, fighters are viewed as content inventory. The second an import with zero domestic drawing power fails to deliver explosive content or drops a decision, there’s little reason to keep them on board.

Bentley was brought in to provide fresh content, look slick, and give their brand a boost. Struggling to pull away from an ordinary fighter like Shane Mosley Jr. was the absolute worst way to introduce himself. He thinks he landed a promotion that genuinely values him as an athlete, but in reality, he signed up for a high-turnover business that will hand him his pink slip the very second he stops producing.

Ghana News.title: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
Ghana News.content:
A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say.

The 24-year-old, who officials said was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies", was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

Krakow police said the suspected gunman died early on Monday morning.

After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man but did not confirm his name.

In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.

Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack.

Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.

On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and 21-year-old sister.

Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.

Speaking on Sunday, one of the two surgeons who treated victims on the street after the attack said his colleague "undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer.

The two surgeons, who were eating near the Main Market Square when the gunman opened fire, rushed to the scene to treat both the attacker and the two injured police officers.

Professor Michal Pędziwiatr told the BBC: "We saw the shooting attack. And what a surgeon can do in a situation like this?... We decided to help the victims as soon as possible."

"We rushed into the area where the shooting was and started our rescue, because there were no ambulances available, there were no professionals around."

Pędziwiatr said his colleague, who has been named by local media as Dr Mateusz Wierdak, used his hand to stem the bleeding from the most severely injured policeman, allowing time for an ambulance to arrive.

On Sunday it was reported that both injured officers had emerged from comas.

Witnesses who were near the Main Market Square have described their panic and confusion as the attack unfolded.

Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives".

She said they "just kept sprinting" until they found a hotel to shelter inside.

Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover".

"I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said.

In the wake of the shooting, Poland declared the country would enter two days of national mourning.

After travelling to Krakow, Tusk said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism...that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Kraków".

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added.

Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted.

Ghana News.title: AFCON 2027Q: ‘Black Stars will go into Somalia games to win’ – Henry Asante Twum
Ghana News.content:
The Communications Director of the Ghana Football Association (GFA) Henry Asante Twum remains optimistic ahead of the doubleheader clash against Somalia in the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), stating that the Black Stars will face their opponents with a positive mindset.

Ghana suffered a 2-0 defeat to Cote d'Ivoire in Bouake, followed by a humiliating 4-2 loss to Gambia at home.

Black Stars sit at the bottom of Group C with no points and must win on matchdays three and four to keep their hopes of returning to AFCON alive.

Despite missing out on the previous AFCON edition in Morocco, Asante Twum told Asempa FM that he still believes the Black Stars can win.

"The Black Stars will go into the Somalia games with a positive mindset to win," he said.

"It has been a difficult start for the team, but the GFA is doing everything possible to ensure the team returns to winning ways."

Ghana will host Somalia on Thursday, November 12, at the Essipong Sports Stadium, followed by a return fixture on Monday, November 16.

After the departure of former coach Carlos Queiroz, Kim Lars Björkegren, who also doubles as Black Queens' head coach, will serve as the team's interim boss for the games.

Björkegren is expected to announce Ghana's final squad for the doubleheader on Monday, November 9.

Ghana News.title: Traffitech: Fewer motorists caught speeding in latest traffic monitoring exercise – TopTech Ghana
Ghana News.content:
A transport consultant at TopTech Ghana, Cecil Ebow Garbrah, says more drivers are complying with speed limits after increased public awareness and road safety education.

He cited findings from two separate traffic monitoring exercises his team conducted, which showed a significant improvement in the number of motorists observing the prescribed speed limits.

Speaking on Joy FM's Super Morning Show on Monday, November 9, during a discussion on Traffitech, Mr Garbrah said a study conducted on August 25 found that the majority of motorists monitored were driving above the speed limit.

He explained that his team counted about 380 vehicles between 8:00 am and midday on that day, with 342 exceeding the permitted speed of 90 kilometres per hour.

However, a subsequent exercise at the same location on Saturday, November 7, showed a marked improvement.

According to him, the team recorded 612 vehicles during the same four-hour period, of which 546 were travelling within the prescribed speed limit.

"Now, on November 7, just this Saturday, my team were at the same place and then we, between 8 and 12, counted about 612 vehicles. 546 were complying with the speed limit," he said.

Mr Garbrah interpreted the findings as evidence that motorists were becoming more conscious of speed limits, although he stressed the need for continued public education.

"Which means that Ghanaians are aware. We need more education, but Ghanaians are aware of speed limits," he added.

Ghana News.title: JUSAG strike: Over 2,000 arrested persons unable to access courts for bail – CLRL
Ghana News.content:
The Centre for Legitimacy and Rule of Law (CLRL) has raised concerns over the continued suspension of court proceedings following the strike by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG), estimating that more than 2,000 people arrested since the industrial action began have been unable to obtain judicial decisions on their bail or remand status.

The Centre says the situation threatens the constitutional rights of arrested persons, particularly those who remain in police custody or have been remanded without the opportunity to return to court on their scheduled dates.

In a statement signed by its Head of Legal, Richard Nii Amarh, CLR, on Monday, November 9, he said the strike, which began on Monday, November 2, has resulted in the suspension of sittings in all courts except the Supreme Court.

It warned that the disruption is compounding an already overburdened justice system characterised by prolonged delays and frequent adjournments.

“Our research desk has estimated that more than two thousand (2,000) people have been arrested by the Ghana Police Service since the declaration of this industrial strike. Consequently, these individuals have been denied the opportunity for a judicial pronouncement on their bail or remand status,” the statement said.

The Centre expressed particular concern about accused persons who were already on remand and had been given specific dates to reappear in court before the strike disrupted proceedings.

It said their inability to return to court has left them facing uncertainty over their continued detention, with limited opportunities to seek their release.

CLRL argued that the situation raises serious questions about Ghana's commitment to the rule of law, especially the constitutional protection requiring arrested or detained persons to be brought before a court within 48 hours.

“While our Constitution mandates that a person arrested or detained be brought before a court within 48 hours, the JUSAG strike has rendered this fundamental right a far-to-reach luxury,” it stated.

The Centre has consequently called on President John Dramani Mahama, the Ministers for Finance, Justice, and Employment and Labour Relations to urgently intervene to resolve the dispute and restore normal court operations.

It said the government must treat the industrial action as a matter of urgency, given its implications for the administration of justice and the liberty of persons caught up in the disruption.

CLRL proposes police bail and special courts for bail applications

As an immediate intervention, the Centre urged the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) to direct investigators to grant police enquiry bail to suspects involved in minor offences.

It believes the measure would help reduce congestion in police cells and prevent people accused of less serious offences from remaining in custody solely because court proceedings have been suspended.

“We are further urging the Inspector General of Police to issue a directive to all investigators to grant bail in all minor offences that have come before their police stations in order to decongest the already congested cells,” the statement said.

CLRL has also appealed to the Chief Justice to establish specialised courts to deal exclusively with bail applications while the strike continues.

Under its proposal, High Court judges would be assisted by Circuit or District Court judges acting as clerks or recorders to facilitate hearings on applications for bail.

The Centre says this arrangement would provide an alternative avenue for accused persons to exercise their right to seek bail despite the disruption to regular court proceedings.

It stressed that the ongoing industrial action should not leave people in detention without access to judicial consideration of their liberty.

Centre calls for comprehensive Bail Act

Beyond the immediate interventions, CLRL is urging Parliament to consider enacting a comprehensive Bail Act to strengthen Ghana's existing legal framework.

It noted that the country's bail regime is currently regulated by the Criminal Procedure Act, 1960 (Act 30), with much of its practical application shaped by judicial decisions and court practices over the years.

According to the Centre, a dedicated Bail Act would provide a more comprehensive framework for bail administration, including provisions to address exceptional circumstances such as disruptions to court operations.

“Finally, we call on the Parliament of Ghana to consider a Bail Act that will be thorough enough to cover situations such as this,” the statement added.

CLRL maintained that urgent action by the relevant state institutions is necessary to protect the rights of arrested and remanded persons while efforts continue to resolve the disagreement between JUSAG and the government.

Ghana News.title: Speed camera warning signs to be installed on major roads next week – ACP Obeng
Ghana News.content:
The Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service is preparing to install standardised speed camera warning signs on major roads across the country as part of efforts to improve compliance with speed limits under the Traffitech initiative.

The signs, which are currently undergoing production, will alert motorists to locations where speed cameras and video monitoring systems are deployed.

The Director of Education and Training at the MTTD, ACP Alexander Obeng, said the move was intended to bring the country's road signage in line with international best practices and improve public awareness of speed enforcement activities.

ACP Obeng said this on Joy FM's Super Morning Show (SMS) on Monday, November 9, during a discussion on Traffitech. He said the decision followed collaboration between the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) and road engineers to develop an approved standard sign for speed camera locations.

ACP Obeng explained that Ghana's existing road traffic regulations did not originally provide for a specific speed camera warning sign.

He referred to the Fourth Schedule of the road traffic regulations, which contains provisions on road markings and traffic signs adopted under the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals.

He specifically cited Regulation 40(8), explaining that the schedule did not include a designated sign for speed cameras.

"At the back, it is a schedule. In it, there is no speed camera sign. It was not embedded," he said.

However, he disclosed that the police, working with road engineers, had now developed a standardised sign to address the gap.

"Because of the proactiveness of the Inspector-General of Police, in collaboration with the road engineer, in matters of this that has been executed, we now have a standard road sign for camera," he said.

ACP Obeng said production of the new signs was ongoing, while surveys were also being conducted to identify suitable locations for their installation.

He indicated that the signs were expected to be rolled out in the coming days, particularly on major roads where speed enforcement and monitoring were considered necessary.

"Production is ongoing. Surveys are ongoing. So, in the coming days, you will see speed camera signs deployed on our major roads in Ghana," he said.

He also presented an image of the proposed sign during the interview, explaining that it was still being produced and had not yet been installed on the roads.

The sign carries the messages '24-hour video monitoring' and 'Speed kills, kill it now', warning motorists that their driving behaviour is being monitored and reminding them of the dangers of excessive speed.

According to ACP Obeng, the signs will be installed at locations based on the outcome of the ongoing surveys and in accordance with accepted road safety practices.

"These signs will be deployed at locations where they are desired, consistent with best practice," he said.

Ghana News.content:
Black Stars midfielder Daniel-Kofi Kyereh says he is excited about his return to the national team after a long absence due to an injury.

Kofi Kyereh was out for almost three years after suffering a third career anterior cruciate ligament injury, which kept him out of action for an extended period.

The VfL Osnabrück midfielder is in life for a return to the Black Stars team for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers after being spotted at the Accra International Airport on Sunday evening.

The 30-year-old revealed his readiness to get going again with the national team after a long time out.

"It's been a long time. I am happy to be back, and I can't wait to see them all. I am ready to play," he told the media in a short interaction at the airport.

Kyereh has made a good start to life in the 2. Bundesliga this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist in nine games.

Black Stars forward Felix Afena-Gyan believes there is still an opportunity for the team to get their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers back on track despite their poor start.

The Black Stars lost their opening two games of the qualifiers against Cote d'Ivoire and Gambia in the extended September international break.

Afena-Gyan, who is expected to be part of the squad for the games, believes it will be a mistake to rule Ghana out of the tournament after just two games.

Afena-Gyan was on target in the 4-2 defeat to Gambia in the last international break.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: At least one person killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight
World.content:
Russia’s second-largest oil refinery was set on fire by drones, while Russian strikes targeted Ukrainian energy sites.

Share At least one person killed as Russia and Ukraine trade strikes overnight on social media

Overnight strikes between Russia and Ukraine have killed at least one person and damaged a Russian oil refinery.

The ⁠⁠Kirishi refinery in the ⁠⁠Leningrad region was set on fire following a Ukrainian ‌‌drone attack, Leningrad Regional Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said on Monday in a post on Telegram.

One woman was killed by falling drone debris, Drozdenko said.

Also on Monday, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that his country had agreed to establish a new mechanism to allow European Union funds to be deployed more quickly in response to Russian attacks against Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

The Kirishi refinery is Russia’s ⁠⁠second-largest, and the Leningrad region is a major hub ‌‌for the country’s oil and grain exports via the Baltic Sea.

Leningrad’s governor also said air defence forces had downed 113 Ukrainian drones, and that an apartment in Kirishi ⁠⁠had been damaged in the ⁠⁠same overnight attack on the region.

Russian forces struck three ⁠⁠power substations across ⁠⁠Ukraine overnight on Monday and also hit ‌‌a cargo ship in the Black Sea that Moscow ⁠⁠said was providing ⁠⁠arms to Ukrainian forces, Russian state ⁠⁠news agencies ⁠⁠reported.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify those claims.

Russia has kept up regular attacks on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure, including energy sites across the country.

“Right now, many of our cities and communities are facing a very difficult situation with power, water, and heating supplies due to Russian strikes,” Ukraine’s president said in a post on X on Monday.



Zelenskyy said that he had agreed with Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, to “activate a special emergency mechanism” that would allow European funding “for what is needed most”.

“Our teams are already working on this,” Zelenskyy added.

The Kyiv, Dnipro, Sumy, and Donetsk regions, as well as Kherson, are facing the most acute energy crisis, the Ukrainian president said.

World.title: Iran’s authorities harden domestic security controls amid US strike threats
World.content:
Iran is cracking down on perceived security threats from alleged spies to crowds of youngsters.

Tehran, Iran – Iran’s domestic security apparatus is on high alert and hardening its approach in dealing with issues that authorities perceive to be jeopardising their control of the country during the war with the United States.

Iranian authorities have issued warnings to the public about tough sentences if they protest against the government and are tightening their control in public spaces after months of loosened restrictions on how people dress.

In short, the Iranian authorities appear to be trying to project an image that they will not yield on the principles of the Islamic Republic after eight months of war and amid the threat of a new, wider, more intense wave of US attacks.

Mahjoob Zweiri, director of the Gulf Studies Center at Qatar University, said the authorities have also been able to publicly mobilise supporters dedicated to the continuity of the government in Tehran amid these tensions.

“They include not only IRGC but also some civilians, and this is likely to continue until the war finishes,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), a military entity established to safeguard the principles of the 1979 Islamic revolution.

Heavy punishments for dissent

Iranian authorities routinely deploy harsh punishments to deter any form of dissent. The war, which began on October 28 with US and Israeli strikes on Iranian leaders, has only accelerated this process.

On Sunday, the judiciary said three young men arrested during nationwide protests in January were executed for allegedly attacking government offices and damaging public property near Tehran to benefit the US and Israel.



The authorities consider the antigovernment protests a “coup” attempt by “terrorists” affiliated with the US and Israel. But an independent United Nations fact-finding mission found the authorities had committed crimes against humanity during a violent crackdown on protesters that human rights groups said killed thousands of people, mostly on the nights of January 8 and 9.

Foreign-based rights organisations said many political cases that result in executions are marred by allegations of torture, forced confessions and other violations of due process.

This year, Iran’s government has executed at least 79 political or religious prisoners, including 40 people arrested during the January protests, according to the Norway-based Hengaw Organization for Human Rights. Some were executed after espionage convictions.

“Iran is a country at war with the world’s lone superpower, whose strategy toward Tehran remains unclear, and with Israel, whose government pursues a declared policy of overthrowing the regime in Tehran, whether through economic and military warfare or by partitioning Iran through a US- and Israeli-backed civil war,” political scientist Ali Alfoneh said.

“Taking these circumstances into consideration, the authorities of the Islamic Republic are no more repressive than any other regime facing similar threats.”

In some cases, authorities have loosened their enforcement of laws on the mandatory headscarf, the consumption of alcohol, the use of narcotics and other social issues in what Alfoneh said was in part to keep people busy with activities that might distract them from political activism.

“Repression appears to be reserved for matters of political freedom and for antiregime uprisings,” Alfoneh said.

Contrasting scenes on the streets

There are signs that authorities are now cracking down on what they perceive to be public opposition to the principles of Iran’s theocracy as the war continues.

In Tehran on October 30, hundreds of mostly Gen Z Iranians celebrated Halloween by wearing makeup or costumes and gathering in cafes on artsy Iranshahr Street.

Within hours, motorcyclists and plainclothes security personnel arrived to disperse the crowds and close down cafes. Assaults and detentions were reported. People enjoying the evening in nearby Artists Park were reportedly ordered away.

The authorities did not officially comment on the incident but have since set up pro-government stations and booths on the same street, where supporters chant “revolutionary” slogans in praise of the government and wave flags.



Pro-government demonstrators have blocked city squares and streets in Tehran since the war began in perceived messages of defiance to domestic and external opponents.

As part of the “self-sacrifice” Janfada campaign, some of them receive gun training and other support at these locations to serve as part of the Basij, a domestic IRGC paramilitary force, which has been used to crack down on antigovernment protests.

Even before Halloween, police criticised gatherings on Iranshahr, Sanai and other streets in Tehran that have become popular gathering spots for young Iranians looking for space to express themselves amid deteriorating living conditions resulting from the war, an economic crisis and domestic mismanagement.

“Those streets have unfortunately turned into a place where people cruise and walk around,” Tehran traffic police chief Teymour Hosseini said last month. He also hinted that the gatherings of young people were the reason cafes and businesses have been shut down by police in recent months.

The government also continues to impose a dress code, especially for women, since shortly after the 1979 revolution. But since the nationwide Mahsa Amini protests of 2022-2023, women have increasingly ditched their headscarves in public in Tehran and other cities in defiance of the law.

Hossein Shariatmadari, a hardline media figure, wrote in an article that loose hijabs were “one of the levers used by the enemy in the coming war” and must be taken seriously.

“The enemy has been defeated in military confrontation with Islamic Iran and has now shifted a considerable part of its abilities towards war in economic and cultural areas, particularly through expanding loose hijab,” he said.

War or negotiations for the future

State crackdowns have also attracted some limited attention in local media although for different reasons.

“A tense night in Iranshahr”, the reformist Shargh newspaper wrote about the operation on the eve of Halloween, urging policymakers to study what people want and provide attractive cultural opportunities. The Rouydad24 news website questioned the usefulness of treating the cultural preferences of young people as security problems.

The ultraconservative Keyhan newspaper wrote that Halloween celebrations were evidence of “cultural alienation” that was weakening knowledge of ancient traditions like Nowruz, the Persian New Year.

But Iranian authorities over the years have politicised domestic traditions too, namely by restricting and shooting at Chaharshanbe Suri fire festival celebrations during the protests.

Qatar University’s Zweiri said whether Iran and the US manage to end the war through a negotiated resolution or engage in a more devastating conflict would play a role in determining if more nationwide protests take place in Iran.

Some Iranians feel that any kind of protest currently could be interpreted as allying with foreign powers.



“The second level of reality is the identity of being Iranian, which means no Iranian wants to be affiliated to an enemy that attacks and destroys the country,” Zweiri said.

“Whether there is a deal or more war in the future will determine how Iran will be developing economically and politically and socially.”

World.title: The DNA that Unmasked a Killer | True Crime Reports
World.content:
For 21 years, Leslie Preer’s murder went unsolved. Then new DNA tech led police to a suspect thousands of miles away.

Leslie Preer’s murder went unsolved for 21 years. Her husband was the longtime suspect, but the case went cold. Then, new DNA technology pointed detectives to someone else entirely – a suspect thousands of miles away. Identifying him was one thing. Catching him meant setting a trap.
