World.title: Qatar PM to meet Trump: What’s the latest on US-Iran negotiations?
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump is set to hold talks with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani behind closed doors at the White House on Monday, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to bridge differences over Iran’s nuclear programme and the terms for ending the conflict.

An unnamed US official told the Reuters news agency that Vice President JD Vance is also scheduled to hold talks with Sheikh Mohammed, who also serves as foreign minister and has been known to act as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran.

Iran has stepped up diplomatic efforts amid suggestions by Trump that the US could resume full-scale strikes on Iran.

Here is a look at where diplomatic efforts stand before the meeting:

What is Iran’s latest position?

Iran offered the US a new nuclear and peace proposal via Qatari mediators on Thursday, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran’s seven demands. The US is examining the proposal.

Iran has been unwilling to hold negotiations over its atomic activities with the Trump administration until the latter agrees to several core conditions that Tehran has been demanding be part of any ceasefire agreement.

Tehran has long maintained that its nuclear programme is peaceful. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency, Iran has 440.9kg (972 pounds) of uranium that is enriched up to 60 percent purity, a short, technical step from weapons-grade levels of 90 percent.

Iran’s enrichment boost came after Trump withdrew from the nuclear deal in 2018. Signed under President Barack Obama, the deal had capped enrichment at below 3.67 percent.



Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday warned that Tehran will “rain down hell” if the US resumes attacks.

Speaking to Al Jazeera last month, Araghchi said Tehran’s two-day proposal was developed with Qatari mediators and based on the seven-day plan Iran announced at the UN General Assembly in September.

“On day one, the US implements a set of measures. On day two, the Strait of Hormuz will reopen, and navigation will be restored to what it used to be,” he said.

Tehran’s demands include lifting the sanctions Washington imposed on Iran after the collapse of a memorandum of understanding, signed in Islamabad, Pakistan, in June, reducing the US military presence in the region, reinstating the oil waivers granted in June as part of the MoU and releasing frozen Iranian funds, including those held in Qatar.

Tehran also requested that the new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz, a global oil chokepoint, worked out by Iran and Oman be formally recognised and that all other routes be closed. Finally, it demanded ending the war on all fronts, including Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Araghchi held talks with 12 regional counterparts over 48 hours last week, calling for a regional security arrangement free from the involvement of extra-regional powers. Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, warned Trump on Saturday against renewed attacks, saying: “Start war and you will face a devastating response.”

What have Trump, Rubio said?

Trump on Sunday warned that Washington had identified additional targets in Iran should military action resume, but said it was “highly unlikely” to ‌launch new strikes if negotiations yielded a strong agreement.

Sheikh Mohammed said mediation efforts continue and that the US has intentions and willingness to “take steps towards finding a solution”, after Trump confirmed on Friday that the White House was talking to Iranian representatives and that the team had “made a lot of progress with Iran”.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said negotiations with Iran had not made progress. He told reporters in Florida on Sunday that while the war was unpopular, Trump “identified a very real threat” in Iran and had worked to stop it from pursuing a nuclear weapon.

Rubio added that although the US president prefers a diplomatic solution, Iranian demands are “not just unacceptable, but in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic”.

“I wouldn’t say we’re at the verge of a breakthrough,” he added.

Where is the war headed?

US media reported that Trump was being pressed by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Central Command (CENTCOM) commander Brad Cooper to resume attacks against Iran.



Axios quoted a US official as saying CENTCOM was preparing for the resumption of major military operations in Iran, and that it was just waiting for orders from Washington.

On Thursday, Trump told reporters the US may have to “destroy” the rest of Iran, adding that people will “know soon enough” if he acts.

Trump warned that US forces have three aircraft carriers stationed in the region “fully locked and loaded”, ready to continue strikes if need be. He said the US identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges, that it would strike if military action resumes.

The US military, meanwhile, has carried out limited strikes on Iran, including against its air defences, at least twice over the past week. It also fired on a commercial ship and disabled it on Saturday, which the US said was trying to breach its naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Rubio said Washington would take “defensive” actions if needed. “If there’s a clear and present threat to shipping or to our forces in the region, we have a right to defend ourselves,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Aerospace Force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Sunday made threats that echoed those of the Iranian foreign minister and said weapons have been “secured for years to come”.

IRGC Brigadier-General Ali Belali said in a statement on Telegram that “the armed forces are at the ready, and if the enemy makes a mistake, Iran’s response will be devastating and severe.”

World.title: Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ for voters
World.content:
Trump concedes some voters were unhappy with his administration’s controversial deportation drive.

Share Trump says his immigration policy ‘too tough’ for voters on social media

United States President Donald Trump has said his immigration policy may have been too extreme for voters, conceding that his deportation policy had damaged his Republican Party’s performance in the last week’s midterm elections.

During his first television interview since his party lost control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate last week, Trump said some voters were unhappy with his administration’s controversial deportation drive, which led to widespread protests.

“I think it might be too tough,” he told CBS’s 60 Minutes programme, which aired on Sunday.

He said he may be able to work with the new Democratic-controlled Congress on some kind of immigration agreement.

“The deal would be we would work something out,” he said, adding, “I think that’s something that’s actually doable.”

The interview was aired after he appointed Stephen Miller, the chief architect of his hardline immigration policy, to replace Susie Wiles as his White House chief of staff, prompting questions about the direction of his immigration policy.

In a post on X, Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said, “Trump says his immigration crackdown went too far”, adding, “Apparently, his solution was to put the man responsible for it in charge of the White House. That’s not a course correction. That’s a promotion.”

Trump had promised an immigration crackdown during his campaign to return to office, blaming undocumented migrant “killers” and “drug dealers” for soaring crime.

Extensive operations to detain and deport immigrants were launched in multiple US cities, causing arrests to soar.



Two US citizens – Renee Good and Alex Pretti – were killed by federal officers during protests against the operations.

Democrats have said oversight of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Department of Homeland Security is a priority for the new Congress.

During his interview, Trump said a moderate immigration deal would still deport criminals, but allow “good people” who had lived and worked in the country “paying taxes” to stay.

World.title: US top Democrat backs impeachment of Pete Hegseth
World.content:
NewsFeed US top Democrat backs impeachment of Pete Hegseth

US top Democrat Hakeem Jefferies says it’s a ‘hard yes’ on supporting efforts to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, in a vote that could be called this week. Jeffries is poised to become Speaker of the Democrat-controlled House of Representatives.

World.title: Trump ‘only kidding’ about Dana White press secretary role
World.content:
NewsFeed Trump ‘only kidding’ about Dana White press secretary role

US President Donald Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about appointing UFC CEO Dana White as the White House press secretary, but added White was ‘capable’ and liked the idea. The two are expected to meet on Monday.

World.title: MotoGP: Bezzecchi denies Marquez world title as motorsport returns to Qatar
World.content:
Marc Marquez has been made to wait another two weeks to win his eighth MotoGP title after finishing behind Marco Bezzecchi at the Qatar Grand Prix in Lusail as motorsport returned to the country after a delay due to the United States-Israel war on Iran.

Ducati’s Marquez had a chance to retain his crown on Sunday after winning the sprint race but needed his closest rival, Jorge Martin, to finish without any points.

Pole-sitter Bezzecchi claimed his sixth GP win of the season to cut the gap separating him from Marquez to 74 points.

However, the Italian, who is third in the championship standings, essentially has no chance of winning his first world title because that gap is the same as the number of points that remain available.

Bezzecchi was undone on Saturday by crashing out of the sprint race when trying to overtake Marquez in a desperate attempt to put pressure on the Spaniard.

“It feels amazing,” Bezzecchi said after he bounced back to win on Sunday. “I’m very happy. It was the performance we deserved

“It’s been a fantastic weekend for us. I’ve been super quick and super comfortable on the bike.

“It’s a shame for yesterday, but it’s part of the game, and to bounce back like this makes everything even better.”

Martin couldn’t quite emulate his heroics from Saturday when he shot up from 11th on the grid to nearly overtake eventual winner Marquez before eventually finishing third.

But racing this weekend for the first time since suffering a broken right wrist, Martin was given a warm round of applause from his team after keeping the title race alive.



Martin, Bezzecchi’s teammate at Aprilia, finished seventh and is still in contention even though he is 60 points off the pace with two race weekends remaining.

But Marquez could claim a record-equalling eighth premier class title, one more than his great rival Valentino Rossi, if he finishes two points ahead of Martin in the Portimao sprint in two weeks.

“[My strategy] was just to try to manage the race for the first five laps,” Marquez said.

“I saw that in one part of the race, I was super fast, but I knew that riding on that riding style, I was eating the front tyre.

“Third position was [would have been] OK, but I saw that [Raul] Fernandez was struggling, so you never know. I attack and four points more.”

Fernandez finished third at Qatar’s MotoGP, which marked the return of major motorsport to the region for the first time since the war on Iran began.

World.title: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
World.content:
A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say.

The 24-year-old, who officials said was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies", was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

Krakow police said the suspected gunman died early on Monday morning.

After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man but did not confirm his name.

In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.

Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack.

World.title: Inside the French drug gangs recruiting children to kill
World.content:
Warning: Strong language and descriptions of sexual violence

Although she had just bought hashish from a drug dealer, the woman decided to call the police.

It was because, along with the illegal drugs, she had been handed a note by the young seller during their brief meeting on a Marseille housing estate in 2022.

"We're being held captive and need help. We are 15-years-old," it read.

The teenage dealer, a French court heard earlier this year, was one of two boys being held by a gang which they had both initially approached looking for paid work - albeit illegal.

One boy had been tasked with handling money, the other worked streets around the Frais-Vallon estate. Soon though, bosses had accused them of being responsible for "shortfalls" in takings.

What followed were regular beatings, the court was told, and being forced to dance naked in front of a camera as a form of blackmail. One of the boys was also raped.

Hours after the woman was passed the note, the two teenagers had tried to escape from a second-storey window, injuring themselves in the process. One managed to get away, while the other was caught, beaten and stabbed, but survived.

Arrests were made. Photos on the phone of one of the boys' alleged torturers showed several other young men in a similarly distressed condition. Six men have since been handed hefty sentences for what happened to the two teenagers.

The boys' story highlights the grip that drug gangs hold over parts of France's second city.

While the blend of Mediterranean culture, street art and hip-hop scene has made Marseille a popular tourist destination - beyond the city centre, it is another story.

After months of trying, a BBC team managed to enter this dangerous world - centred on deprived streets and high-rise housing estates in the port city, which police do not enter lightly.

We found an environment where ruthless gangs lure vulnerable young people with promises of easy money, but end up trapping them in a world of drug dealing, brutality and exploitation.

We saw how gangs use social media to recruit hitmen and spoke to several young men caught up in the violence. From prison, one gang member accused of involvement in several murders explained how his "cold-bloodedness" had helped him rise through the ranks.

World.title: Trump says he was 'kidding' about Dana White press secretary offer
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has said he "was kidding" about asking Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be the White House press secretary.

Trump told the media on Sunday that White "loves the idea" but that the invitation was "just a little fun".

It comes after the president posted on his Truth Social platform on Saturday that he had offered White the role, asking him to take it while writing, "Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other."

White said later that day he was going to meet the president on Monday, but would not be drawn into whether or not he would take the vacant position.

On Sunday Trump told reporters White was visiting him on Monday for "other reasons".

"I think he's going to be in Washington. So he's going to come over and see me.

"I will tell you, I was only kidding. But Dana loves the idea. And there's only one Dana. He's great," the president said.

"But, it was it was just a little fun."

The press secretary role is yet to be filled after it became vacant in October when Katie Zacharia quit after less than five days in the job.

She took over from Karoline Leavitt, who was the youngest press secretary in US history and had held the role since Trump began his second term.

Trump's job offer came after a heavy loss in the midterm elections, where the Republican Party lost its majority in both houses of Congress.

In his Truth Social post on Saturday, he said he was "pleased to announce" that White "has been offered the job".

He said he had asked White to bring with him several current and former mixed martial arts fighters as "assistants".

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," he wrote.

"Dana, please take the job!"

Asked about the Trump offer at a news conference on Saturday, the UFC chief executive said he had "lot of jobs already".

"I'm sure we'll have something to talk about after that," he said of their planned Monday meeting, but did not say whether or not he would take the job.

White leads UFC, and PowerSlap, a regulated slap-fighting promotion league, as well as recently launching promotion company Zuffa Boxing.

He is also a board member of Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

White appeared as a speaker in support of Trump's White House campaigns at the Republican National Conventions in 2016, 2020 and 2024.

He also appeared on stage for Trump's victory speech in the 2024 presidential election.

This summer, the UFC staged a cage match on the White House lawn.

World.title: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
World.content:
At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source.

The Interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established.

The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands.

Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors.

Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued.

President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings.

In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys.

"We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said.

The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea.

Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored.

Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain.

Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria.

Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals.

More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities.

The Canary Islands have become a major entry point into Europe for migrants and refugees making the dangerous Atlantic crossing from West Africa.

The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean.

Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat.

Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency.

The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections.

In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries.

World.title: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has said Argentina's economy must benefit everyone including the poor, in a diplomatic but pointed critique of President Javier Milei's austerity measures.

The Pope was speaking as he arrived in Buenos Aires, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, only three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

In response, right-wing leader Milei said his government was working to avoid "punishing the Argentines of tomorrow in order to benefit the Argentines of today".

This leg of the Pope's journey was expected be the most politically sensitive, with the president's agenda of slashing public spending having been denounced by the Catholic Church for hitting the poorest hardest.

"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," Pope Leo said.

He stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs", and urged that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" - a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.

World.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean
World.content:
A cruise ship pianist was found treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast after falling overboard, according to US media reports.

Two fishermen discovered the Royal Caribbean employee near Catalina Island on Friday and officials believe he may have been in the Pacific Ocean for nine hours, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner.

"I'm like, 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat; let's get all of our lines in," Grant Garrett was quoted as saying, recalling the moment he and Sean Norton spotted him.

The man, who has not yet been identified, was taken to hospital in a stable condition, the US Coast Guard told the BBC, adding it was investigating the incident.

The fishermen say the man identified himself as a pianist on a 14-deck cruise ship called the Ovation of the Seas.

"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said.

The Coast Guard said in a statement it had received a report from "a Good Samaritan who recovered a conscious individual from the water".

The person was handed over to Newport Beach Lifeguards, who confirmed he was an employee of the Ovation of the Seas cruise ship, it said.

Lifeguard officials believe he may have fallen overboard at around 02:30, about nine hours before he was discovered.

"It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean," Newport Beach Lifeguard Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda told CBS.

Norton credited the man's survival to unusually warm ocean temperatures.

"You have this crazy super El NiÃ±o year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water's 76 degrees," Norton said, which equates to about 24C.

"A different year, no way he makes it," Norton said.

The developing El NiÃ±o climate phenomenon is now the strongest on record, according to scientists monitoring the Pacific, with ocean temperatures about 3.05C above average.

In a statement to the BBC, a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson said: "We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time.

"To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share."

World.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
World.content:
At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured.

The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.

Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.

Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".

The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise.

World.title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election
World.content:
South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic".

While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 31% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 65% 20 years ago.

The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second in the overall vote with 25%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town. Former president Jacob Zuma's MK party came third overall with 10%, unseating the ANC as winner in the city of Durban, while the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), led by Julius Malema, once seen as a serious challenge to the ANC, came fourth with 6%.

"This has been a very catastrophic outcome for the ANC," said secretary-general Fikile Mbalula on Saturday. "We knew this disaster is coming, we're staring at it. As we got into elections, the cost of living of our people was too high. The middle class have turned on the ANC in big numbers."

Entering the count centre on Sunday nigh, South Africa's president and ANC leader Cyril Ramaphosa said: "We accept the will of the people however concerning it might be, we accept that this is how the people of South Africa in our towns, in our cities, in our metros have spoken - and this is their verdict, we accept it with humility. It is a decline that is concerning, that is how I characterise it."

World.title: 2027: ‘We’re prepared to secure victory for all APC candidates’ – Ukwueze
World.content:
The Chairman of Igbo-Eze South Local Government Area of Enugu State and Deputy Chairman of ALGON, Enugu State, Ugo Ferdinand Ukwueze, has expressed confidence in the readiness of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to secure victory for all its candidates in the 2027 general elections, following the successful flag-off of the Enugu State APC Campaign at Nsukka Township Stadium on Wednesday, 4 November.

Mr Ukwueze made this known after joining Governor of Enugu State Peter Mbah, alongside other political leaders, stakeholders and party faithful at the historic campaign rally, which attracted a massive crowd from across the state.

Mr Ukwueze described the impressive turnout as a powerful demonstration of the growing acceptance of the APC and the confidence Ndi Enugu have continued to repose in the leadership of Governor Mbah and the progressive ideals of the party.

According to him, the rally was not merely a formal commencement of political activities ahead of the 2027 elections, but a clear manifestation of the party’s strength, unity, organisational capacity and determination to consolidate the gains of purposeful governance.

He noted that the developmental strides of the Mbah administration, particularly in infrastructure, education, healthcare, security, economic transformation and human capital development, have continued to inspire confidence and strengthen the resolve of the people to support the party.

The council chairman further emphasised that the overwhelming enthusiasm witnessed at the flag-off was a strong indication of the political momentum building across Enugu State, expressing optimism that the energy and unity displayed would translate into electoral success for the APC in 2027.

He reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening grassroots mobilisation and ensuring that the achievements and vision of the administration reach every ward, community and household across Igbo-Eze South and beyond.

“As a party, we are prepared to take our message to the people, consolidate our structures and work tirelessly towards securing victory for all APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. The enthusiasm witnessed at Nsukka has further strengthened our confidence and determination,” he stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He congratulated the APC leadership and members on the successful flag-off, urging party faithful to remain united, focused and committed to the collective task of delivering victory at the polls.

World.title: Speeding car kills tricycle rider, four passengers
World.content:
A speeding car has killed a commercial tricycle rider and four passengers in a road crash in Delta State, South-south Nigeria.

The victims included a pregnant woman and a four-month-old child.

A witness, Jude Okonkwo, told the News Agency of Nigeria that the accident occurred around 8:25 a.m. on Saturday.

The crash happened along the Ogwashi-Uku Polytechnic–Azagba Road in Ogwashi-Uku, Aniocha South Local Government Area of Delta State.

Mr Okonkwo said a man was driving a Lexus 350 from the Azagba axis at high speed and allegedly crossed into the opposite lane and rammed into the oncoming tricycle.

The impact reportedly killed the tricycle rider and the four passengers instantly.

The driver, who escaped unhurt, reportedly abandoned his vehicle and fled to avoid being attacked by an angry mob.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Witnesses and passers-by subsequently set the Lexus car ablaze before police operatives from Ogwashi-Uku Division arrived.

However, a combined team of police officers and local vigilantes intercepted and rescued the fleeing suspect. He was subsequently taken into police custody.

Witnesses said four of the victims were women traders travelling from Ogwashi-Uku to the weekly Nkwor Azagba Market.

They were reportedly carrying goods to the market along the Benin-Asaba Expressway.

When contacted, the spokesperson for the police command in Delta, Bright Edafe, a police superintendent, said he was unaware of the incident.

“I am not aware of the incident. I have not received any brief from the police in Ogwashi-Uku on the incident. I will get back to you once I am briefed,” he said.

World.title: Omo-Agege condemns violent attack on NDC rally, demands investigation
World.content:
The former deputy president of the Senate Ovie Omo-Agege has called for a comprehensive investigation into the recent attack on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Asaba, Delta State.

Mr Omo-Agege is the NDC senatorial candidate for the Delta Central District in the forthcoming 2027 general elections.

He made the call on Sunday in a statement through his Special Adviser, Strategy and Communications, Godwin Anaughe in Warri.

“Thousands of ordinary residents of Delta on Saturday, came out to walk peacefully and campaign for the NDC ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“The residents, led by the Obidient/OK Movement filled the streets, singing and carrying the message of Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the NDC to the people.

“Suddenly, thugs, fully armed with dangerous weapons, descended on the unarmed campaigners. More than 30 vehicles were smashed, while over 10 of NDC members and supporters were left bleeding heavily,” Mr Omo-Agege stated.

According to him, the police have confirmed one death. Reports say the deceased was one of the attackers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“One death is one too many. Whoever sent armed thugs into a peaceful march must answer for it.

“We demand the police to identify the deceased, tell us how he died, and prosecute everyone, who organised and sponsored this attack,” he further stated.

Mr Omo-Agege described the attack as “animalistic and barbaric”.

He said the attack was borne out of fear of NDC’s grip on the grassroots in Delta.

The former senator said the Asaba incident was not a one-off. He recalled other incidences in which the party suffered attacks in the state.

“On 13 August, in Usiefrun, Ughelli South, armed men attacked our people who had simply gathered to receive us.

“On 21 August, over 50 armed men stormed Uvwie and destroyed the venue we had prepared for a campaign meeting.

“Also, on 18 September, in Warri and Effurun, our One Million-Man March for Deacon Chris Iyovwaye was ambushed at Angle Park, Uvwie junction, Ugborokoko, Jakpa Road, Urhuomarho,” he said.

Omo-Agege called on security agencies to provide the party with security to march and to do road shows.

He also called on the Inspector-General of Police, Oluwatunji Disu and the Director-General of the Department of State Services, Adeola Ajayi to arrest and prosecute those involved in the attack.

He urged the party supporters to remain steadfast, assuring that the party’s rallies would be properly guarded.

Mr Omo-Agege, while thanking the bystanders, shop owners, traders, and artisans for their quick intervention in the attack, urged the youth not to allow themselves to be used as thugs.

The Delta State Government and the Delta APC campaign council have also condemned the attack on the NDC supporters.

Charles Aniagwu, Delta State commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information/ Media Committee Chairman of the APC, said in a statement on Sunday that the attack was as unacceptable. He warned political parties and their supporters to desist from taking actions that could threaten public peace and security.

(NAN)

World.title: 2027 Politics Watch: Atiku fights to stay on ballot, Tinubu backers’ claim 500-plus vehicles
World.content:
Rauf Aregbesola’s separate appeal against the judgement invalidating the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) became public on Sunday, adding another legal challenge to a ruling that also voided Atiku Abubakar’s presidential nomination.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), meanwhile, said it would obtain the certified copy and examine the judgement before deciding how to respond.

The dispute could affect more than Atiku’s place on the ballot. INEC’s procedures require national party chairmen to receive access codes for submitting polling agents, with the portal scheduled to close on 10 December.

Elsewhere, the Delta State Government demanded an investigation into Saturday’s deadly opposition procession in Asaba, while a group supporting President Bola Tinubu claimed to have distributed more than 500 campaign vehicles.

Sunday also brought a fresh argument over the Ibom Deep Sea Port, with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) questioning whether the president’s latest approval represented progress beyond an earlier federal decision.

The developments put party authority, campaign security, political financing and government promises at the centre of another day of electioneering.

ADC’s legal battle reaches polling-agent preparations

Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja ruled on 5 November that the ADC leadership headed by former Senate President David Mark had been unlawfully constituted.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The court invalidated decisions arising from the party’s disputed 99th National Executive Committee meeting, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate.

The suit, identified in court reporting as FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, was brought by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former ADC deputy national chairman who challenged the leadership succession following Ralph Nwosu’s departure.

The ADC has appealed the ruling and applied for a stay of execution.

On Sunday, details emerged of a separate appeal filed by Mr Aregbesola, the party’s national secretary, through his lawyer, Mohammed Sheriff, a senior advocate of Nigeria.

Mr Aregbesola challenged the trial court’s jurisdiction and interpretation of the party’s constitution. His lawyers argued that the court failed to distinguish between an election to fill a leadership vacancy and a temporary appointment permitted under the ADC constitution.

The notice of appeal was filed on Friday, 6 November, while a separate application seeking to suspend enforcement of specified orders was filed the following day.

Neither an appeal nor an application for a stay automatically establishes that the judgment has been suspended.

The News Agency of Nigeria reported the separate appeal, while PREMIUM TIMES previously reported the ADC’s challenge.

INEC National Commissioner Mohammed Haruna told Sunday PUNCH that the commission would study the judgement and discuss its implications at its next meeting.

One administrative question concerns the party’s polling agents.

INEC’s electronic platform states that access codes are issued to national party chairmen, who distribute them to authorised officials responsible for uploading agents’ details.

The portal gives 10 December, at 11.59 p.m. West Africa Time, as the submission deadline for the 16 January presidential election.

The disputed ADC leadership could therefore raise questions about which officials INEC recognises for that process. There is, however, no established evidence that the commission has denied the party access or rejected its polling-agent submissions.

The controversy has a parallel in the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

On 4 November, the Court of Appeal upheld a decision refusing to compel INEC to recognise the interim leadership associated with Kabiru Turaki.

INEC’s party directory identifies Abdulrahman Mohammed, who leads the rival faction supported by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, as national chairman.

At a Sunday briefing, Mr Turaki accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of benefiting from judicial decisions against opposition factions.

He also criticised Mr Wike’s Rainbow Coalition, whose members support Mr Tinubu despite belonging to different political parties.

The allegations of political interference remain unproven. The APC has denied responsibility for the ADC’s internal leadership dispute.

PREMIUM TIMES reported Mr Turaki’s allegations.

INEC lists Sandy Onor as the PDP presidential candidate, illustrating the difference between a party’s formal nomination and the presidential preferences of influential politicians within its ranks.

Delta demands inquiry into fatal opposition procession

The Delta State Government on Sunday called for an investigation into violence that left one person dead and five others injured during an opposition procession in Asaba the previous day.

The event, organised by the Obidient/OK Movement, was intended to mobilise support for NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso.

The incident occurred along Nnebisi Road.

Mr Obi had condemned the violence on Saturday evening and demanded that those responsible be identified and prosecuted.

Sunday’s development was the state government’s intervention and the emergence of competing accounts of the security arrangements.

Delta’s Commissioner for Works, Rural Roads and Public Information, Charles Aniagwu, said organisers should have followed police advice to use a designated venue.

Police said they had warned of possible violence and subsequently responded to a distress call, taking injured persons to hospital.

The movement’s state coordinator, Favour Emerure, disputed the suggestion that organisers disregarded police instructions.

He said the command had been notified and that the procession avoided Inter-Bua Junction as directed. He also questioned the absence of officers when the violence began.

These accounts leave unresolved whether adequate security arrangements were agreed, what happened before the confrontation and who was responsible for the attack.

The police-reported casualty figures do not establish the identity or political affiliation of the perpetrators.

The Guardian reported the state government’s response, while PREMIUM TIMES covered the fatal incident in Saturday’s roundup.

The incident adds to concerns about campaign security as political activities expand ahead of the January presidential election.

Tinubu’s supporters expand campaign network across North-West

The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, associated with Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, said on Sunday that it had distributed more than 500 vehicles for grassroots mobilisation in approximately 20 states.

Its national coordinator, Sunday Asuku, announced a further tour of Enugu, Cross River, Bayelsa, Zamfara, Jigawa, Anambra, Kebbi and Abia between 9 and 14 November.

The claimed fleet has not been independently verified.

PREMIUM TIMES previously documented the presentation of 26 vehicles each in Ondo and Gombe states.

The movement has not published a complete inventory showing the acquisition costs, ownership, funding sources or recipients of the wider fleet.

Those records matter for determining whether particular contributions or expenditures fall within the disclosure requirements governing political parties and campaigns.

Section 93 of the Electoral Act 2026 requires political parties to submit audited election-expense returns within six months after an election. The returns must include expenditure incurred by or on behalf of the party and the commercial value of relevant goods and services received.

Whether the claimed vehicles form part of reportable APC expenditure depends on their financing, use and relationship with the party’s campaign.

The announcement coincided with fresh APC organisational activity in the North-West.

In Kebbi, Governor Nasir Idris inaugurated the party’s state campaign council on Sunday, days after Atiku campaigned in Birnin Kebbi.

The state is politically significant because Atiku defeated Mr Tinubu there in the 2023 presidential election, receiving 285,175 votes against 248,088.

In neighbouring Jigawa, Governor Umar Namadi said the APC could deliver two million votes for Mr Tinubu in 2027.

That ambition is more than twice the 954,805 votes cast in Jigawa during the 2023 presidential election, when Mr Tinubu won with 421,390 votes.

The comparison measures the scale of the governor’s target against historical turnout; it does not establish how many people will vote in 2027.

Mr Kwankwaso, campaigning separately in Dutse for the NDC, also revisited his failure to reach an alliance with Mr Obi before the 2023 election.

The two politicians, who contested separately that year, now share the NDC presidential ticket.

Their alliance illustrates one form of opposition cooperation, although Mr Atiku continues to pursue the presidency under the ADC.

Ibom port dispute raises questions over what Tinubu approved

The NDC challenged President Tinubu’s latest announcement concerning the Ibom Deep Sea Port, arguing that the project had already received federal approval under former President Muhammadu Buhari.

At an APC rally in Uyo on Friday, Mr Tinubu approved a request presented by Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno.

On Sunday, NDC spokesperson Osa Director questioned what the new approval added to decisions previously taken by the federal government.

The Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission’s 2020 annual report records Federal Executive Council approval of the project’s full business case on 16 December 2020.

But that approval was not equivalent to confirmation that the project had been fully financed or constructed.

The regulator identified the finalisation of contracts and financing as subsequent steps.

At the time, Akwa Ibom officials estimated the first phase would cost approximately $2 billion, with the state expected to provide 40 per cent and a preferred private bidder the remainder.

Mr Eno has described the latest presidential decision as approval of financing arrangements.

That explanation raises questions the earlier approval alone cannot answer: how much financing has now been committed, on what terms, by which institutions and against what construction timetable?

The NDC’s accusation that the president recycled an earlier promise remains a political claim. Establishing whether the new decision is substantive requires the underlying financing and project documents.

The PUNCH reported the NDC’s challenge, while Channels Television reported Mr Eno’s explanation.

The APC also promoted railway construction as evidence of its infrastructure record.

Its presidential campaign council announced 3 December as the proposed inauguration date for the 190-kilometre Jaji–Kano section of the Kaduna–Kano railway and the 250-kilometre Dawanu–Kano–Kazaure–Daura–Katsina section of the Kano–Maradi project.

The campaign council cited estimated completion levels of 90 per cent for Kaduna–Kano and 70 per cent for Kano–Maradi.

The transport ministry had previously identified December as a commissioning target.

An inauguration announcement does not establish that regular passenger operations will begin on that date. Operational readiness and the timetable for commercial services require confirmation from the responsible transport authorities.

PREMIUM TIMES reported the railway announcement.

Lagos candidates clash over transport and healthcare financing

In Lagos, Sunday’s governorship debate brought competing approaches to public infrastructure and healthcare into sharper focus.

ADC candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour proposed greater reliance on private infrastructure financing for rail expansion, with investors repaid over an extended period.

APC candidate and Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat favoured substantial government investment, arguing that recovering construction costs directly through fares could make rail transport unaffordable.

The disagreement went beyond the number of projects each candidate promised. It concerned who should bear the initial financial burden and how those costs would ultimately reach commuters or taxpayers.

Mr Hamzat also proposed expanding the bus fleet to 4,000 and introducing 77 electric ferries.

NDC candidate Funso Doherty called for modern buses to replace ageing commercial vehicles, while PDP candidate Deji Doherty identified heavy goods traffic, poor roads and delays in major infrastructure projects as contributors to congestion.

Healthcare produced another set of measurable commitments.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour proposed establishing emergency response centres in each of Lagos’s 245 wards, with two ambulances per centre, while Mr Hamzat promised to extend health insurance coverage to one in three residents.

Mr Funso Doherty advocated free maternal and child healthcare, including medicines and diagnostic tests. Mr Deji Doherty emphasised increasing the health workforce and supporting local medical production.

The proposals also differed in their budget implications.

Mr Rhodes-Vivour advocated raising the health sector’s share of state expenditure towards 15 per cent. Mr Funso Doherty proposed increasing the combined allocation to health and education to 28 per cent during his first term.

Earlier in the year, Lagos Health Commissioner Akin Abayomi said the state allocated approximately eight per cent of its budget to health and faced an estimated N100 billion gap between projected needs and available funding.

Those figures provide a starting point for assessing the candidates’ proposals, but none of the promises can be judged on headline percentages alone.

Their feasibility will depend on revenue assumptions, existing spending commitments, implementation costs and the services each proposal is intended to deliver.

PREMIUM TIMES reported the candidates’ competing proposals.

World.title: Federal High Court announces two-week Christmas/New Year break, appoints vacation judges
World.content:
The Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, John Tsoho, has announced a two-week Yuletide break starting from 21 December appointed vacation judges who will attend to emergency cases during the period.

Justice Tsoho, who announced this in a statement signed by Catherine Oby-Christopher, the Director of Information of the court, said the vacation begins on 21 December and ends on 5 January.

“Pursuant to the provisions of Order 46, Rule 4(c) of the Federal High Court (Civil ) Procedure Rules, 2019, the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court has approved the Christmas Vacation of the Court for the year 2026 and the roster of Judges designated to sit during the vacation period.

“Regular court sittings shall resume on 6 January,” the chief judge said.

The chief judge only the designated judicial divisions shall remain operational during the vacation to provide judicial services to the litigating public.

He said Justice Inyang Ekwo and Justice Obiora Egwuatu will sit as vacation judges for the Abuja division while Justice Akintayo Aluko and Justice Ogazi Nkemakonam will sit at the Lagos division.

READ ALSO: Court restrains Kaduna university unions from strike

He also said Justice P. M. Ayua and Justice A. T. Mohammed will sit at Port Harcourt division while Justice Folashade Giwa-Ogunbanjo and Justice M. T. Segun-Bello will sit at the Enugu judicial division.

“It is important to note that, during the vacation period, the vacation judges shall entertain only matters relating to the enforcement of fundamental rights, the arrest or release of vessels, and other matters of urgent national importance such as trial of pre- election cases,” Mr Tsoho said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The chief judge wished all judges and members of the court a Merry Christmas and a prosperous New Year in advance.

(NAN)

World.title: Delta govt, APC condemn attack on NDC, urge independent investigation
World.content:
The Delta State Government, All Progressives Congress (APC) and its Delta Campaign Council on Sunday condemned the fatal political violence that erupted on Saturday during the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) road rally in Asaba.

This is contained in a statement by Charles Aniagwu, State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information/ Media Committee Chairman of the APC in Asaba.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that the NDC one-million-man rally in Asaba on Saturday claimed one life with many others sustaining serious injuries from attacks by unknown political thugs.

The rally, organised by NDC supporters, was disrupted by suspected political thugs, leaving several participants injured and destroying more than 30 vehicles, including campaign buses and tricycles.

NAN reports that no fewer than 10 party members and supporters sustained injuries, with some reportedly rushed to the hospital for medical attention.

Victor Ochei, NDC Delta North Senatorial Candidate, condemned the attack and called on the Delta State Government and security agencies to investigate the incident and bring those responsible to justice.

According to Mr Ochei, the rally was conceived as a one-million-man march to demonstrate the growing popularity of the NDC and its readiness to participate in the 2027 general elections.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Responding to the NDC attack, Mr Aniagwu described the incident as unacceptable, warning political parties and their supporters against actions capable of threatening public peace and security.

The commissioner said the state government, under Governor Sheriff Oborevwori’s watch, has zero tolerance for political violence, intimidation and other forms of political radicalism.

He said the government had repeatedly cautioned political parties against engaging in activities capable of disrupting the peace, stressing that the unfortunate incident could have been avoided if the organisers had heeded security advice.

He explained that the police had advised the organisers to shelve the proposed street march and instead, hold their campaign at a designated venue where adequate security arrangements could be provided.

The government expressed concern that the advice was ignored, resulting in a confrontation that claimed a life and left several others injured.

APC campaign council ‘deeply saddened’

Mr Aniagwu said the APC campaign council was deeply saddened by reports of loss of life, injuries and destruction of property arising from the unfortunate incident.

“Our thoughts and sympathies are with the family of the deceased, those injured and everyone affected by this regrettable development.

READ ALSO: NDC senatorial candidate expresses concerns over alleged intimidation of opposition parties in Edo

“No political ambition or disagreement is worth the life of any citizen, and no political contest should ever degenerate into violence.

“As a council, we demand an impartial investigation into the unfortunate development even as we insist that political disagreements must not degenerate to any form of intimidation, violence or destruction of property.

“It is important to reiterate that, from the very outset of our political mobilisation, particularly at the inauguration of the Delta APC campaign council, our leadership made an unequivocal commitment to peaceful, responsible and issue-based campaigns.

“That commitment remains unwavering. Our campaign philosophy is anchored on presenting our achievements, programmes, vision and policy alternatives to the good people of Delta, and we have no intention of deviating from that path,” he said.

He urged the police to conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that everyone found responsible is brought to justice.

He also urged political parties, their leaders and supporters to conduct their activities within the bounds of the law and demonstrate respect for human life, public order and the rights of others.

(NAN).

World.title: Jigawa governor speaks on President Tinubu’s visit, projects to be commissioned
World.content:
The Jigawa State Government has promised President Bola Tinubu a rousing reception when he arrives in the state on Tuesday for a working visit and campaign rally.

Speaking to reporters late Sunday after conducting an inspection tour of the project sites and the campaign rally venue, Governor Umar Namadi said all logistical and security arrangements have been finalised ahead of the visit.

According to the governor, President Tinubu will inaugurate key developmental and agricultural empowerment projects in Dutse, the state capital, during the visit.

He said the president will unveil 400 brand-new tractors fitted with implements, 60 combined harvesters, 150 threshers, and 150 boom sprayers.

The governor said Mr Tinubu will also commission the Renewed Hope Technical Services, the Bola Ahmed Tinubu Multipurpose Skills Acquisition Centre, and the newly dualised Garo Road within the Dutse metropolis.

Governor Namadi said his administration has executed projects across the state’s 27 local government areas, but those to be commissioned on Tuesday were selected in Dutse due to the president’s tight itinerary.

“We have supervised all the project sites that will be commissioned by the President and the venue for the campaign rally, and we are very confident and waiting for Mr President. I can say, perfectly, that Jigawa is waiting for Mr President,” Governor Namadi stated.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We selected a few projects within the metropolis, conscious of the timing of the President. We have hundreds of projects spread across the 27 local government areas, but because of the President’s schedule, he cannot do that in a one-day visit,” he added.

Reaffirming the state’s solidarity with the administration, Governor Namadi expressed optimism about massive public turnout, noting that the people of Jigawa hold the President in high esteem.

“We believe that Jigawa is for President Bola Tinubu; all we need to do is inform the people that the president is coming, and they will come out en masse to welcome him. The residents are ready to receive the President,” the governor stated.

Why Jigawa is included in the president’s campaign itinerary

Jigawa State is not in the schedued 12-state campaign tour of Mr Tinubu released by the All Progressives Congress (APC).

While inaugurating the Jigawa State APC campaign council on Saturday, the Speaker of the state House of Assembly, Haruna Aliyu, announced that the president had included Jigawa because of his confidence in the state’s leadership and its people.

World.title: Toluwanisings burial underway in Ibadan
World.content:
Family members, friends and colleagues have gathered in Ibadan, Oyo State, to bid Nigerian singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji a final farewell as his burial ceremony gets underway.

A funeral flyer posted on the singer’s social media page on Monday outlined the activities for his final rites.

The programme shows that the family will hold his lying-in-state between 9 a.m. and 10 a.m. today at Banjola Event and Conference Centre, No. 20 Hope Road, Alakia, Ibadan.

The burial service will follow immediately, running from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m., before the family commits his remains to the earth.

However, the flyer does not disclose the specific location where the singer will be buried.

“Forever in our hearts always in our lives. Order of funeral arrangements. Monday, 9th November, 2026. Lying-in-state: 9:00AM – 10:00AM Burial service: 10:00AM – 11:00AM.

“Venue: Banjola event and conference center, No. 20 Hope road, Alakia, Ibadan. Hope Road is the road before the airport junction in Ibadan”, the flyer contents read.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Backstory

The announcement of the singer’s burial followed the intervention of the Oyo State Police Command in a dispute over his final resting place involving his family, wife and associates.

The disagreement began after the singer’s family rejected plans by his wife, Elizabeth, and associates to bury him in a cemetery. PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the family instead demanded that they inter his remains at his residence.

The dispute generated considerable attention on social media, where the family threatened to exhume the singer’s body if the parties buried him in a cemetery.

They also urged the authorities to establish the circumstances of his death before conducting the burial, expressing concerns about possible foul play.

Reacting to the development, police spokesperson Ayanlade Olayinka said the command stepped in after the disagreement prompted allegations of conspiracy, defamation and conduct that could undermine public peace.

He said the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received complaints about the dispute over the burial arrangements after the parties exchanged heated remarks on different public communication platforms.

The singer’s wife, his father, Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, Oyindamola Esther, Babadunmi Gbolabo and Lawal Rafiu; his personal assistant; and other representatives later signed a peace undertaking.

The agreement required all parties to maintain peace, conduct themselves responsibly and avoid actions that could provoke unrest.

They also committed to ending public arguments, interviews and discussions that could further inflame tensions over the singer’s death and other related matters.

World.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
World.content:
Murat Kurum, COP31 President and Turkeys Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change, gives a speech during the opening session of the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference at the Antalya Expo Center on November 9, 2026. Turkey will host the COP31 climate talks from November 9 to 20 in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, with Australia presiding over the negotiations. (Photo by Ozan KOSE / AFP)

The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday with an early fight over money as the UN’s chief urged world leaders to “get serious” about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes.

Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN’s annual two-week climate conference.

The summit comes after a year of punishing heatwaves in Europe, major wildfires in Indonesia and catastrophic floods in Nepal, with an exceptionally strong El Nino weather phenomenon fuelling more climate chaos.

“We have entered a new age of climate extremes,” Guterres said in a statement.

The UN secretary-general urged leaders to “get serious by cutting emissions faster, accelerating a just transition from fossil fuels and delivering the finance and protection vulnerable countries need”.

The COP31 opening ceremony opened an hour-and-a-half late without explanation.

Negotiators had been locked in discussions late Sunday over demands by developing nations to include items on climate finance in the official agenda.

“This has already been a difficult start for COP31,” said Jasper Inventor, head of Greenpeace’s COP31 delegation.

Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy. But poorer countries say the sums remain insufficient.

Inventor said developed countries took a “hard line” over whether to include a platform, agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year, aimed at discussing how wealthy nations should provide funds to developing nations.

A source familiar with the talks said the “climate finance work programme” would be included in the agenda.

African countries had also pushed for the agenda to include the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops.

The source said there would be no separate agenda point on tripling of adaptation finance but that it would be discussed under other items.

A senior European Union official warned last week that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges at COP31.

Observers say few major breakthroughs are expected at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine.

The long-term climate outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement.

– Fossil fuel fight –

Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference but raised concerns over how it would work.

The two sides have celebrated their cooperation so far, with COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey’s environment minister, and Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen raising their clasped hands above their heads to applause during the opening ceremony.

The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements.

“We know that delay carries one of the heaviest costs in climate action,” Kurum said.

Turkey is inviting countries to join a voluntary “electrification” pledge to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035.

– ‘Clean’ electrification? –

But the initiative could become a source of friction.

The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal.

Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action.

COP30 ended with a deal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels after oil-producing countries opposed the language.

Instead, Brazil produced a voluntary “roadmap” with proposals for phasing out fossil fuels that each country can tailor to their circumstances.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who will be among leaders addressing COP31 later this week, was due to arrive late Monday, fresh from a re-election win that activists hailed as a victory for climate change.

But climate diplomacy is still missing a major player as climate-sceptic US President Donald Trump has not sent officials to COP31.

A US congressional delegation, however, will come to Antalya, with Democrats beaming after last week’s historic US midterm election win.

World.title: Government offices shut in Osun as NLC directs workers strike
World.content:
Government offices in Osun were shut on Monday as workers embark on a three-day strike as directed by the state chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on Sunday.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the gates to the Osun Government Secretariat and the State House of Assembly in Osogbo were under lock with no workers or business activities ongoing in the premises.

Similarly, the Olorunda Local Government Secretariat and Osogbo Local Government Secretariat gates were also locked.

Students of public schools in Osogbo were also asked to return home, as teachers in public schools equally joined the strike.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that NLC Chairman in Osun, Christopher Arapasopo, and Secretary, Victor Amusan, in a statement on Sunday, directed all affiliate members of the congress to embark on a three-day sympathy strike with the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE).

The NLC leadership explained that the strike followed the expiration of the seven-day ultimatum issued to the Federal and Osun governments over the continued withholding of the state local government statutory allocations.

The NLC said that the issues raised concerning the local government allocations had remained unresolved.

It said that after exhausting all reasonable avenues and in accordance with the resolutions reached at the emergency meeting of the State Executive Council (SEC) held on Oct. 28, all affiliate members of NLC were directed to embark on strike. (NAN)

World.title: African players in Europe: Jackson scores as Villa squander leads at United
World.content:
Aston Villa’s Senegalese striker #11 Nicolas Jackson (C) celebrates after scoring his team’s second goal during the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Aston Villa at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on November 8, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Senegal star Nicolas Jackson scored after just four minutes for Aston Villa, who twice surrendered two-goal leads in a remarkable 4-4 Premier League draw away to Manchester United at the weekend.

AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues:

ENGLAND

NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa)

Jackson put his side 2-0 ahead against United, but it wasn’t enough to inspire a victory at Old Trafford. When Jackson tapped in after United goalkeeper Senne Lammens palmed the ball into his path, it appeared the 25-year-old’s ninth goal in 14 games in all competitions this term would be the spark for a comfortable Villa win. But in an incredible finale, United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue a draw.

YANN GBOHO (Coventry City)

The Ivory Coast winger scored his first Premier League goal in a 3-1 defeat at Everton. Gboho, signed from French side Toulouse in September, put Coventry ahead with a composed finish after evading slack defending in the 52nd minute. But Frank Lampard’s team crumbled after the 25-year-old’s strike as Everton scored three times to leave the visitors one point above the relegation zone.

SPAIN

YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander)

Moroccan forward Zabiri continued his superb season with another goal to help Santander win 2-1 at Malaga. The 21-year-old bagged his ninth of the campaign with a simple finish to tuck a rebound home into the empty net. Only Raphinha, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal have scored more goals this season in La Liga.

ITALY

KONAN N’DRI (Lecce)

After Angolan Kailonda Gaspar conceded a 60th-minute own goal to give Torino the lead in a clash of bottom-half Serie A clubs, Niger international N’Dri scored to salvage a 1-1 draw for visiting Lecce. The architect of the equaliser was Mali international Lassana Coulibaly.

GERMANY

EZECHIEL BANZUZI (RB Leipzig)

Banzuzi’s goal proved the turning point as he kick-started Leipzig’s recovery to beat Augsburg 5-2 at home in the Bundesliga after conceding inside the opening minute. Anton Kade had Augsburg in front after 36 seconds but Banzuzi levelled in the 33rd minute when he turned a Brajan Gruda pass into the bottom right corner. The 21-year-old Democratic Republic of Congo internnational has two goals and two assists in the league this season.

UCHENNA OGUNDU (Augsburg)

Ogundu’s first goal in Augsburg colours was a mere consolation as his side crashed at Leipzig. With Leipzig 5-1 up, Augsburg’s Alexis Claude Maurice intercepted the ball and sent his side in the other direction. Fabian Rieder latched on to Claude Maurice’s pass before finding Ogundu, who slid the ball into the bottom corner.

FRANCE

LASSINE SINAYOKO (Paris FC)

Ligue 1’s leading scorer Sinayoko netted after 63 minutes to give third-placed Paris FC a 1-0 win at lowly Auxerre. It was the ninth goal of the campaign in 10 matches for the Mali striker.

World.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [INEC in Eye of the Storm] Electoral body battles to clean voters’ register — Investigation

In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with an investigation on how the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) faces test of integrity in cleaning up the voters’ register said to contain duplications and other discrepancies.

Another headline features the African Democratic Congress (ADC) telling the governing party, All Progressives Congress (APC), to test its popularity at the polls instead of using courts.
