World.title: Booshle G engagement: ‘I got engaged to my best friend’ [video]
World.content:
Singer Booshle G proposed to his partner, Gabriela, on 2 November 2026. Image: Instagram @booshle_gsa

The Booshle G engagement has given fans one more reason to celebrate in what has already been a busy few weeks for the singer.

Booshle G, whose real name is Buhle Gayika, is a South African singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist known for blending pop, folk and rock into his music.

Now he has surprised his partner with a cinematic outdoor proposal, and judging by the video, she never saw it coming.



He popped the question to his partner and best friend, Gabriela, on Monday, 2 November.

The couple shared the news on social media, alongside a video of the surprise proposal.

How the Booshle G engagement unfolded

The proposal took place in a picturesque setting, with a grassy valley, a pond and rolling hills in the background. Gabriela can be heard exclaiming again and again as the moment unfolds, clearly overwhelmed.

Family and friends had been in on the plan.

Once she said yes, the gathering moved to a garden for an impromptu celebration.



“I got engaged to my best friend. Thank you to all our friends and family who made this possible.

We owe it to you,” Booshle G wrote. He also thanked videographer Daniel Storm Smith for capturing the moment.

Booshle G engaged as a big month continues

The engagement news comes as the singer’s career continues to grow.

He recently announced his Love is Free tour, a 20-date run across South Africa, Europe and the UK in 2027.

His next single, Dirty Blazers, is due out on Friday, 20 November.

Cape Town fans will also get to see him live soon. Booshle G will share the stage with Freshlyground at the Kirstenbosch Summer Sunset Concerts on Sunday, 29 November, the second concert of the summer series.

Wedding season in celebville

The singer joins a growing list of South African celebrities sharing relationship milestones this season.

Fans flooded his comments with congratulations, and many said the proposal video had left them emotional.

World.title: Donald Trump claims offer of press secretary role to Dana White was a joke
World.content:
An Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) fight planned at the White House will take place on Donald Trump's 80th birthday. Image: Wikimedia Commons

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he was only joking when he offered the role of White House press secretary to Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief Dana White earlier in the weekend.

“I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea,” Trump told reporters on the tarmac of his namesake airport in Florida.

Dana White, a longtime friend of Donald Trump, was with the president when he declared reelection victory in November 2024. Image: Jim WATSON / AFP

Vacant

The press secretary role – traditionally one of the administration’s most visible positions – has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week on the job.



White, the 57-year-old president and CEO of UFC, and is a long-time friend of the president.

Speaking in London late on Saturday, White was reticent, saying that he would “have more to talk about” after meeting with Trump on Monday.

White’s UFC staged a bloody cage fight on the White House South Lawn on Trump’s 80th birthday in June, and he appeared on stage with Trump during his reelection victory speech in 2024.

‘Please take the job!’

In a social media post on Saturday, Donald Trump implored White to accept his offer, writing, “Dana, please take the job!” and calling him a “violent fighter and warrior.”

He also suggested White bring along several fighters as assistants, three of whom were not American.

In his comments on Sunday, Trump suggested the inclusion of the fighters “from parts unknown” was how the public should have known it was a joke.



“Of course I was kidding, and you could see that because I put all of the great fighters as his assistants,” Trump said.

Trump also confirmed that a meeting with White was still planned for Monday.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Australia axe Marnus Labuschagne
World.content:
Australia's Marnus Labuschagne has been dropped for their Test series against New Zealand. Image: Saeed KHAN / AFP

Marnus Labuschagne was Monday axed from Australia’s squad for their upcoming four-Test series against New Zealand, paying the price for a long run of poor form.

The number three, who has played 68 Tests, was under-pressure going into their recent tour of South Africa and failed to fire across the three Tests.

Lot of speculation

“At this stage we won’t be considering Marn for selection for certainly that first Test, but for the New Zealand series,” chairman of selectors George Bailey said.



“There’s been a lot of speculation around his place in the team.

“So I think this gives him a little bit of space and clears up a bit of conjecture as we work through the next round of (Sheffield) Shield cricket.”

Marnus Labuschagne, who at one stage was the world’s top-ranked batter, had a tortured tour of South Africa, where his highest score was 39.

Left the door open

The 32-year-old has not scored a century since the 2023 Ashes series against England, but Bailey left the door open for a recall if he again finds form in the domestic red-ball competition.

“It’s still possible, absolutely,” he said.

“And I think we all know how good and how effective Marnus can be at his best. But that performance hasn’t been there.



“But I don’t think we’ve ever ruled anyone out permanently … and that’s no different in this case.”

The first Test against New Zealand starts on December 9 in Perth with the squad set to be named after the next round of Shield action, which begins on Wednesday.

With Marnus Labuschagne gone, the question is who replaces him, with Steve Smith tipped to move up from four to three.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Disgraced comedian Russell Brand to learn his fate
World.content:
British comedian and TV star Russell Brand, who became a household name in the 2000s as a sex-obsessed provocateur, will find out on Monday how long he will spend in jail, after he was convicted of rape and sexual assaults.

Brand’s conviction last week marked the final blow in a scandal-hit showbiz career that saw him embody the anything-goes culture of 2000s British TV and radio.

‘Significant custodial term’

On Monday, he will be sentenced at London’s Southwark Crown Court, where he was told by the judge he faced a “significant custodial term” after being found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults against four women, committed between 2004 and 2009.



The maximum sentence in the UK for rape is life imprisonment.

Russell Brand, 51, who was cleared of two other alleged rapes and one count of attempted indecent assault, was remanded in custody and spent the weekend in a cell.

He is facing further investigations after London’s Metropolitan Police said it was probing rape allegations by two more women.



From Channel 4 to MTV and an eponymous primetime show on BBC Radio 2, the wild-haired comedian passed through major British media houses in the 2000s, where his obsession with sex contributed to his notoriety.

That behaviour was also a feature of the high-profile trial, with Brand admitting that he had been “extremely promiscuous” and had used his fame to “facilitate sexual access”, although he denied the charges.

He was accompanied to court most days by his wife Laura Gallacher, with whom he has three children.



Calling him a “wonderful father to our children”, Gallacher told the jury that when they first dated in 2006: “It was clear it was difficult for him to be monogamous.”

She said she was “very aware” of Brand’s promiscuity, as “you could read about it regularly in the papers”.

‘Shapeshifter’

Russell Brand’s hypersexualised persona was a running joke in tabloids, with the comedian named “shagger of the year” three years in a row by The Sun newspaper from 2006-2009.



“He’s a bit of a shapeshifter,” then-showbiz editor of The Sun, Gordon Smart told Channel 4. “He would present to you as he thought appropriate, quite chameleon-like.”

Born to working-class parents in Essex, east of London in 1975, Brand dropped out of drama school before joining MTV at the age of 25.

He was fired for turning up to work dressed as Osama bin Laden following the 9/11 terror attacks and for inviting his drug dealer into the studios.



He went on to have his own radio show at the BBC, which last week apologised for the “culture and failings” when Brand was part of the organisation between 2006 and 2008.

Brand left the BBC amid controversy for sending a well-known actor sexually explicit messages about having slept with their granddaughter.

He later made a foray into Hollywood after a brief marriage in 2010 to US pop star Katy Perry, followed by a stint as a left-wing commentator and campaigner.



In television and stage appearances throughout this time, Brand joked about his predatory behaviour and made crude comments often at the expense of younger women and staff.

A 2023 investigation by Channel 4, The Sunday Times and The Times aired accusations of rape and sexual assault, sparking a police investigation.

‘Wake-up call’

On Thursday, Russell Brand was found guilty of sexual assaults against an MTV worker, a Channel 4 worker and a Capital Radio employee, as well as raping a 21-year-old fan.



The organisations that propped up Brand for years despite complaints are now facing questions about why he was allowed to continue for so long.

British culture minister Lisa Nandy said men in power were still exploiting young women in the media industry.

“Hand on heart, I don’t think we can say that this couldn’t happen today,” Nandy told Sky News on Sunday.



“In fact, I would wager that this is probably happening today.”

“I’m asking media and entertainment organisations now to step up and really treat this as the wake-up call that it has to be,” she added.

In recent years, Brand has reinvented himself as a faith-based, conservative commentator to millions of social media followers.



In 2024, he became a Christian after being baptised in the River Thames. Brand carried a copy of the Bible with him to court through the three-week trial, repeatedly telling reporters he was “blessed”.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Mosimane vs McCarthy: What Bafana Bafana vs Kenya means
World.content:
Pitso Mosimane and Benni McCarthy are under different kinds of pressure heading into Bafana Bafana vs Kenya this month. Image: Bafana Bafana, Harambee Stars (X).

In four days, Bafana Bafana continue their AFCON 2027 qualifying journey.

South Africa host Kenya on 13 November, followed by the return leg next week.

Coaches Pitso Mosimane and Benni McCarthy are set for a crucial tactical battle.



AFCON qualifiers: Where Bafana Bafana stands

South Africa are leading Group D with full points from two games played so far, according to CAF.

Guinea are second with one win, followed by Kenya and Eritrea, respectively.

However, the Harambee Stars have already secured a place in the main tournament as the co-hosts.

This means Guinea, Eritrea, and South Africa are fighting for the one remaining spot.

Bafana Bafana could all but secure that place with wins against Kenya this month.

They face the Harambee Stars on 13 November at the Orlando Stadium, kicking off at 18:00.



The return leg is on 17 November, and SAFA still lists the fixture details as “to be confirmed”.

The qualifiers wrap up in March next year with the final round of fixtures.

Bafana Bafana coach Pitso Mosimane has announced his squad for this month’s back-to-back 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Kenya. SA will host the Kenyans at Orlando Amstel Arena in Johannesburg on Friday, 13 November 2026 before traveling to Nairobi for the second… pic.twitter.com/b0TeY4sx9H — Bafana Bafana (@BafanaBafana) November 5, 2026

Mosimane chasing redemption, McCarthy in danger

The two coaches find themselves in starkly different positions so far.

Mosimane took over as Bafana Bafana coach in September, as confirmed by SAFA.

He replaced Hugo Broos, who had led South Africa to the 2026 FIFA World Cup Round of 32.

Mosimane has hit the ground running in his second stint as national coach.

In the AFCON 2027 qualifiers, Bafana Bafana defeated Guinea 2-1, then hammered Eritrea 5-0.

South Africa also got the better of Egypt in their friendly in Cairo in October.

Meanwhile, McCarthy could find himself out of a job if things go south against Bafana Bafana.

He took over from caretaker coach Francis Kimanzi in 2025 and is still facing criticism.

McCarthy’s record as Kenya’s national coach is eight wins, five draws, and eight losses, according to Transfermarkt.

This includes a draw against Eritrea and a loss to Guinea in the AFCON qualifiers.

Despite Kenya’s confirmed place at AFCON 2027, pressure is mounting for the South African tactician to see the Harambee Stars on a winning path.

MOSIMANE DOWNPLAYS EDGE FOR EITHER COACH

Some believe the Mosimane vs McCarthy battle comes down to familiarity.

However, the Bafana Bafana coach does not believe their past gives either the edge.

They had a player-coach relationship during Mosimane’s first stint as Bafana Bafana handler.

They have also faced each other as opposition coaches in the Premier Soccer League.

Mosimane does not believe these interactions are a genuine factor, according to Africa Soccer:

“It doesn’t mean that when I know an opponent, I have an advantage. No, it just gives me a little bit of data, and I understand certain patterns and what is most likely to happen.”

World.title: New Durban shopping mall set for April 2027 opening
World.content:
One of Durban's busiest residential areas is getting a major retail development, with construction plans moving ahead. Image: AJ Property Holdings

Ntuzuma is set for a major retail development, with a new shopping centre planned to bring several well-known national retailers to the Durban township.

The R388 million project, known as Ntuzuma Junction, is being developed by Exemplar Retail and AJ Property Holdings, with an opening targeted for April 2027.

Which stores are coming to Ntuzuma Junction?

The shopping centre will be anchored by two major grocery retailers, Boxer and Shoprite, giving residents access to everyday essentials under one roof.



Other retailers expected to open at the centre include:

Clicks,

Foschini,

Pep,

KFC,

McDonald’s, as well as

Three banks.

The development is also expected to include healthcare, technology, cellular and other convenience retailers.

According to the developers, the aim is to provide a mix of affordable shopping, essential services and food outlets that cater to the needs of the surrounding community.

Ntuzuma Junction is planned as a two-level shopping centre with approximately 17 000m² of retail space.

Why THE DURBAN TOWNSHIP was chosen for the development

The shopping mall will be built in Ntuzuma G, an area with a large residential population and strong demand for formal retail facilities.

The development’s research estimates that approximately 119 500 people live within its main catchment area, spread across around 29 000 households.



The area has an estimated annual per capita income of R33 100 and retail buying power of approximately R1.5 billion.

The site also benefits from its position along key local roads, with traffic volumes estimated at between 700 and 1 000 vehicles per hour.

Existing taxi and bus routes are expected to make the centre accessible to residents who rely on public transport.

When will the new shopping mall open?

Ntuzuma Junction is targeting an opening in April 2027.

The developers have indicated that municipal approvals have also been secured and that several national retailers are progressing through their approval processes.

World.title: Sundowns clash could mark Phili’s long-awaited Kaizer Chiefs return
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs could welcome back winger Langelihle Phili for their upcoming clash against Mamelodi Sundowns in the Carling Knockout Cup.

Masandawana are set to host Amakhosi in the semi-final later this month, with Phili potentially in contention to make his return.

The winger suffered a serious ankle injury during the 15 August draw against Sundowns and subsequently missed eight matches.



However, after Kaizer Chiefs’ 2-1 win over Siwelele in the Carling Knockout Cup quarter-finals, assistant coach Fernando Da Cruz said Phili had returned to training with the squad.

“[Langelihle] Phili restarted this week [last week] with the squad and has been taking part in football sessions on the field,” he told FARPost.

“So, he is close to restarting to play competitions.

“Maybe he will be ready for the semi-final; we don’t know, but we’ll work a lot with him during this FIFA [international] break for [November].”

Phili has been a joy to watch since joining Chiefs from Stellenbosch in August.

Phili to return to Kaizer Chiefs lineup

The winger scored his first goal for Amakhosi against Mamelodi Sundowns in the Betway Premiership three months ago. Unfortunately, he picked up an injury during the same match, ruling him out for several weeks.



With a two-week FIFA international break providing an opportunity to work on his fitness, Phili will be hoping to regain full match sharpness ahead of Kaizer Chiefs’ next fixture.

His potential return would be a timely boost for Amakhosi as they prepare for a crucial cup encounter against Sundowns.

Will Amakhosi get better with Phili playing?

World.title: Nine arrested in SA over alleged plans to join Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Nine foreign nationals have been arrested at OR Tambo International Airport and a hotel in Bruma in connection with an alleged attempt to travel from South Africa to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war.

According to Hawks spokesperson Katlego Mogale, the suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested on Sunday following an intelligence-driven operation.

The arrests followed a multidisciplinary investigation involving Interpol, the Hawks in Germiston, international law enforcement agencies, SAPS Crime Intelligence, the Gauteng Provincial Tracking Team and other law enforcement structures.

The suspects are expected to face charges relating to the contravention of the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act 15 of 1998.

They are expected to appear before the Kempton Park Magistrate’s Court.

World.title: LIVE | 'Cat' Matlala returns to Madlanga Commission for two days of testimony
World.content:
PRETORIA - Controversial businessman Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala is expected to return to the Madlanga Commission when public hearings resume on Monday.

His legal team and the commission’s evidence leaders had until 5pm on Sunday to submit written representations on the issues Matlala can and cannot be questioned about.

During his first appearance, Matlala refused to answer certain questions, invoking his right against self-incrimination.

He is expected to face further questioning over two days.

Matlala is at the centre of the controversial multi-million-rand Medicare24 contract and has been linked to alleged drug trafficking networks.

World.title: EFF to open criminal case against IEC over Buffalo City vote discrepancies
World.content:
KUGOMPO CITY - The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) in the Eastern Cape will open a criminal case against the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) on Monday over alleged irregularities in the counting and capturing of votes in Ward 15 in Buffalo City.

The party says discrepancies were uncovered during a recount, which resulted in an additional 97 votes being added to its tally.

According to the EFF, 39 of the additional votes were for the ward ballot, while 58 were proportional representation (PR) votes.

The party wants the Commission to account for the discrepancies and explain how the votes were initially miscounted or incorrectly captured.

World.title: Tech firms claw back some losses after midterms rout, eyes on Nvidia
World.content:
HONG KONG - Tech firms rose Monday to claw back some of last week's painful losses fuelled by AI regulation worries, though traders were keeping a wary eye on a probe into Nvidia boss Jensen Huang amid claims of an affair with a Chinese spy.

Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after Tuesday's US midterms saw Democrats sweep both houses of Congress in a rebuke to Donald Trump and his Republican party.

The results suggested voters were angry at the president's Iran war and tariffs, which have sent prices soaring, as well as a sharp kickback against the huge data centre buildout that has taken place across the country in recent years.

That has led to speculation the new Congress will seek to wind in tech firms' construction drive, which could put thousands of jobs at risk.

The uncertainty comes with traders already nervous about when the hundreds of billions of dollars pumped into the sector would actually see a profit.

After taking a lashing on Thursday, Wall Street enjoyed a little stability at the end of last week, and Asia -- which had suffered a hammering itself on Friday -- largely followed suit to start this week.

Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei -- which are heavily weighted with AI-linked tech giants -- led the advances.

The Japanese Nikkei 225 piled on more than three percent thanks to rallies in Kioxia, Tokyo Electron and Advantest, while SK hynix and Samsung piled on around three percent to push the South Korean Kospi sharply higher.

Taiwan's TSMC rocketed nearly six percent to drag the Taiex five percent higher.

There were also healthy gains in Hong Kong and Shanghai, though Sydney, Wellington and Manila edged down.

"Investors will be watching carefully this week to get a sense as to whether these gains are just short-covering, bargain hunting or the beginning of something more sustainable in nature," said Sally Auld at National Australia Bank.

"Fears around AI regulation, the outlook for (capital expenditure) and free cash flow have been the driver of risk reduction in recent weeks and these issues are not likely to be resolved with any conviction in the near term.

"Nonetheless, the valuation of many tech stocks now looks less expensive."

- Nvidia probe -

However, a little more uncertainty was injected into markets with news that Nvidia's board was launching an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot following his admission that he was unfaithful to his wife.

The New York Times reported last month that US intelligence officials concluded a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company called Megaspeed had been funnelling information to Beijing.

The executive, Alice Huang -- also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen -- developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the Times said.

Nvidia is a global leader in producing chips used to train and run AI models and one of the world's most valuable companies, and last year became the first to reach a market capitalisation of $5 trillion.

Jensen Huang is a huge figure in the AI revolution and a close informal adviser to Trump, and the Times said the Nvidia boss's extra-marital relationship could have revealed insights into Trump's thinking around AI.

Technology analyst Dan Ives, at investment bank Yorkville Ives, said the crisis will at the very least spark multiple congressional inquiries and "create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons".

"This will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally," Ives added. "This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China, which remains a key battleground issue in DC."

Investors will be keeping tabs this week on the release of fresh US inflation data, after figures Friday showed the economy created far more jobs than expected in October.

The figures will key for the Federal Reserve in determining whether or not to hike interest rates when it meets next in December, with markets saying there is an 80 percent chance of a lift.

World.title: Pakistan farmers in long fight to make German firms pay for flood damage
World.content:
ISLAMABAD - In a Pakistani village nestled in rice fields, Abdul Hafeez Khoso remembers the vast industrial zones he saw in Germany when he visited to file a pioneering climate legal case.

"They're spreading pollution: up in the sky there are no borders, it can affect anywhere," the 43-year-old said, describing areas far larger than his village of 800 people.

"This is a problem for the whole world -- that is why it should be resolved at the global level."

Khoso and 38 other farmers from Pakistan's southern Sindh province who were devastated by "apocalyptic" flooding in 2022 are suing German energy firm RWE and cement maker Heidelberg Materials in a rare bid to make big polluters pay damages for climate impacts.

The companies are being targeted not over specific operations in Pakistan, but because of their climate-warming emissions. They are headquartered in Germany, where a recent legal case opened the door to such suits.

World.title: Gauff outlasts Pegula to win group opener at WTA Finals
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS - Coco Gauff outlasted fellow American Jessica Pegula to win a tension-packed group stage opener 6-4, 6-7 (5/7), 6-2 on Sunday in the WTA Finals at Indian Wells.

Two-time major winner Gauff fell behind 5-1 in the second set but saved three set points in the 10th game and captured five games in a row to seize a 6-5 edge.

Pegula denied a Gauff match point and held in the 12th game to force a tie-breaker, then jumped to a 5-2 lead and forced a third set with a forehand return winner.

Gauff seized a 3-0 lead in the third set and dominated from there, holding in the final game to take the match after two hours and 39 minutes when Pegula swatted a backhand beyond the baseline.

"I was having a lot of fun," Gauff said. "I took a little break. First match in like a month. To play a tournament like this with no preparation is something I've never done in my career.

"I'm just really happy to get through today. It was a tough match. It was 2 1/2 hours and I feel like every point was -- I don't know if you guys were holding my breath but me too, so just happy to be through.

"I'm really proud of myself for this one."

Gauff, the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open champion, and Pegula had split 10 prior career matches, Gauff winning the Cincinnati final and a Wimbledon quarter-final this year in their most recent prior meetings.

In the other Group One opener, reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova defeated Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-4.

Noskova, a 21-year-old Czech, needed only 86 minutes to defeat Ukraine's Kostyuk.

World number one and reigning champion Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals on Saturday due to a viral illness with Kostyuk replacing her at the California hardcourt event.

Noskova improved to 3-1 against Kostyuk, all matches coming this year as both made the WTA Finals for the first time.

Noskova won in three sets at the US Open fourth round in their most recent prior meeting and in the Wimbledon semi-finals, while Kostyuk won on her way to the Madrid clay crown.

This year's WTA Finals were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia but in July were moved to Indian Wells after US military strikes on Iran in February and the subsequent war in the region.

World.title: 'Godzilla Minus Zero' stomps to the top of North America box office
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Japan's "Godzilla Minus Zero" roared to first place in the North American box office over the weekend, industry estimates showed Sunday, gobbling up $31.6 million in sales on its opening weekend.

Set in 1949 as postwar Japan looks to rebuild, the film sees a new threat emerge: A giant three-headed dragon-like monster called King Ghidorah.

Enter Godzilla -- believed defeated in the 2023 "Godzilla Minus One," but radioactively regenerated -- who takes on the three-headed beast with at least some human assistance.

"This weekend's opening takes the Japanese production to a new level -- it's nearly three times the previous opening in Dec 2023," veteran industry analyst David A. Gross wrote.

Godzilla in this making is the same iconic beast that many North American viewers know from the 1998 Sony Pictures film, but he exists in a different storyline with different producers.

Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, "Godzilla Minus Zero" is produced by Japan's Toho and distributed in North America by GKIDS.

In second place sat a far less scary beast: "The Cat in the Hat."

The legendary Dr Seuss feline brought in an estimated $20.5 million in its opening weekend in the latest instalment distributed by Warner Bros.

Gross warned that Dr Seuss films don't typically perform well outside the United States, but may be able to make up for that by earning money on streaming platforms or through television rights.

Marching into third place was Angel Studio's "Drummer Boy," which banged out $9.3 million at the box office, according to estimates by Exhibitor Relations Co.

The unique film -- a combination of historical drama and musical -- follows an American soldier and his brother during the Revolutionary war, with the brother marrying an enslaved woman and fighting for the British.

Gross said the film brought in double what would be expected of a similar film on its opening weekend.

"Angel specialises in inspirational stories and they know how to reach this audience," Gross wrote in his weekly newsletter.

Fourth place went to A24's "You Can See Everything," the biopic that follows convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes in the month before she began an 11-year prison sentence.

The film brought in about $8.9 million over the weekend, bringing its four-week total to an estimated $79.8 million.

In fifth was Sony's "Ramayana," earning about $8.7 million on its opening weekend, according to estimates.

Gross noted that it was "one of only five Indian wide releases in the US" over the last three decades.

World.title: What does it cost to run SA's local government elections?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa’s 2026 local government elections are estimated to have cost around R4.3-billion, although the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) is yet to confirm its final expenditure.

The commission told Parliament in May that it had budgeted R3.2 billion for the elections. It later indicated that it required an additional R1.1-billion.

Former IEC commissioner and executive chairperson of the Institute of Electoral Management Services in Africa, Terry Tselane, says the scale of the logistical operation involved in running an election requires substantial resources.

He says this includes investment in information and communications technology (ICT), particularly as more of the commission’s processes become automated.

“The fact that most of the aspects of the Commission are now automated would require ICT to put a lot of money into those processes,” Tselane said.

The IEC also needs to recruit and deploy thousands of electoral staff to service voting stations across the country.

World.title: Ruto brands Gachagua 'chief extortionist'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto speaking at Nyangori in Nyamira County on November 9, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a blistering attack on his former deputy, Rigathi Gachagua, branding him a “chief extortionist” and accusing him of allegedly demanding millions of shillings from businesspeople and political aspirants seeking his support.

Speaking at Nyangori in Nyamira County, the President accused Gachagua, who is now the leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), of frustrating business owners and candidates during his tenure as Deputy President.

In a strongly worded address delivered partly in Swahili, Ruto alleged that Gachagua had turned political engagements into opportunities to demand money, claiming that even securing an opportunity to address a gathering required payment.

“Wewe ndiye chief extortionist, umefukuzwa kazi kwa sababu ya extortion. Umeangaisha wafanyabiashara na extortion, umeangaisha candidate wa chama chako na extortion. Kila mtu akija kwako ni lazima atoe pesa,” Ruto said.

The President further alleged that Gachagua demanded Sh10 million from one gubernatorial aspirant and Sh20 million from another, while other candidates were allegedly required to pay varying amounts.

He also claimed that individuals seeking an opportunity to use a microphone during political meetings were required to pay Sh50,000.

“Extortionist, wewe mtu wa pesa, achana na Wakenya, endelea na extortion yako. Uli-extort wafanyabiashara eti unapigana na pombe. Wafanyabiashara hawana amani, candidates hawana amani, wananchi hawana amani kwa sababu ya extortionist. Halafu unatuambia mambo ya pesa, please shut up,” he added.

Ruto also dismissed Gachagua's repeated claims that he played a decisive role in securing his victory in the 2022 presidential election.

The Head of State questioned why the former Deputy President continued to take credit for his political rise, contrasting their respective electoral histories.

“Anazunguka kila mahali kwamba mimi ndiye nimefanya Ruto awe president. Mtu one-term MP anazunguka dunia hii yote. Mimi nimechaguliwa mara saba, wewe mara moja,” he said.

The President went further, accusing Gachagua of having excessive pride despite what he described as limited political achievements.

“Kiburi nyingi na akili kidogo. Bure kabisa. Kiburi inabebwa na gunia, chuki inabebwa na lorry,” Ruto remarked, drawing laughter from sections of the audience.

He also revisited the political process that led to Gachagua's selection as his running mate in 2022, claiming that the former Mathira MP had initially struggled to secure sufficient support from a group of leaders involved in the selection process.

Ruto alleged that during a vote involving 30 people, Gachagua received only four votes, adding that he eventually supported his candidature out of sympathy and consideration for his age.

The President further accused his former deputy of falling out with several political colleagues after being given the opportunity to serve in government.

According to Ruto, Gachagua's disagreements with other leaders eventually contributed to his political isolation and removal from office.

The remarks come amid continued political rivalry between the two leaders following Gachagua's impeachment as Deputy President in October 2024 and his subsequent establishment of DCP as a political vehicle.

Ruto also questioned the opposition's ability to provide effective leadership, arguing that disagreements among its leaders would undermine their capacity to address the concerns of ordinary Kenyans.

He dismissed the ongoing political discussions surrounding competing candidates and party arrangements, insisting that Kenyans were more interested in development plans and solutions to their everyday challenges.

“Who cares if you have one candidate or not? Hiyo ni shauri yenu. Wananchi hawa wa Kenya wanataka kujua mpango wao ni gani,” he said.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses opposition divisions as 'polygamous family' rivalry
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County on November 8, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims of divisions within the Opposition, describing the disagreements among its leaders as normal sibling rivalry in a polygamous family, while insisting that the coalition remains united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.

Gachagua said the Opposition leaders were committed to working together to challenge President William Ruto, despite their differing opinions on the timing of selecting a joint presidential flagbearer and occasional disagreements among their political camps.

Speaking during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County, the former Deputy President likened the political differences to children from the same father competing for attention but eventually uniting whenever an external threat emerges.

“The Opposition is united to a man, and we have agreed that we will have a single presidential candidate. Everybody is committed, and we talk on a daily basis. The only challenge is normal petty problems,” he said.

He added that the disagreements should not be interpreted as a breakdown of the coalition, maintaining that such differences were healthy and expected in a broad political alliance.

“Ile shida kidogo ni ya boma, watoto wengi wa baba mmoja. Watoto huko ndani, oh, baba anakupenda kuliko mimi. Mbona ulinunua kiatu kabla mimi? Si hiyo ni kawaida kwa polygamous family?” he posed.

Gachagua said the bigger threat to Opposition unity was not necessarily disagreements among its principals but the conduct of their supporters, social media influencers and political bloggers, whom he accused of fuelling unnecessary tensions through insults and online confrontations.

He cautioned Opposition leaders against allowing overzealous supporters to dictate their political relationships, warning that unchecked political attacks could eventually weaken the coalition and undermine its common objective.

“If there is anything to separate us, it is our supporters and social media bloggers. Wanawakisha moto hakuna, watu wangu na wa Matiang'i wanatukanana na sisi tunakula breakfast pamoja,” he said.

He further claimed that some political influencers associated with his DCP party had been recruited and allegedly paid by individuals opposed to him to attack his leadership and the party.

Gachagua urged coalition principals to exercise restraint and avoid reacting to every provocation from supporters, insisting that political leaders must remain focused on the bigger picture.

“I want to ask leaders in the Opposition, be careful. Don't listen to overzealous supporters and influencers; they will lead you astray. Remain focused,” he warned.

On the question of selecting a joint presidential candidate, Gachagua revealed that differences remained over the appropriate timing, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka proposing that the flagbearer be identified before December, while Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna favoured February and Narc Kenya leader Martha Karua suggested May.

Gachagua, however, argued that selecting a candidate too early could expose the individual to political pressure and possible frustration from the government.

He proposed April next year as a more suitable time, maintaining that the coalition was united on the principle of having one candidate even if its leaders differed on the timing.

The DCP leader also dismissed arguments that academic qualifications, experience or political credentials should determine who becomes the coalition's presidential candidate, insisting that electoral numbers and the support of ordinary Kenyans would ultimately decide.

“As others say they have experience and an agenda in the Opposition, the deciding factor is the numbers. I'm with the people. You say you have capacity, but the person to decide is the voter,” he said.

He added: “Akili nyingi ni nzuri, but bila kura unaweza kaa nayo nyumbani.”

World.title: Mudavadi urges Western Kenya to unite, says region cannot remain on sidelines
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi. [File, Standard]

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi has urged Western Kenya to unite ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying the region must strengthen its political representation to have a greater say in national decision-making.

Speaking during a UDA delegates' meeting in Shitoto village, Mumias East, Kakamega County, he said Western Kenya could not afford to remain on the sidelines while decisions affecting the country were being made.

"2027 is the moment we must change the narrative. We must make sure that we are at the table where decisions are made. We cannot afford to remain spectators when the future of our country and our region is being determined," he said.

Mudavadi said parliamentary influence depended on numbers, arguing that electing more MPs would give the region a stronger voice in key parliamentary committees, including the Budget Committee.

"Parliament exercises authority in its own right. We want more MPs so that we can have a say in the Budget Committee and other important committees. These positions are secured through numbers, and numbers matter when decisions affecting the country are being made," he said.

Turning to the opposition, Mudavadi described its leaders as divided and challenged them to present clear manifestos outlining what they would offer Kenyans.

He said the divisions within the opposition would work in President William Ruto's favour as he seeks re-election in 2027, expressing confidence that he would win in the first round.

"We want Ruto to win without a petition. We want to thrash them in the first round," he said.

World.title: Family identifies two security officers involved in Abshir Abdi abduction
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

LSK president Charles Kanjama leads members in a protest over the disappearance of lawyer Abshir Abdi. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The family of Nairobi lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi has identified two security officers alleged to have taken part in their kin's abduction, even as his colleagues threatened mass protests to push for his release.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) said the two names have been forwarded to the police to aid in investigations and demanded that the office of the Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, speed up the probe into the abduction.

"One is named Siad and the other is Hussein, and we want them released for investigation, arrest, prosecution, conviction, sentencing and imprisonment," said LSK.

The revelation came during a demonstration led by (LSK outside the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police and other towns yesterday .

Abshir was forcibly taken on November 1 along Muchai Road, his vehicle was pursued and intercepted by armed individuals in two vehicles before he was seized.

While state security agencies have denied holding him in custody, court filings and colleagues suggest his abduction may be connected to his professional work representing clients in high-profile cases involving senior police officers.

Furthermore, the LSK presented additional names of security personnel linked to the incident, demanding immediate legal action against Chief Inspector Vitalis Kibet, Inspector Kennedy Kimani Karanja, Siad Mohammed, Abdurahman of the Anti-Terrorism Police Unit (ATPU), and KDF officer Ali Hussein.

The leadership voiced their frustration over the state's inaction and the alarming pattern of extrajudicial actions targeting officers of the court. Representatives insisted that lawyers must be allowed to execute their duties without fear of intimidation, torture, or abduction.

"We demand that the officers involved be handed over, arrested, prosecuted, and convicted. We will stand in the courts, in the streets, and in the boardrooms until abductions come to an end," they said in a statement.

The LSK has issued a stern ultimatum to the police command, including the president, DIG Gilbert Masengeli, Inspector General Douglas Kanja, and senior commanders. If Abshir is not released safely and the identified suspects are not formally charged in court by Monday, the LSK warned it will initiate private prosecutions itself.

Furthermore, the society threatened to bring activities to a complete shutdown and demand the immediate resignation of Kanja, Masingeli and Minister for Security Kipchumba Murkomen, carrying their demonstrations to Parliament and State House if necessary.

As court proceedings continue under a habeas corpus application at the Milimani High Court, the legal fraternity remains resolute: the protest at Jogoo House is merely the beginning of an unyielding campaign for justice and the rule of law.

In Nakuru, lawyers protested within the Law Courts, calling for his production.

“It is shocking that one of our colleagues was picked and today we do not know where he is. Unless we voice our concern, there will be complete lawlessness in the country,” said LSK member Ekaterina Handa. “Our lives matter and silencing lawyers is silencing justice. we will not relent until we get justice.”

Rift Valley LSK Chair Wangari Mwangi said it was shocking that the alleged abduction was captured on CCTV.

She rubbished the narrative that the missing lawyer was involved in a crime syndicate, maintaining that he should have been arrested and charged in court. [Additional reporting by Daniel Chege]

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Trump says renewed attacks on Iran ‘highly unlikely’ if talks show progress
World.content:
President Donald Trump said on Sunday that it is “highly unlikely” he will need to order the US back to war with Iran as long as there is progress in negotiations over Tehran’s nuclear program and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, repeating his assertion five times during an interview with CNN.

“It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” Trump told CNN’s Jim Sciutto during a 20-minute phone interview, referring to Iran. “The answer is highly unlikely it’s going to be necessary. They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 percent inflation. Highly unlikely it will be necessary. I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them.”

“So it’s highly unlikely I’ll have to,” he continued. “They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.”

‘We’re ready for it’

Eight months after the war started, the two sides have been in a stalemate, with little military action or significant diplomatic progress made while oil tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz have come under Iranian attack.

The two countries and officials from Qatar, which has mediated the talks, have kept quiet about the status of their negotiations. But Iranian hardliners have seized on the results of last week’s midterm elections — fueled in part by the war’s unpopularity with US voters — as a sign of a weakened Trump presidency that would be more willing to given in to their country’s demands to be allowed to continue its nuclear program, which it says it needs for energy, and maintain control of the strait.

Iran has also struggled to sell crude oil on global markets under US sanctions, while billions of dollars in assets held in foreign banks have been frozen.

Meanwhile, the US military has begun offering a reward of up to $20 million for information on Iran’s nuclear program and has launched a task force aimed at blocking Tehran from using land routes to move advanced weapons and other materials — signs that Washington is intensifying pressure rather than easing it.

Trump, who has in the past offered mixed messages about his willingness to end the war, made clear during the interview that US forces are in position in the region if he were to give the order to strike. “We’re ready for it. I’ve got three aircraft carriers here. The other one just arrived. We have three. They’re fully locked and loaded,” he said.

The president also said that the US has identified infrastructure targets inside Iran in the event of renewed military action, including power plants and bridges. “We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour, “ he said. “They’ll all be down.”

However, he said he would prefer not to destroy Iranian infrastructure. “I don’t want to do that because essentially, it’ll take 10 years to rebuild them,” he said. “I don’t like ripping down bridges. And the hardest thing to build is a bridge. It takes years, and I’m a good builder.”

Diplomatic activity across the Middle East has increased since Tuesday’s midterm elections.

On Friday, Qatar said that Trump had called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani to discuss de-escalation, and a day earlier, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spoke with his counterparts from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Pakistan, Kuwait, Jordan, Turkey, Cyprus and Qatar.

Before leaving on Sunday for the G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a resolution in the talks did not appear to be close.

“I wouldn’t say we’re on the verge of a breakthrough,” he told reporters in Florida. “Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic.”

Depleted Iranian stockpiles

In terms of Iran’s ability to defend against new US strikes, Trump said Iran’s air defenses have been destroyed. “It’s unstoppable because they have no anti-aircraft stuff. All of their anti-aircraft is gone,” he said.

The president also provided new details on the state of Iranian missile and drone stockpiles, saying that the regime maintains 10 percent of its missile capacity and 15 percent of its drone capabilities.

“The only thing they can do is about 10 percent level — make some missiles and make some drones. Drones at about 15 percent because much of their factories are gone,” he said.

“Most likely it will not be necessary,” he repeated about the prospect of new military action. “They want to make a deal so badly.”

World.title: Ahead of peace talks, Trump suggests Ukraine will have to cede territory
World.content:
Days before US negotiators are set to lead ongoing peace and diplomatic efforts in Abu Dhabi around Russia’s years-long war in Ukraine, President Donald Trump suggested Ukraine may have to cede some of its territory to achieve peace.

“They’re gonna end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine,” Trump told “60 Minutes” in an interview that aired Sunday.

Ukraine’s territorial integrity is protected under its constitution, making a formal concession of territory illegal, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and US special envoy Steve Witkoff will be in Abu Dhabi this week for the US-led trilateral meeting between the US, Ukraine and Russia.

World.title: Seven dead and 114 Injured in al-Ayyat train collision
World.content:
The village of al-Reqqa in the al-Ayyat district of Giza Governorate witnessed a collision between two trains on Giza-Fayoum and Cairo-Aswan lines on Sunday.

The accident caused several carriages to derail, resulting in casualties and injuries.

State authorities took urgent actions to address the aftermath and transport the injured to hospitals, while the incident drew responses from both the House of Representatives and the Presidency.

Upon being notified of the accident, police commanders, executive officials, and investigative personnel arrived at the scene to oversee the situation firsthand. A security cordon was established around the area to facilitate rescue and evacuation operations.

Details of the collision

The Egyptian National Railways Authority announced a collision between train #134 (“Tahya Misr”), traveling from Giza to Fayoum, and the rear of train No. 2010, traveling from Cairo to Aswan, between the Kafr Ammar and al- Reqqa stations.

The collision resulted in several carriages derailing and passengers killed and other sustaining injuries. It also caused a disruption to train traffic along the line in both directions, toward Upper Egypt and toward the north.

The Authority said that it has dispatched emergency teams and cranes to the scene to clear the wreckage, remove the damaged carriages, and restore regular train operations along the Cairo–High Dam line in both directions.

Up to 114 Injured and 7 Dead

Minister of Health and Population, Khaled Abdel-Ghaffar, ordered that the state of readiness be raised across all healthcare facilities in the governorates of Giza and Beni Suef, and that the necessary medical care and emergency services be provided to those injured.

Seventy-two ambulances participated in the transport and evacuation operations. The total number of injured has reached 114, while the death toll stands at seven; all cases are now under the purview of the Public Prosecution.

The Ministry of Health affirmed that it is closely monitoring the health status of the injured and providing them with comprehensive medical care.

The Ministry also expressed its deepest condolences and sympathies to the families of the victims, and wished a speedy recovery to those injured.

An official source at the Ministry of Transport revealed that the driver of train No. 134, “Tahya Misr,” died following the collision with train No. 2010 (Cairo–Aswan).

Officials at the scene

As part of the response to the incident, Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir and Giza Governor Ahmed Rashed arrived at the scene.

Support for the victims, their families

Minister of Social Solidarity Maya Morsy directed the Central Administration for Social Protection to coordinate immediately with the Giza Directorate of Social Solidarity and the Egyptian Red Crescent relief team to monitor the situation and provide necessary support and relief interventions.

Investigations

Security forces established a security cordon around the site of the collision to prevent crowds from gathering and to facilitate the movement of ambulances and railway authority recovery equipment.

Authorities have begun conducting preliminary inquiries and interviewing eyewitnesses, including passengers and local residents, to determine the causes of the accident and its technical and operational circumstances.

Parliamentary inquiry

MP Sanaa al-Saeed, a member of the House of Representatives representing the Egyptian Social Democratic Party, submitted a parliamentary inquiry regarding the incident to the Speaker of the House, addressed to the Prime Minister and the Transport Minister.

The MP said that the accident raises fundamental questions concerning the efficiency of the Egyptian National Railways’ operational, control, signaling, oversight, and maintenance systems, as well as the extent to which the ministry properly adheres to safety protocols.

She added that the development of the railway sector should not be measured solely by the amount spent on purchasing trains or upgrading stations, but rather by the state’s ability to safeguard the lives of its citizens and ensure they reach their destinations safely.

Financial Regulatory Authority

The Chairman of the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Islam Azzam directed the “Insurance Pool for Railway and Metro Accident Risks” to expedite the necessary procedures for disbursing compensation to the families of the victims of this tragic accident.

He further ordered an exceptional increase in the compensation amount—from LE 30,000 to LE 50,000—for cases of death or permanent total disability.

Sisi yntervenes

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi announced that he is closely monitoring the aftermath of the train collision in Giza. He expressed his deepest condolences and sympathy to the families of the victims and wished a speedy recovery to all those injured.

Sisi added that he has instructed state authorities to provide the necessary medical care to the injured, to conduct an urgent investigation into the circumstances of the accident, and to hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Moderate weather expected in Egypt for Monday, cold by the evening
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) anticipates relatively moderate temperatures to persist during the day on Monday, followed by a noticeable drop at night and in the early morning, resulting in cool to cold conditions across most parts of the country.

While the weather remains moderate during the day in most regions, it tends to be hot in the governorates of southern Upper Egypt, which record the highest temperatures nationwide.

Temperatures will fall further as the sun sets, making the chill more pronounced during the late night and early morning hours.

Forecasts indicate the possibility of light rain in scattered areas along the northern coast and the northern Lower Egypt, occurring intermittently.

Additionally, winds may occasionally pick up in several regions.

These weather conditions are part of the rapid shifts typically seen on weather maps during the autumn season, as temperatures continue to gradually decline across most areas.

Mediterranean Sea conditions will range from moderate to rough, with wave heights between two and three meters; winds will be northwesterly.

Red Sea conditions will also range from moderate to rough, with wave heights between 1.5 and 2.5 meters; winds will be northwestern.

Temperatures expected for Monday:

Matrouh: 22C

Alexandria: 23C

Cairo: 24C

Luxor: 27C

Aswan: 28C

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egyptian National Team’s new coach Ali Maher announces his coaching staff
World.content:
The head coach of the Egyptian national team, Ali Maher, announced his new coaching staff following his appointment to the role, succeeding Hossam Hassan.

As announced by the Egyptian Football Association on Sunday, Ali Maher’s coaching staff is as follows:

Mohamed Abdel-Karim serves as general coach, Bassem Ali as assistant coach, and Mostafa Fathy as goalkeeping coach.

Mahmoud Selim and Abdel-Rahman al-Zoghby will act as performance analysts, while Diego Giacchino and Wael Raafat will oversee physical conditioning and load planning.

The Egyptian national team is set to enter a closed training camp this November in preparation for two matches against Malawi, which will take place during the third and fourth rounds of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

World.title: How the rejection of Trump produced a biblical downpour on Republicans
World.content:
From the weakest to the strongest Republican candidates, from purple to ruby-red terrain, hardly anyone in the GOP escaped untouched by last week’s ferocious roar from American voters.

It was a night when, to paraphrase the Bible, the electoral rain fell on the just and the unjust alike.

Tactical campaign decisions and financial advantages, or even candidate quality cannot explain movement of this magnitude and consistency; change this big flows only from a current broad and deep enough to cut through the entire country.

That current wasn’t hard to identity: towering discontent with President Donald Trump’s tumultuous second term.

In the Voter Poll conducted by SSRS for CNN and a consortium of other news organizations, as of the Friday after the elections, just 37 percent of voters approved of Trump’s performance as president, while 63 percent disapproved. That was a significantly greater level of disapproval than Trump faced in 2018 — or that Barack Obama in 2010, George W. Bush in 2006 and Bill Clinton in 1994 confronted in midterm elections that also routed their parties.

As the veteran Democratic pollster Celinda Lake told me in October, across her more than four decades in politics, Trump is now facing “the broadest sense we’ve had that a president has failed. It is broader than it was in 2018 for him, or even for George W. Bush in 2006.”

That wave of discontent surged over the walls that Republican had hoped would contain it — their advantages in money and the map of states and districts being contested.

Democrats made dramatic breakthroughs in House, Senate, governor and state legislative races in every region. Voter polls showed them recording significant gains among the big voter groups that moved toward Trump in 2024 — including Latinos and young adults — while also improving among the electorate’s key swing groups (such as independents and college-educated White men) and benefiting from robust turnout among their traditional core supporters. Democrats seized multiple Senate seats in states that had only elected Republicans for decades.

Unusually strong Democratic candidates (such as Senate victors Adam Hamilton in Kansas and James Talarico in Texas, or House winners Cait Conley in New York and Bobby Pulido in Texas) and unusually weak Republican candidates (including losing Senate nominees Roger Marshall in Kansas, Darline Graham in South Carolina and Ken Paxton in Texas) help explain some of those seismic shifts.

But Democrats won plenty of races with only average candidates, and undeniably talented Republicans like New York’s Mike Lawler, Pennsylvania’s Brian Fitzpatrick and Iowa’s Ashley Hinson were swept away with the laggards, too. The problem for those Republicans was that the name on the back of the jersey didn’t matter as much to furious voters as the red color of the front.

The impact of that consensus was immediately evident in every race and every county that we flagged as markers for how the election might go.

The early signals

Residents vote in the midterm elections at the Old Stone School in Hillsboro, Virginia, on Tuesday. John McDonnell/AP

The headwinds facing Republicans were clear in two of the East Coast states we thought would provide the best early gauge of how high the wave would grow. In the VA-2 House race, Democrat Elaine Luria comfortably ousted Republican Jen Kiggans in a contest that showed the party on track for a solid night. Democrat Shannon Taylor narrowly edged Republican Rob Wittman in VA-1, a district Trump carried by 5 points in 2024. That was an early sign that the wave was reaching deeper into Republican territory.

In Pennsylvania, Democrats comfortably flipped seats at each level of difficulty. Double-digit wins for Democrat Bob Brooks against Republican Rep. Ryan Mackenzie in PA-7 and Janelle Stelson over Republican Rep. Scott Perry in PA-10 showed dramatic movement in two seats Trump won by 5 points or less. Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti’s nearly 9-point victory over Republican Rob Bresnahan in PA-8, a blue-collar northeastern Pennsylvania district Trump carried by 9 points, was an early sign of deeper distress for the GOP.

Most striking was Democrat Bob Harvie’s comfortable 5-point victory over Brian Fitzpatrick, who had defied all previous efforts to dislodge him from PA-1, a suburban Philadelphia district that usually voted blue for president. That was an early marker that even Republicans who had tried to build a reputation somewhat independent of Trump could not survive the powerful undertow of discontent with his second term.

The same message was evident in Democrat Rebecca Bennett’s resounding double-digit win over Republican Tom Kean Jr. in NJ-7 and Conley’s solid 4-point victory over Lawler, a skilled and tenacious opponent, in the NY-17 seat stretching from affluent Westchester County into the Hudson Valley.

Democratic candidate for Senate Troy Jackson greets some of his canvassers in Portland, Maine, on Tuesday. Jackson would go on to defeat incumbent Sen. Susan Collins. Hilary Swift for CNN

But the force of the Trump undertow that would define the night first became fully apparent in the fall of Republican Sen. Susan Collins in Maine.
