Skip next section Ousted Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport in sign of return from India exile

11/09/2026 November 9, 2026 Ousted Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport in sign of return from India exile

Hasina had earlier said that she wants to return to Bangladesh in December at any cost Image: Mohammad Ponir Hossain/REUTERS

Former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been in a self-imposed exile in India since her 2024 ouster, has requested a new passport and identity card to facilitate her planned return to Bangladesh, reports said Monday.

Lawyers at London-based firm Matrix Chambers, representing Hasina, have reportedly written to Bangladesh’s embassy in New Delhi, seeking the fresh documents.

"In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to ​issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," Reuters cited the letter addressed to the diplomatic mission as saying.

The letter urged for the applications to be processed “expeditiously” on the basis of Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with “obligations arising under international human rights instruments."

The Bangladeshi government, however, said it does not provide "passport to a terrorist."

Hasina had earlier said that she wants to return to Bangladesh — where she has been sentenced to death in absentia for ordering a deadly crackdown on the 2024 student-led uprising — in December at any cost.

Bangladesh’s government has been seeking her extradition from India.

"She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with ⁠India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told ​the media.

The ties between between the two South Asian neighbors took a hit after Hasina resigned and fled to India aboard a military helicopter amid deadly mass protests against her government.

World.title: Krakow mass shooting suspect has died in hospital, police in Poland say
World.content:
The alleged gunman who killed six people in a shooting spree in the Polish city of Krakow has died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police, authorities say.

The alleged shooter who went on a shooting rampage in the Polish city of Krakow on Saturday has died two days after being critically wounded by officers, police said on Monday.

"We inform you that the perpetrator of the tragic events died this morning in the hospital," regional police said in a post on X.

The man drove past the square in Krakow's Old Town, an area of Poland's second-largest city visited by many tourists, and carried out the shooting. He continued shooting even after suffering wounds by police officers, according to the authorities.

He is also suspected of killing his parents and sister at his family home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles), before carrying out the alleged attack in central Krakow.

Six people were killed and 15 wounded in the shooting spree by the 24-year-old Polish man who allegedly carried out the attack.

The victims were of various nationalities. Three women and one man were Polish, with two other victims being an Austrian woman and a British man. The list of people injured includes people from Britain, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria.

The two officers who stopped the assailant also remained in hospital.

Poland in mourning

The shooting is being investigated as a terrorist offense. While Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the assailant held radical and ultranationalist views, no information has been given as to whether he was a member of any extremist organization.

Grief and shock took over Poland after the shooting.

The attack's site at the city's central square became a place of commemoration as many people laid candles and flowers.

The St. Mary's Trumpet Call, the melody played at Krakow's Main Square every hour, stopped in honor of the victims. This was the first time this happened since World War II. The St. Anne's Church received a wave of mourners who came to attend a service for the victims.

Mass shootings are not common in Poland. Some 411,000 hold gun permits across the country, with interest in gun ownership being on the rise.

World.title: US President Donald Trump says deportation policy was 'too tough' for voters
World.content:
Trump said his deportation policy may be one of the reasons the Republicans lost so much ground in the midterm elections.

US President Donald Trump on Sunday said that his deportation policy for undocumented immigrants was "too tough" for voters and he can work with the Democrats in the new Congress to craft an immigration deal.

Speaking during his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm election, Trump said his deportation policy may have been part of the reason Republicans lost.

"I think it was too tough," Trump said. "I think it might be too tough, yeah. And a lot of people would say that it’s great. But a lot of people think it’s too tough."

In his interview to CBS that aired on Sunday, Trump said that he can find a way to work with the Democrats.

"The deal would be we would work something out. And I think it's something — I think that's something that's actually doable," he said in the interview.

Trump did not share the details of what the immigration deal would look like but shortly after the interview he appointed Stephen Miller, who designed the Trump administration's hardline deportation policy, as his chief of staff.

When ICE comes knocking: the fight against Trump's deportations To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In his tenure, Trump's administration has aggressively pushed to deport millions of undocumented migrants which drew widespread criticism.

Trump 'only kidding' about Dana White press secretary job offer

Trump said he was just joking about making Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White his next White House press secretary.

"I was only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump told reporters.

In a social media post Saturday, Trump implored White to accept his offer, writing, "Dana, please take the job!" and calling him a "violent fighter and warrior."

White is a long-time friend of Trump. He has maintained silence on Trump's remarks, saying that he would "have more to talk about" after meeting with Trump on Monday.

The position of the press secretary has been vacant since Katie Zacharia left on October 16 after less than a week on the job.

Trump to meet Xi, Putin to end Iran war

Trump on Sunday said that he will be meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin ‌at an ⁠APEC ⁠leaders' summit in China next week to discuss ending the Iran war.

Before flying back to Washington from Florida, Trump while speaking to the media said: "One of the meetings, I think, will be with ‌President Putin and President Xi, and that'll be ‌interesting. ​We're talking a lot of things, including denuclearization, but we'll be talking a lot of things. We're trying to end the ​war in Iran."

Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran if no deal is reached To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Russia in October has said that this first of its kind trilateral meeting is "being prepared."

While Trump has mentioned denuclearization as the focus of the meeting, a Wall Street Journal report said that Putin wanted the three-way talks to broker a peace deal to end Russia's war in Ukraine.

In his interview with CBS Trump said that "I believe we're very close to ⁠making a ​deal" to end the Russia-Ukraine war that would result in a "little bit different shape Ukraine," without sharing any further details.

World.title: G7 ministers meet as Europe seeks greater say in Ukraine peace talks
World.content:
With Washington preparing negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv, European leaders fear Ukraine could face pressure to accept a bad deal. Iran tensions and the threat of renewed US strikes are also on the agenda.

Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven (G7) leading industrialized nations are set to meet in Paris on Monday and Tuesday for talks on how Europe can be part of US efforts to end Russia’s war on Ukraine and how to urge Washington to not resume military action against Iran.

The meeting will bring together leading diplomats from Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.

It coincides with US-mediated talks between Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi scheduled to begin on Tuesday.

European governments are concerned the US might be pushing Ukraine to a settlement favoring Russia. US President Donald Trump, in the run-up to the Abu Dhabi talks, said a "very big" deal was in the making, suggesting Ukraine could emerge from a settlement with altered ‌borders.

"I think we're gonna have it done, and I think it's ‌gonna happen ​and they're gonna end up with a little bit different shape Ukraine," Trump told broadcaster CBS. The US president also said the deal would involve all of Europe.

European leaders fear that Putin may have too much influence over the Trump administration Image: Dmitry Azarov/Kommersant Photo/Sipa USA/picture alliance

Europe insists it's at the table

About the talks in Abu Dhabi, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio that "Europeans will be represented and France will participate in these talks."

European leaders have long insisted that any deal to end the war should include the continent's participation in the talks and that any settlement should not come at the expense of Ukraine's sovereignty.

When asked about the US plans for a possible agreement to end the war in Ukraine, Barrot said he did not know the details but stressed that no deal affecting the European security architecture could be done without the Europeans.

Particular attention at the upcoming meeting will be on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio who will attend both days unlike the last G7 meeting where he came only for one.

Rubio suggested that recent discussions had made progress on security guarantees for Ukraine and the wider European region. Trump's envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner has also described US efforts to develop a broader European security framework.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has in the past expressed doubts over proposals for a new European security framework, suggesting that any such debates should follow, rather than precede, efforts to end the war.

What Trump’s Russia talks could cost Europe To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

US strategy on Iran remains unclear

The G7 ministers are also expected to discuss US tensions with Iran, as Trump has not ruled out additional military strikes against the country.

Washington has previously considered targeting suspected nuclear facilities, including the site known as Pickaxe Mountain, following the US midterm elections last week. Tehran denies that the location is a nuclear facility.

European governments are seeking a diplomatic resolution rather than a resumption of military action. Global attention is particularly on the restoration of normal shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical route for international energy supplies.

Trump recently said that Iranian officials were keen to reach an agreement, suggesting negotiations remained possible.

The Paris gathering is among the final major diplomatic events of France's G7 presidency. The United States is scheduled to assume the group's rotating presidency in 2027.

World.title: Pope Leo urges Argentina's Milei to put people before the economy
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has urged Argentina to protect democracy and ensure economic growth benefits the poor, delivering a message to President Javier Milei over austerity, social welfare and political divisions.

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday, urging to protect democracy and ensure economic growth benefits the poor.

The pope's remarks were widely watched for criticism of President Javier Milei's harsh austerity programs and cuts affecting social services.

While Leo did not address the government's policies directly, he said "the economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy."

Talking to Milei and other government officials, he pointed to the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."

With regards to democracy, he said it was "part of Argentina's heritage that needs to be safeguarded."

The visit to Buenos Aires marks the second leg of the pope's South America tour and is the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly 40 years.

The 71-year old pontiff, who underwent surgery for lung cancer less than a month ago, arrived from Uruguay and is scheduled to visit several cities in the Catholic-majority country before continuing to Peru on Wednesday.

People were excited about the first papal visit in almost 40 years Image: Tomas Cuesta/AFP

Milei's rocky relationship with the Catholic Church

Milei's policies have in the past drawn strong criticism from Argentina's Catholic Church, particularly cuts affecting social services, pensions, disability assistance and public universities.

The Argentine leader, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has defended his aggressive spending cuts as necessary to stabilize the country's ailing economy and curb inflation.

Annual inflation has fallen from more than 200% to approximately 33% under his administration, but households continue to face financial pressure, and there's been anger over public-sector layoffs and business closures.

In the past, he agressively dismissed criticsm from the Catholic Church, going as far as calling Leo's predecessor, Pope Francis, an "imbecile." He had later though softened his tone and met with Francis in Rome.

On Sunday, Milei struck a significantly more conciliatory note, praising Francis as an "exceptional figure" and the "most important Argentine in history."

Safeguarding democracy

Pope Leo also stressed the need to safeguard democracy in the country.

"Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community."

The pope's words carry particular significance ahead of Argentina's presidential election in 2027, in which Milei has said he will seek another term.

The president's aggressive rhetoric and frequent attacks on journalists and political opponents are widely seen as part of an increasing political polarization in the country.

Leo told Milei that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."

His visit marks the first time a pope has traveled to Argentina since John Paul II's trip in 1987. It also brings renewed attention to the legacy of Francis, the country's first pope, who died in April 2025 without returning to his homeland during his 12-year papacy.

World.title: Nvidia CEO Huang admits affair amid rumors of China spy ties
World.content:
Following reports of Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang becoming involved with a Chinese spy, Huang offered an apology for cheating on his wife. Meanwhile, the US tech company pledged to investigate the alleged espionage.

US tech giant Nvidia said on Sunday it would investigate claims that its CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by "foreign intelligence efforts."

Multiple media outlets, including The Financial Times, recently reported on American intelligence sharing information on Huang's extramarital affair with a Chinese woman. The woman, according to US intelligence sources, had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.

Chipmaker NVIDIA profits up, despite trade war challenges To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The reports identified her as an executive for Singapore-based company Megaspeed. The US is investigating the company over suspicions that it was helping Beijing bypass export restrictions and obtain cutting-edge AI chips. According to The New York Times, the company has bought Nvidia chips worth billions of dollars in the last two years.

US lawmakers have invited the Nvidia chief to brief them on the reports.

Nvidia's Huang as rich as Warren Buffet

On Sunday, Nvidia's top executive admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife of 40 years.

"My actions hurt her and our children," Jensen Huang wrote in an email sent to Nvidia staff. "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Nvidia's AI PC explained: AI agents, speed and data privacy To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

He also said he was he committed to protecting the company and "supporting America's national security."

Huang was born in Taipei and spent part of his childhood in Taiwan before moving to the US. In 1993, he and two other people launched Nvidia, a company that grew to become a leading manufacturer of computer graphic cards and then an essential supplier of computer chips in the AI boom.

Nvidia's Cage for AI: can it prevent disaster? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The 63-year-old Nvidia CEO is one of the richest people in the world, according to the Forbes magazine, with his $162.2 billion (€145.5 billion) net worth as of Sunday putting him roughly on par with globally renowned investor Warren Buffet.

Huang stays on as Nvidia CEO

In their statement, Nvidia's board of directors said Huang will remain the head of the US-based company while the probe is taking place.

Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," according to their statement.

The board said a group of "independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."

At the same time, the heads of the $4.5 trillion company said they had "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

World.title: El bloque de la derecha mantiene su ventaja pero el PSOE se acerca al PP
World.content:
A tres semanas para que se abran las urnas en España, la ventaja del bloque de la derecha se muestra inalterable. La suma del PP, Vox y UPN en las elecciones generales del próximo día 29 reuniría la mitad de los votos emitidos y rebasaría los 190 escaños, más de 15 por encima de la mayoría absoluta del Congreso, según la última encuesta de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER. La mayor incertidumbre en estos momentos reside en quién será el más votado de entre los dos grandes partidos, ya que la diferencia entre PP y PSOE se ha acortado a dos puntos, dentro del margen de error del sondeo. Los socialistas experimentan un importante avance, pese a la catástrofe ferroviaria de Urda, mientras los grupos a su izquierda se sitúan bajo mínimos.

La encuesta —cuyos datos internos pueden consultarse en las webs de ambos medios— se realizó los pasados días 2 al 4, en plena conmoción nacional y debate político sobre el trágico choque de dos trenes en la línea del AVE Madrid-Sevilla, con 69 víctimas mortales. El tramo final del trabajo de 40dB. —con 2.000 entrevistas en línea— coincidió con las horas posteriores a la dimisión del ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente. Esta primera prospección demoscópica apunta a que el Gobierno no parece haber sufrido impacto electoral por el gravísimo accidente ferroviario, el segundo en menos de un año. Es más, el PSOE presenta una relevante mejoría de 1,8 puntos respecto a finales de octubre, el PP sigue en los mismos números y Vox cede casi un punto.

Más allá de esos últimos movimientos, la ventaja del bloque de la derecha continúa siendo muy holgada, gracias al crecimiento de Vox a lo largo de la legislatura. El partido de Santiago Abascal aumentaría 5,6 puntos respecto a 2023 y casi duplicaría su número de escaños, al pasar de 33 a 61. El PP permanecería como primera fuerza, pero con una presencia algo menor que en el anterior Congreso. Restaría más de un punto para situarse en el 31,9% de los sufragios, que le reportarían 129 escaños, ocho menos que hasta ahora.

Esas cifras se explican por los trasvases en el electorado de la derecha, con fugas hacia Vox que pueden alcanzar el 15% de quienes habían votado al PP (1,2 millones en términos absolutos). Entre las preferencias para presidente del Gobierno, el líder popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, prácticamente empata con Abascal: lo señalan el 20% de los entrevistados, solo dos décimas más que al máximo dirigente de la extrema derecha.

Uno de los objetivos proclamados por el PSOE para el 29-N es situarse como primera fuerza política, aun en el caso de que perdiese el Gobierno. La hipótesis no es descartable, a tenor del trabajo de 40dB. Los socialistas sufren la desafección en favor del PP del 6,5% de sus votantes (sobre medio millón), pero captan uno de cada cuatro que habían apoyado a Sumar en 2023, mejoran su valoración entre los que se declaran de centro y aún tendrían margen para movilizar a potenciales seguidores. Entre el electorado de los principales partidos, el del PSOE es el que se declara menos decidido a votar. Lo asegura el 68%, casi siete puntos menos que en el caso de los populares. De hecho, pese a sus recientes avances, el partido de Pedro Sánchez aún está casi dos puntos por debajo de sus resultados de julio de 2023 y, según este sondeo, perdería dos de sus 121 diputados actuales.

Sánchez encabeza las preferencias para presidente del Gobierno, con un 30% de respaldo. No solo es el favorito entre los votantes socialistas y de las formaciones soberanistas, sino también entre los del Frente Amplio, cuya candidata, Ada Colau, apenas recoge el 4,4% en el conjunto de la población, casi igualada con Irene Montero, de Podemos.

La resistencia del PSOE coincide con la amenaza de desplome que se cierne sobre las fuerzas a su izquierda. La encuesta otorga al Frente Amplio el 5% de los votos, que se traducirían en 10 escaños frente a los 31 que Sumar sentó en el último Congreso. Podemos, tras su decisión de concurrir en solitario, corre el riesgo de quedar fuera del Parlamento: la encuesta le adjudica un raquítico 1,2% -por debajo del grupo de Alvise Pérez, que tampoco obtendría representación- al no retener más que 8 de cada 100 votantes que en 2023 apostaron por la coalición Sumar. Solo en los territorios con fuerzas soberanistas muestra pujanza ese espacio político: ERC puede pasar de 7 a 10 escaños, EH Bildu de 6 a 7, el BNG de 1 a 2 y Adelante Andalucía tendría una irrupción estelar con 3.

Por el contrario, el nacionalismo más a la derecha retrocedería de modo notable. El PNV puede perder 2 de sus 5 diputados actuales, con lo que, por primera vez desde 1978, se quedaría sin grupo parlamentario. Lo mismo le sucedería a Junts, el partido de Carles Puigdemont, que retendría solo 3 de sus 7 asientos en el Congreso recién disuelto. Coalición Canaria mantendría su único diputado, mientras UPN añadiría al suyo otro del PP tras la coalición formada por ambos en Navarra.

Fuera de la atribución de votos y escaños, la investigación demoscópica ofrece otros apuntes que refuerzan el empuje electoral de la derecha. El promedio de la autoubicación ideológica de los votantes, tradicionalmente con una ligera escora hacia el centroizquierda, se ha desplazado al centro justo, el 5 en una escala de 0 a 10. Cuando se pregunta para qué sirven las elecciones, el 41,9% contesta que “para terminar con el sanchismo”, por delante del 31% cuya motivación principal es que no gobierne la extrema derecha. La opinión bastante extendida es que ganará la derecha y eso se refleja en el estado de ánimo de sus votantes. Entre ellos priman los sentimientos positivos, como esperanza o ilusión, por contraste con la izquierda, donde se imponen la preocupación y el miedo.

Una mayoría de los entrevistados, el 42%, da por hecho que Vox formará parte del próximo Ejecutivo, una posibilidad ante la que se declaran preocupados uno de cada tres y que causa miedo a un 20%. Esa coalición de Gobierno es la preferida por el 25,4% de los españoles, un poco más de los que querrían que se repitiese la alianza de izquierdas (23%). El pacto entre PP y Vox para apoyarse mutuamente en las listas al Senado cosecha más apoyos entre los votantes de esos partidos que el suscrito con anterioridad por PSOE y Frente Amplio entre los suyos.

El cuadro se presenta más equilibrado cuando se piden valoraciones tanto del Gobierno como de la oposición. Ahí los grados de apoyo y de rechazo son casi idénticos en ambos casos: solo uno de cada cuatro les da una calificación positiva y cerca de la mitad los suspende. Apenas un 30% cree que el PP habría gestionado mejor el país y más del 50% -incluido un tercio de su electorado- comparte la idea de que ha hecho una oposición crispada con el objetivo de derribar al Gobierno.

World.title: El bienestar de las mascotas inspira a los emprendedores
World.content:
Más de 15.000 empresas se esmeran en ofrecer productos y servicios tan especializados como sorprendentes: una ‘app’ de citas caninas, tartas perrunas o relojes inteligentes para gatos

El mercado de productos y servicios enfocados a los animales de compañía crece empujado por dos fuerzas. Una brota de las necesidades reales que tienen las mascotas, que incentiva la oferta de productos de mejor calidad y más especializados. La otra nace del deseo de los dueños, o tutores, como prefieren llamarse, por mostrar su afecto. “Vivimos un cambio de mentalidad, hemos aceptado que nuestros animales necesitan tanta atención como nosotros”, destaca Alba Ciordia, fundadora de la marca de cosmética ecológica The Doog Life, que participa en un nuevo capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen, de Banco Sabadell.

La evolución hacia un cuidado más humanizado de los animales se ha visto durante mucho tiempo como una excentricidad, pero realmente resulta beneficiosa para mascotas y humanos, añade Kike Domingo, propietario de Wild Balance, una compañía valenciana especializada en alimentación natural para perros y gatos. “Es un cambio de paradigma que empieza en la comida y se extiende a otros ámbitos”, añade Domingo, que comparte el pódcast con Ciordia.

Consejos de empresario Vivimos un cambio de mentalidad. Hemos aceptado que nuestros animales tienen casi tantas necesidades como nosotros, y triunfa quien sabe verlo Alba Ciordia, fundadora de la marca de cosmética ecológica The Doog Life

Esta humanización nos hace pensar que las mascotas pueden disfrutar de las mismas actividades que los humanos, como relajarse en un spa o conocer otros congéneres, y alimentarse con comida más saludable o adaptada. Todo ello abre un camino lleno de posibilidades para los empresarios que tengan buen olfato, afirma Ignasi Solana, presidente de la Asociación Española de la Industria y el Comercio del Sector del Animal de Compañía (AEDPAC).

“Es un sector perfecto para emprender, un refugio, no una burbuja, pues la mejora en el cuidado animal es un cambio de sensibilidad en la sociedad”, defiende Solana. ¿Por dónde empezar? Lo tiene claro: “Las oportunidades se presentan en ámbitos tan diversos como la alimentación, la cosmética o la electrónica”, señala el portavoz de AEDPAC. Varios empresarios repasan los negocios más sorprendentes o con más tirón dentro de la industria que representa el 0,38% del PIB español.

La revolución en la alimentación: experiencia gourmet compartida

El interés por alimentar mejor a perros y gatos ha llevado a los fabricantes a ofrecer opciones adaptadas a las necesidades particulares de las mascotas, señala Solana. “Es el campo de mayor crecimiento porque los consumidores se preocupan más por la salud de sus animales de compañía. Hoy, existen opciones para mascotas que tienen que perder peso, para las que realizan mucha actividad física o para las que acaban de ser operadas...”, explica el portavoz de AEDPAC.

También surgen nuevas alternativas a la alimentación convencional, elaboradas a partir de ingredientes naturales y similares a los que consumen los humanos, señala Kike Domingo. Su empresa ofrece distintas opciones, como un pienso elaborado con carne y verduras que se pueden ver y oler, al que ha denominado NøPienso; comida precocinada, y la dieta BARF (por sus siglas en inglés, biologically appropriate raw food, que significa alimento crudo biológicamente apropiado), basada en materias primas crudas y frescas. Unos modelos de alimentación que, según defiende, buscan ofrecer alternativas más naturales, nutritivas y saludables para los animales.

Consejos de empresario El interés por mejorar el cuidado de sus mascotas ha crecido, pero uno de los mayores retos del sector es convencer a los consumidores de que prueben nuevos productos y servicios Kike Domingo,fundador de Wild Balance, empresa dedicada a la alimentación natural

Este interés se está reflejando en las cifras de venta del sector de la alimentación. En 2025 crecieron un 6% respecto al año anterior, de acuerdo con el último informe de la Asociación Nacional de Fabricantes de Alimentos para Animales de Compañía (ANFAAC). El estudio refleja un retroceso del pienso seco, en favor de los piensos húmedos, más jugosos, y los snacks o aperitivos, entre los que toman peso los dulces.

El campo de la repostería, indica Solana, vive un auge gracias precisamente a esa humanización en el trato a los animales. En la última década han surgido fabricantes de dulces aptos para ellos, que se venden en sus propias pastelerías. Producen galletas, bizcochos y helados, además de tartas, que cambian el azúcar y las harinas refinadas, por el yogur, la carne de pollo, de pavo y quesos como el parmesano. Estos productos, que son más saludables que los que se elaboran para humanos, no surgen como una necesidad alimenticia, sino una manera de incluir a las mascotas en las celebraciones familiares, expresarles afecto, y que puedan consumir de manera segura productos que replican los de los humanos, explica Solana.

Tecnología punta: el reloj inteligente animal para cuidar su salud

Cada vez más tutores visten a sus perros y gatos con collares y arneses electrónicos. Estos dispositivos permiten recopilar información sobre la actividad del animal, como su ubicación en cada momento, explica Laura Haesen, desarrolladora de negocio en Weenect, compañía francesa que comercializa este tipo de aparatos. “Pesan muy poco, su batería dura una semana y se pueden configurar para avisar al dueño si su mascota sale del perímetro delimitado o si se ha acercado a una zona marcada como peligrosa. Esto reduce los extravíos y los riesgos a los que se expone al animal cuando se sale de paseo o si se tiene suelto por un terreno abierto”, explica Haesen.

Alba Ciordia destaca un campo con mucho potencial dentro del ámbito de estos wearables (dispositivos tecnológicos que se visten o se llevan encima), los que miden la salud del animal. “Registran parámetros como el ritmo cardíaco, el sueño... y establecen patrones, de manera que pueden detectar cambios y ayudar al veterinario”, explica. De hecho, añade Kike Domingo, muchos fondos de inversión en Europa y Estados Unidos han puesto los ojos en las empresas que los desarrollan. Actualmente, en torno al 19% de los responsables de perros utilizan collares o arneses con GPS o con sensores para medir su actividad, de acuerdo con AEDPAC. “Yo creo ahí hay un filón”, completa el empresario.

Un tratamiento para pieles sensibles y un masaje: el spa perruno

Las peluquerías caninas se están transformando en salones de belleza con multitud de servicios. El clásico “lavado, secado y corte” está dando paso a circuitos de baño, espacios de relajación y tratamientos especiales para cabellos dañados y pieles sensibles, explica Sofia Bienes, fundadora del hotel de lujo para perros, The Dogg, en Madrid, que dispone de un concurrido spa.

“La estética canina no es nueva, pero sí que ha cambiado muchísimo la forma en la que entendemos estos servicios”, explica la empresaria. Este fenómeno se apoya en la creciente disposición de los tutores en invertir en cuidados, especialmente en razas que necesitan un mantenimiento frecuente o que padecen afecciones de la piel. Las versiones prémium de estos servicios incluyen atención a domicilio o recogida y entrega del animal, así como programas periódicos de mantenimiento.

The Dogg es un hotel con spa en el centro de Madrid que sigue la máxima de que los servicios han de adaptarse a las necesidades de cada perro y no al revés. The Dogg

Este auge va acompañado del desarrollo de una cosmética adaptada a las particularidades caninas. La dificultad para encontrar productos adecuados para la piel sensible de una de sus perras llevó a Ciordia a desarrollar fórmulas naturales junto a laboratorios cosméticos especializados. “Pensé que seguramente había muchos más perros en la misma situación y muchas familias en busca de esas alternativas, así que me lancé al mercado con un champú y una bruma hidratante para uso diario”, explica. Hoy, su marca, The Doog Life, comercializa más de 30 referencias. El de Ciordia es una muestra de la especialización de la industria cosmética animal, señala Solana. “La variedad de productos es tan grande y los envases son tan cuidados que a veces resulta casi imposible distinguirlos de los que utilizamos los humanos”, puntualiza.

Encontrar compañero de juegos (o una cita): apps para perros tímidos

La preocupación de los tutores porque sus mascotas hagan amigos ha abierto un campo nuevo en el mercado animal: las aplicaciones de citas. El objetivo principal es que muchos perros con una personalidad introvertida que tienen miedo o que viven aislados, alejados de otros de su especie, encuentren compañeros afines. “La socialización es vital para los canes, influye en su personalidad y en su salud”, explica Solana.

Existen varias plataformas en el mercado en las que los dueños pueden ayudar a sus mascotas a hacer match después de subir fotos, indicar su ubicación y explicar sus preferencias. “Son una excusa perfecta para dar con los compañeros compatibles de juegos o paseos”, puntualiza Ciordia. El valor comercial de estas plataformas reside en que permiten crear una comunidad de usuarios a los que se les ofrecen funcionalidades extra de pago. Aún es un mercado pequeño, pero al que ya se han lanzado empresarios españoles, como la gallega Dappy Dog, que ofrece otros servicios, como el seguimiento de las rutinas de los perros a través de sus paseos, su dieta y sus deposiciones, además de permitir encontrar amigos o, quién sabe, la pareja perfecta.

World.title: Un viaje en tren por Georgia a bordo de modernos vagones y reliquias soviéticas
World.content:
Georgia está llevando a cabo una modernización de su sistema ferroviario. En la imagen, un tren en dirección a Bakuriani.

El país puede atravesarse en ferrocarril desde el mar Negro hasta el Cáucaso. Este es un recorrido con inicio en Batumi y final en Tiflis

Recorrer Georgia en tren puede ser un rápido y eficiente trayecto entre el mar Negro y Tiflis o una pintoresca reminiscencia de la época soviética, en vagones destartalados y hasta recónditos pueblos de montaña. Viajar en unos u otros dependerá de la prisa y de la antelación con que uno compre sus billetes, pero, en cualquier caso, podremos visitar de forma segura los puntos más atractivos del país, con vistas que nos mantendrán pegados a la ventana. Puntualmente, para ir a los lugares más apartados, no quedará más remedio que echar mano de una marshrutka, una de esas pequeñas furgonetas que se retuercen por donde no llegan el tren ni los autobuses, a velocidades capaces de infartar al más viajero más tranquilo.

Actualmente, Georgia está llevando a cabo una modernización integral de su sistema ferroviario, que este verano alcanzó el hito de reducir el trayecto entre Batumi y Tiflis a cuatro horas. Los billetes, a partir de 35 lari (unos 12 euros), se agotan rápido en verano, por lo que es conveniente reservarlos con hasta tres semanas de antelación por internet (la web más cómoda es tkt.ge), o tener en cuenta que en las estaciones solo se acepta efectivo. Con dos frecuencias diarias (y hasta cinco en verano), es el único tren de estas características, con paradas solo en Kutaisi, Ureki y Kobuleti. Así que el resto de trayectos nos ofrecerán más margen de improvisación y requerirán mucha más paciencia (y muy poco dinero).

En nuestra ruta desde la ciudad costera de Batumi hasta el pueblecito de Gardabani, en el extremo oriental de la línea, probaremos las dos modalidades, que tan bien reflejan esa Georgia moderna con miras europeas y otra mucho más rural, entregada al paisaje y al contacto humano. La duración del viaje dependerá del tiempo que dediquemos a cada una de las ciudades en las que paramos.

Antes de arrancar, Batumi

La historia georgiana parece escrita en vertical, por colonos otomanos y persas llegados desde el sur o rusos, venidos desde el norte. Aventuras que encontraban en la cordillera del Cáucaso, la más alta de Europa, el límite a sus ambiciones imperiales y el recipiente para un legado que, todavía hoy, hace de Georgia ese crisol del que solo pueden presumir las zonas de frontera.

Sin embargo, a finales del siglo XIX, los descubrimientos de petróleo en Azerbaiyán reformularon el mapa del viajero con el ferrocarril de Transcaucasia, que unía el mar Negro y el Caspio, de Batumi hasta Bakú. Una línea internacional que, por cierto, acaba de reabrir tras seis años cerrada, pero que todavía impide a los ciudadanos de la UE cruzar la frontera azerí (una medida que Azerbaiyán reevaluará a inicios de 2027). Esas mismas vías articulan Georgia en dirección oeste-este.

Una mujer en el andén de la ciudad georgiana de Borjomi. Ryhor Bruyeu ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Por eso, nuestra ruta empieza en el suroeste del país, junto al mar Negro y en la capital de la república de Adjara, Batumi. La segunda ciudad georgiana es una extraña mezcla de historia, naturaleza y consumo desatado. Aquí, el viajero tiene la sensación de asistir a una combinación aleatoria de elementos solo unidos por la exuberancia y el exceso. Por ejemplo, desde la monumental plaza de Europa sale la calle Memed Abashidze, con galerías, cafés y tiendas, pero si uno se deja llevar un poco, hasta la plaza Batumi, es posible que sienta haberse perdido por completo, dada la arquitectura kitsch de estilo veneciano.

Ya cerca del frente marítimo, dará con un Las Vegas caucásico donde nada existe si no es cubierto de neones, y el desconcierto aumenta ante una gigante estatua de Medea, una noria más grande todavía, una torre dedicada al alfabeto georgiano, acristalados hoteles, discotecas y una playa kilométrica. Un paraíso para rusos, turcos, armenios e israelíes que encuentran aquí lo que no les ofrecen sus países: sol, calor, alcohol asequible y casinos 24 horas.

Imagen aérea de Batumi, con la plaza de la Libertad en el centro. Vladimir Zapletin ( GETTY IMAGES )

Batumi-Samtredia

Nuestro primer trayecto en tren, hacia Samtredia (dos horas), transcurre en una lenta y ruidosa sauna metálica, que sirve para recrearnos en dos de las principales virtudes del país: un paisaje que no da tregua y una hospitalidad que siempre se traduce en ritual gastronómico; en este caso, té, jachapuri y galletas que nos ofrece la familia de nuestro compartimento. Desde Samtredia, tenemos dos opciones (ambas, a poco menos de dos horas, pero con frecuencias reducidas).

La primera es dejarnos llevar por la vegetación subtropical hacia la ciudad portuaria de Poti, base para visitar los humedales del parque natural de Kolkheti, cuya biodiversidad es reconocida como patrimonio mundial por la Unesco. De nuevo, las orillas tibias y turquesas del mar Negro, cercadas por una frondosidad selvática.

La segunda opción es otro tipo de naturaleza, más salvaje, como la que se encuentra en el extremo septentrional de la línea, en la pequeña Zugdidi. Ahí comienzan las estribaciones del Cáucaso y una de las mecas europeas para el senderismo: las montañas de Svaneti. Quien quiera caminar por ellas, deberá ir desde Zugdidi hasta Mestia, y hacerlo en marshrutka. Mucho más que la escalada, los trayectos de marshrutka, impenitente adelantadora, serán el verdadero deporte de riesgo en el Cáucaso.

Panorámica de la vía de ferrocarril frente a la costa de Batumi. Ryhor Bruyeu ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Comer en Imericia

Sin embargo, seguimos en nuestro tren abarrotado y lento hacia Kutaisi, cuna de los cólquidas, dos veces capital de Georgia en la Edad Media y actualmente la principal ciudad de la región de Imericia. Referencia arqueológica y del turismo de naturaleza, acaba siéndolo también a nivel gastronómico: el jachapuri imeruli (de Imericia) es el más popular del país y acompaña cada comida. Basta con entrar a cualquier restaurante o tasca y pedir la recomendación del día para comprobar que, aquí, comer es una religión con la que comulgamos. En el restaurante Palaty encontramos la mejor cena posible, con pjali (paté vegetal), berenjena rellena, khinkali (una especie de empanadillas) de cordero y vino saperavi, especialidad de la región.

Una excursión habitual en tren desde Kutaisi es a la zona rural de Sachkhere. El servicio, inactivo entre diciembre y marzo, es uno de los más vetustos, lentos y, a la vez, espectaculares, por cómo se adentra en las montañas hasta dejarnos en la no menos alucinante Chiatura (a casi tres horas), un espectro de la extinta minería de magnesio y conocida por su sistema de teleféricos.

Edificio abandonado en Tskaltubo. Vyacheslav Saltayev ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Algo similar encontraremos en Tskaltubo. Aunque la antigua conexión ferroviaria no opera, merece la pena subirse a otra marshrutka para visitar esta ciudad-balneario, hace décadas famosa por los baños en aguas de radón y ahora como destino de turismo urbex. Es difícil imaginar una definición gráfica más explícita del auge y caída de la Unión Soviética: la propia estación de tren abandonada, las decenas de sanatorios, hoteles y balnearios, construidos en un monumental clasicismo soviético, perecen ahora entre la vegetación como esqueletos de una civilización extinta hace no tanto tiempo, y a la espera de una restauración que no acaba de consumarse. Allí, el baño nº6, el único aún operativo, conserva como un tesoro la sauna personal de Stalin.

Stalin en Gori

La memoria histórica pega un giro aún más brusco cuando el tren nos deja en Gori, en el centro del país, y a unas dos horas y media desde Kutaisi. El propio nombre (montaña, en georgiano) da una pista sobre su orografía, con un aire fresco que ventila los abundantes parques y la colina en la que se asienta la muralla del siglo VII. No obstante, Gori se asocia mucho más con las cruentas —y todavía palpables— batallas de la guerra con Rusia en 2008 y, sobre todo, con la ciudad natal de Iósif Vissariónovich Dzhugashvili; o, para entendernos, Stalin. Su figura es todavía omnipresente, pone nombre a varios lugares de la ciudad y es homenajeada en el Museo Estatal de Stalin.

Un visitante frente a un retrato de Stalin, en el museo dedicado al dictador en su ciudad natal. George Gogua ( picture alliance / Getty Images)

Lejos de un centro documental que informe sobre la vida del dictador, este complejo exalta al que fue el habitante más ilustre de Gori con un estilo rococó de vidrieras, mármol, estatuas y alfombras que le dan el tratamiento de glorioso conquistador. Los guías (la mayor parte de las visitas son en georgiano y ruso) y la colección no escatiman en halagos para quien retratan como justiciero, bardo, revolucionario e indiscutido estadista. Quizá aún le agradezcan que el centro de Gori, pese a su modesto tamaño, posea una arquitectura más propia de una gran ciudad.

Tiflis, fin del trayecto

Apenas nos quedan 70 kilómetros hasta Tiflis, una ciudad que pide hacer un alto de varios días. Joven, multicultural, nocturna, creativa, inesperada, laberíntica, bulliciosa, alegre y reivindicativa, emana la historia y la vitalidad de una capital que trasciende a un país. En ella, se hacen evidentes la diáspora rusa, las tensiones políticas georgianas, la (de nuevo) comunión en torno a la gastronomía y la voluntad de encontrar nuevas vías de expresión. Como fue el tren lo que nos trajo hasta aquí, cabe decir que las estaciones de metro no desmerecen la reputación de otras antiguas capitales soviéticas. Pero, como de lo que se trataba era de cruzar el país, nos volvemos a subir a un viejo vagón para terminar el recorrido en Gardabani, a una hora al este de la Tiflis y ya rozando la frontera con Azerbaiyán.

El puente de la Paz, en el centro de Tiflis. Mirko Kuzmanovic ( Alamy / CORDON PRESS )

Para quien prefiera emociones más fuertes, siempre quedan los viajes en marshrutka hacia Stepantsminda (la base para subir al monte Kazbegi) y la recóndita región vinícola de Kajetia, en la frontera con el Daguestán ruso.

World.title: Dutch home workers reluctant to spend more time in the office
World.content:
More than half of people who work from home would struggle to return to the office full-time because their home and working lives have become so intertwined, according to a survey for the FNV union and current affairs show Nieuwsuur.

The most common reasons for the 3,000 workers not to increase their office hours were concerns about declining productivity, more time spent commuting and a negative impact on their health and well-being.

Businesses have tried to encourage their staff to spend more time in the office since the end of the coronavirus pandemic, but none of the Netherlands’ 25 largest companies said they require their employees to leave the house five days a week.

Jelle Kajim, who works for HR support company Remote, told Nieuwsuur he valued the flexibility of working from home.

“We have 2,000 people, but we don’t have any offices,” he said. “In 10 years I’ve never worked in an office and sometimes I’m curious about it.

“I recently had to go to Paris for work, but I don’t see myself sitting in a metro train every day.”

Booking.com case

Travel website Booking.com won a court case last month against its works council, which objected to the company’s plans to compel staff to spend 40% of their contracted hours at its head office in Amsterdam.

The judge in the case remarked that it was “very normal” for people to travel to work two days a week, but only around a quarter of the company’s staff currently do so.

Other major employers said they had embraced the concept of homeworking in recent years. Just 14% of new collective bargaining agreements in 2019 made arrangements for working from home, but last year the proportion rose to 38%.

A spokesman for insurer Nationale Nederlanden said it promoted a balanced approach, with staff encouraged to spend two days a week in the office.

“The strength of working in the office lies mainly in co-operation, innovation, development and social conections. The strength of home working lies in flexibility, concentration and a good balance between work and private life,” a spokesman said.

Rabobank, which does not have a minimum office-time requirement, said: “We see no reason to set a target for presenteeism. Our experiences with hybrid working are positive.”

World.title: Foreign workers often left in the dark over EU pension rights
World.content:
People in the Netherlands who have worked in multiple EU countries have no way of knowing how much pension they’ve built up, and the country is not yet part of a European system to fix the problem, according to broadcaster NOS.

There is no single body covering all EU member states, so if you lived and worked in other countries for some time you have to remember to contact each one before retiring.

“It is incredibly complicated,” Lisa Bruggen, director of pension research institute Netspar, told NOS. You can’t simply add up the amounts you see on, for example, the Dutch and German pension portals, because they’re calculated differently.

Around 700,000 people receiving the Dutch state pension (AOW) currently get a reduced amount because they lived abroad, according to social insurance bank SVB.

Foreign workers in lower-paid sectors such as construction, hospitality and transport are most at risk of pension poverty, NOS said.

One pension fund told the broadcaster it has some 18,000 retired members who have not claimed their pension, but that privacy rules prevent it from tracing them.

An EU-backed platform, Find Your Pension, aims to show people where they have pension savings, how much they are worth, and how to claim them. The Dutch pension law must be changed before the Netherlands can join, the social affairs ministry told NOS, saying that the cabinet is working on it.

The organisation behind the platform does not expect the Netherlands to join before 2028. Even after more than a decade of work, the platform can so far retrieve personal pension information only from Belgium and France, and users say that does not always work.

World.title: Work exhaustion rising, especially among women and young people
World.content:
Exhaustion from work has been on the rise in the Netherlands for the past decade, with 21% of people saying they feel mentally fatigued at least a few times per month, according to new research by national statistics office CBS and research institute TNO. In 2015, the figure was 13%.

The findings are drawn from an annual national survey of around 57,000 people aged 15 to 74, excluding self employed. Mental fatigue was defined as feeling mentally exhausted several times per month at least, for example feeling emotionally drained or empty at the end of the day.

Women are more affected than men, the survey showed. In 2025, 24% of female employees reported fatigue, up from 14% a decade earlier. Among men, the figure rose from 13% to 18%.

Younger people are the most affected, with the 25-34 year-old age group showing the biggest rise. In 2015, 15% reported fatigue and in 2025 the number had risen to 28%. In 2023, TNO found that one in four workers aged 18 to 34 had burnout complaints.

The more complex the job, the higher the chance of mental fatigue. People in the most complex jobs, which involve highly specialised tasks and usually require a higher level of education, had a fatigue rate of 23%, compared with 18% in the least complex jobs.

Psychologists and sociologists reported the highest rate of fatigue, at 37%. The least exhausted were those working in agriculture, at only 12%.

Psychological complaints, stress and burnout were the reason for 9% of employees’ most recent sick leave, second only to flu and colds (55%). They also kept people off work the longest, at an average of 67 days, compared with 15 days for sick leave overall.

Burnout was also the most commonly reported occupational illness, with 1.9% of workers saying a doctor had diagnosed them with burnout or work-related stress. In July 2025, psychiatrists and occupational health experts called for a rethink of burnout diagnosis in the Netherlands, after Sweden dropped the term.

Two months later, the government’s health advisory council RVS warned of a “hypernervous society”, estimating the cost of mental health problems at €18 billion a year.

World.title: PSV back on top of Eredivisie as Feyenoord slump in Heerenveen
World.content:
PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”

Meerdinck penalty drama

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Valk own goal

Fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

World.title: Fog warning issued as mist engulfs north-east Netherlands
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A code yellow weather warning has been issued by the KNMI as thick fog engulfed parts of the Netherlands overnight.

The warning is for parts of Drenthe, Groningen and Overijssel, under the new regional weather warning system, which was first used on Saturday.

Fog consumed other areas over the weekend, including Utrecht, Noord-Brabant and parts of Gelderland and Zuid-Holland.

Two freight ships collided on the Maas river near Den Bosch on Saturday morning. No one was reported injured but one of the ships was badly damaged, according to Omroep Brabant.

The alert went out on Monday morning at 2am and will last until around 10am when the mist has cleared.

Road drivers are being warned to slow down and take more distance while driving. Fog reduces visibility to within 200 metres in certain places.

World.title: Organisers say 200,000 join Amsterdam rally against Gaza war
World.content:
At least 200,000 protesters joined the ongoing march in Amsterdam for the country’s fourth “Red Line” rally, demanding tougher action by the Dutch government against Israel’s war on Gaza. The estimated number comes from the rally’s organisers.

The Rights Forum along with 13 other groups, including Amnesty International, PAX and Oxfam Novib, set up the demonstration to demand the Dutch government stop buying Israeli weapons and impose sanctions on the country for war crimes.

Extra transport has been put in place, including more metros and longer NS trains to Amsterdam. Trams and buses around Museumplein are being diverted. The rally starts on Museumplein at 1pm with speeches, followed by a march through Amsterdam Zuid and Oud-West from 1.45pm to 4pm.

Previous Red Line rallies have drawn huge crowds. Organisers estimated turnout at more than 100,000 in The Hague in May 2025, 150,000 in The Hague in June 2025 and 250,000 in Amsterdam last October.

There has been some controversy in the run-up to the protest. Prime Minister Rob Jetten, who joined a previous Red Line protest as D66 leader, said at his weekly press conference on Friday that he would not be attending this one and that it would be inappropriate for him to do so now that he is prime minister.

Some of the speakers at the rally have also been accused of links to Hamas and other armed Palestinian groups. These include Omar Barghouti, co-founder of the BDS boycott movement, and Medhat Alamawi of the Palestinian Community Netherlands, who is also involved with activist group Utrecht4Palestine.

The Rights Forum spokesman Edwin van ’t Pad dismissed the criticism, telling newssite de Kanttekening: “Even if we had put the pope on stage, the right would have accused us of antisemitism and Hamas sympathies.”

It also comes at a time when the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague is coming under increasing pressure from the Trump administration. In July, Secretary of State Marco Rubio vowed to “dismantle the ICC, brick by brick, if necessary”, partly in response to the court’s investigation of Israeli officials.

World.title: Tea leaves and turmoil: a Dutch classic
World.content:
If the characters in The Tea Lords feel real, it is because they are. The grande dame of Dutch literature, Hella S. Haasse, based her internationally acclaimed magnum opus about plantation life in the Dutch East Indies on a trove of letters and documents pulled from extensive archival research.

The book follows Rudolf Kerkhoven, who finishes his studies at what is now TU Delft and moves to a remote tea plantation on Java, a place he nicknames “Eldorado”. The young man is hoping to follow in his father’s footsteps but struggles to adjust to life in Indonesia. While the venture eventually prospers, Kerkhoven’s intimate thoughts show that he does not enjoy the success.

“Never in his life had Rudolf felt such profound relief as when the Telank dropped anchor in the roadstead of Batavia,” Haasse writes.

The reader sees Kerkhoven’s struggle with the land, which can be inhospitable as well as with his wife, who has issues with fertility and with himself. The young man, 24-years old when the novel starts, is deeply anxious and concerned about his position in society and whether he is adhering to the complicated social rules of his class.

The book also follows the complicated political and social structures at the time, as well as an indepth look at the business of tea, something many of us consume frequently but think about rarely.

Like the correspondence referenced in the book, the plot moves slowly, if at all – an interesting juxtaposition to today’s instant communication.

The Tea Lords is not a compilation of letters, but rather a work loosely based on one family’s experience as plantation holders. Haasse found the Kerkhoven family documents in the Indies Tea and Family Archive, but she also drew from her own childhood. She was born in Batavia, modern-day Jakarta.

Haasse is a staple read for Dutch schoolchildren. Born in 1918, her novella Oeroeg is also set in the Dutch East Indies and was written as the gift for Dutch-language Book Week in 1948. Oeroeg is translated into English as The Black Lake and is still taught in classrooms around the country.

Nearly 50 years later, The Tea Lords was published as Heren van de thee in 1992. It was also published during Dutch Book Week and Haasse is the only author to have taken home the Book Week Prize three times.

She was also awarded the Constantijn Huygens Prize and the P. C. Hooft Award, as well as the NS Public Prize twice. She died in 2011 at the age of 93.

Nearly a decade after The Tea Lords was first published, it was translated into English by Ina Rilke. The Guardian called the work “a graceful, marvellously achieved improvisation that only a novelist of the greatest imagination and sympathy could have written.”

It’s a patient read but a fascinating look at life during an often romanticised time. You can get your copy of The Tea Lords at the American Book Center.

World.title: Cabinet sets out AI plan, seeks partners beyond US and China
World.content:
The cabinet is establishing a vision of how to integrate AI into Dutch society so as to take advantage of its benefits, control reliance on foreign powers and strengthen national security.

Digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts released 28-page vision letter to parliament on Friday, acknowledging that AI will “largely determine our future”.

“We want a Netherlands where AI makes everyone better and helps us move forward. Where a nurse has more time for patients, entrepreneurs can grow, and technology helps us with the major challenges of our time,” she said.

“That requires choices. Where do we want to lead the way and where do we draw the line? We don’t have to be able to do everything ourselves, but we do want to decide for ourselves which direction we take.”

The vision names Canada, Japan, Singapore and South Korea as “middle powers” the Netherlands wants to work with, alongside other EU member states.

It also says the Netherlands will keep working on “stable and predictable relations” with the US and China. The letter notes that the Netherlands has joined Pax Silica, a US-led partnership on chips, computing power and AI infrastructure.

The only funding figure in the vision is €120 million for Dutch participation in an EU-wide AI project, which was already set aside in September. The letter says more “targeted and structural investment” is needed in infrastructure, talent and research, but gives no amounts.

“This is a toothless tiger,” Volt leader Laurens Dassen told broadcaster NOS. “AI should be a top priority. It isn’t if there is no budget.”

Plans for computing power and datacentres, which use large amounts of electricity and water, will follow in the first quarter of 2027.

The cabinet is also exploring whether to set up a Dutch AI safety institute modelled on the UK’s AI Security Institute. An advisory report is due in December.

Aerdts and the education minister plan to agree a “media pact” with public and private media organisations, which will also cover how AI systems use journalistic content. No details on that have been given yet.

World.title: Perpetrator of Kraków terrorist attack dies of injuries in hospital
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This is a breaking news story and will be updated as further information becomes available. The man who carried out Saturday’s deadly terrorist attack in the Polish city of Kraków – and who can now be named as 24-year-old Michał Oksiński – has died in hospital. Oksiński suffered serious injuries in a firefight with two police officers, who heroically brought his rampage to an end. On Sunday, Krzysztof Klęczar, the governor of the Małopolska province in which Kraków is located, revealed that Oksiński remained in critical condition. On Monday morning, provincial police announced that “the perpetrator of the tragic events [in Kraków] died this morning in hospital”. “There was a constant struggle to save this man’s life, despite the evil he had committed,” Klęczar told broadcaster TVN after the death was confirmed. “He underwent at least three surgeries.” Informujemy, że sprawca tragicznych wydarzeń zmarł dzisiaj nad ranem w szpitalu. — Małopolska Policja (@kwpkrakow) November 9, 2026 The two police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who engaged Oksiński also suffered serious injuries, with Kulik’s condition the more critical of the two. The situation would have been much worse were it not for the fact that two leading local surgeons had, by pure chance, been eating a meal with their families in a restaurant near where the shootout took place, and provided emergency aid to the officers. There was also a huge public response to appeals for people to donate blood for Kulik, who underwent a series of surgeries. On Sunday, it was announced that both Kulik and Morański had come out of the comas they had previously been placed in. Kulik’s condition was described as “serious but stable” by Karolina Gałecka, spokeswoman for the interior ministry. CCTV footage shows the moment two police officers confront the Krakow shooter. pic.twitter.com/vcQ0Xvi1nX — WarMonitor🇺🇦🇬🇧 (@WarMonitor3) November 7, 2026 Just after 3 p.m. local time on Saturday afternoon, Oksiński drove through the historic city centre of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, including its famous market square, which was packed with tourists and locals. He fired at random from the car, killing six people. Four of those victims have been identified as Polish women, aged 47, 53 and 61, and a Polish man in his 50s. The other two were foreign nationals: a 32-year-old British man and a 51-year-old Austrian woman. A further 16 people were injured in the attack, 11 of them Polish. The interior ministry has said that, among the dead and injured are citizens of the UK, Austria, Germany, Russia and Portugal. On Saturday evening, it was announced that a search of the perpetrator’s home in the small town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski in southeast Poland, around 160 km from Krakow, had revealed three further dead bodies. They were later confirmed to belong to Oksiński’s parents, aged 53 and 52, and 21-year-old sister. Prosecutors believe Oksiński murdered them before launching his rampage in Kraków. Oksiński’s motive remains unknown. On Saturday evening, in the wake of the attacks, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński announced at a press conference that the information obtained so far indicated that the suspect had “very, very radical views” and “may have been fascinated by far-right ideologies”. However, when pressed on this claim during an interview with TVN on Sunday evening, Kierwiński refused to provide evidence, said that his remarks had referred to “initial hypotheses”, and confirmed that the potential motive was still being investigated. Poland's interior minister refuses to reveal on what basis he said the Kraków terrorist had "very radical views" and was "fascinated by the far right". "In cases like this, there are always first hypotheses, first clues. That's why I made this statement" pic.twitter.com/Wpud1FrAYM — Daniel Tilles (@danieltilles1) November 8, 2026 The incident has caused shock in Poland, where gun crime is exceedingly rare. The country has one of the lowest levels of gun ownership in Europe and has never previously suffered a mass public shooting of this kind. In response to the tragedy, a period of two days of official public mourning has been declared, with a decree to that effect signed by President Karol Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk. On Monday evening, a silent march will be held in Kraków at 8 p.m. to pay tribute to the victims. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Prosecutors launch terror investigation as Poland reels from fatal shootings
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish prosecutors have announced the opening of a terrorism investigation following Saturday’s attack in the city of Kraków, where a man opened fire from his vehicle, killing six people. Later, three further bodies – believed to be the perpetrator’s parents and sister – were found in his home. Further details have also emerged regarding the victims of the attack, the heroic actions of police and medical personnel, as well as the attacker himself – though the motive for his actions remains unknown. On Saturday, the suspected attacker, who has been named only as 24-year-old Michał O. under Polish privacy law, drove through the historic city centre of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, including its famous market square, which was packed with tourists and locals. He fired at random from the car, killing six people. Three of those victims have been identified as Polish women, aged 47, 53 and 61. Another was a 32-year-old British man. The final two victims were a foreign woman aged 51, whose nationality has not yet been announced, and a Polish man in his 50s. A further 16 people were injured in the attack, 11 of them Polish. The interior ministry has said that, among the dead and injured are citizens of the UK, Austria, Germany, Russia and Portugal. Two of the injured are police officers who pursued the attacker and engaged in a firefight with him. They and Michał O. were hospitalised with what have been described as critical injuries. Due to his ongoing medical treatment, law enforcement authorities have not yet been able to formally take the suspect into detention. CCTV footage shows the moment two police officers confront the Krakow shooter. pic.twitter.com/vcQ0Xvi1nX — WarMonitor🇺🇦🇬🇧 (@WarMonitor3) November 7, 2026 However, on Sunday morning, the National Prosecutor’s Office announced that it has launched a formal investigation into the killing of six people in Krkaów and the attempted murder of numerous others. The actions are being treated as a terrorist offence. Meanwhile, they are also investigating the killing by gunshot of three people in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, also on Saturday. That is Michał O.’s hometown, and on Saturday evening Prime Minister Donald Tusk revealed that three bodies had been found at the address where he lived. Prosecutors say that “the evidence indicates that the same person committed the acts” in both Kraków and Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski. Previously, on Saturday evening, interior minister Marcin Kierwiński announced that initial findings indicate the suspect had “very radical far-right views”. However, he cautioned that investigators were still seeking to confirm this, as well as to understand the possible motive behind the attack. Minister @MKierwinski na konferencji w Krakowie: 💬 Sprawca mógł być zafascynowany ideologiami skrajnie prawicowymi. Ten wątek będzie jednak szczegółowo weryfikowany. Czynności prowadzą funkcjonariusze @PolskaPolicja, jak i @ABW_GOV_PL – na miejscu zdarzenia oraz w domu rodzinnym… pic.twitter.com/PppmMPmWYW — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) November 7, 2026 Gun crime is exceedingly rare in Poland, which has one of the lowest levels of gun ownership in Europe. Saturday was the first time that the country has experienced a mass public shooting of this type. In response, a period of two days of official public mourning has been declared, with a decree to that effect signed by President Karol Nawrocki and Tusk. Meanwhile, political leaders have praised the heroic actions of police, especially the two officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were critically injured while bringing Michał O’s rampage to an end. “They are heroes,” said Krzysztof Klęczar, governor of the Małopolska province in which Kraków is located. “Considering how many weapons were still in the perpetrator’s car, if it weren’t for the effective and selfless intervention of these two young men, the number of victims could have been significantly higher.” It has also emerged that the police officers were treated by two leading surgeons who, by complete chance, had been eating dinner with their families at a restaurant near where the final shootout took place. One of them, Michał Pędziwiatr, a professor of surgery at the Jagiellonian University, told the media that he and fellow surgeon Mateusz Wierdak had seen the police subduing the attacker. While their families took shelter, the two doctors rushed to the scene once the shooting had finished. “Mateusz’s dedication in stopping the bleeding of the most injured police officer [Kulik] undoubtedly saved his life,” Pędziwiatr told the Fakt newspaper. Pędziwiatr himself called a local hospital that he knew would be best equipped to treat the officer so that they could prepare for his arrival. ⚫️"Tato, strzelają do ludzi!". Lekarz ujawnia kulisy zamachu Prof. Michał Pędziwiatr i dr Mateusz Wierdak byli w pobliskiej restauracji, gdy doszło do strzelaniny. Zanim przyjechały karetki, lekarze udzielili pomocy rannym. – Wyszliśmy na zewnątrz. Już się żegnaliśmy. Nagle mój… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) November 8, 2026 Public authorities in Poland, including the police and military, launched a drive for blood donations to help in the treatment of Kulik, who remains in critical condition. They said they had been overwhelmed by the number of people coming forward. The defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, also revealed that Kulik is a former soldier from the elite 6th Airborne Brigade, which is headquartered in Kraków. “The entire military community is proud of Jakub. We will support him and his loved ones,” wrote Kosiniak-Kamysz. A public fundraiser launched by Krzysztof Stanowski, a prominent media personality, has, at the time of writing, raised over 3.5 million zloty (€777,000) to support the police officers and their families. On Sunday morning, Klęczar also confirmed that Michał O. had “undergone several surgeries during the night” and “remained in critical condition”. ❗Kiedyś żołnierz 6 Brygady Powietrznodesantowej, dziś policjant i bohater- starszy posterunkowy Jakub Kulik, który wczoraj został ranny w zamachu w Krakowie potrzebuje naszego wsparcia. Ranny policjant przebywa w szpitalu. Potrzebna jest krew grupy AB Rh+. Krew można oddać… — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 8, 2026 The authorities have confirmed that Michał O. holds a firearms licence. During the incident on Saturday, he appears to have used an AR-15-style rifle, but police also found a number of other firearms in his vehicle. On Sunday morning, a shooting club in the town of Starachowice that media reports suggested had been used by Michał O. and his father issued a statement saying that the suspect “has never been trained in dynamic, tactical or combat shooting in our club”. They added that the club is fully cooperating with the authorities to provide any necessary and relevant information for the investigation. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Six killed in terrorist shooting in Polish city of Kraków
