World.title: COP31 opens as climate and geopolitical pressures mount
World.content:
Antalya – The UN’s annual climate talks kick off Monday in Turkey as rising temperatures heighten the urgency of action, with financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicating efforts to secure global cooperation.

More than 100,000 people are expected to attend COP31 in a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean seaside city of Antalya over the next two weeks.

Negotiators from nearly 200 countries are facing tough discussions over how to accelerate the energy transition and provide funds to help developing nations cope with the worsening climate emergency.

But observers say few major breakthroughs are expected as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine.

The climate emergency, meanwhile, continued to wreak havoc this year as punishing heatwaves baked Europe, wildfires raged in Indonesia and a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal.

An exceptionally strong El Nino climate phenomenon is forecast to peak later this year, adding to extreme weather and possibly helping to make 2026 or 2027 the hottest year on record.

The outlook is bleak: the United Nations warned in September that global temperatures were on course to exceed 1.5C above preindustrial levels, breaching the most ambitious threshold set by the Paris Agreement.

“Global leaders must pull us back from the brink and commit to rapidly transitioning away from fossil fuels and expanding renewable energy, an imperative reinforced by the current energy affordability crisis,” said Rachel Cleetus, climate programme director at the Union of Concerned Scientists.

– ‘Clean’ electrification? –

Turkey is presiding over COP31, with Australia leading negotiations under an unusual arrangement that settled a dispute over who would host the conference.

The partners have branded the summit as the “implementation COP”, focusing on turning commitments into concrete action after years of pledges and ambitious announcements.

Turkey is promoting an “action agenda” alongside the formal negotiations that encourages countries to support non-binding pledges on issues from artificial intelligence to waste management.

Its centrepiece is an “electrification” drive to raise the share of global energy demand met by electricity from around 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035.

But the initiative could become a source of friction.

The European Union has called for “clean” electrification, a term that could spark debate over the role of fossil fuels in the Turkish proposal.

Countries committed to transition away from fossil fuels in a landmark pact at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 but have struggled to agree on how to turn that pledge into action.

COP30 ended with a deal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels after oil-producing countries opposed the language.

Instead, Brazil produced a voluntary “roadmap” with proposals for phasing out fossil fuels that each country can tailor to their circumstances.

– Finance fight –

The EU, for its part, and other developed countries are under pressure from the developing nations to fulfil promises to provide funds they need to adapt to climate impacts and recover from extreme weather disasters.

A senior EU official warned that there would be “no political will” for extra funding pledges.

African countries are pushing for the COP31 agenda to include discussions on the tripling of adaptation finance, which aims to help poorer nations pay for measures such as building sea walls or planting drought-resistant crops.

Climate diplomacy is still missing a major player as President Donald Trump pulled the United States out of the Paris Agreement and has not sent officials to COP31.

A US congressional delegation, however, will come to Antalya, with Democrats beaming after last week’s historic US midterm election win.

While negotiations are facing two weeks of gruelling talks, “the mood is very good”, Azerbaijan’s chief negotiator Yalchin Rafiyev told AFP.

Countries need to turn “this positive spirit of being in a favourable environment into concrete, successful results”, he said.

World.title: 'PM won't dare face jawan again': Rahul Gandhi tells CRPF, challenges Modi to debate over 'Naxal' jab
World.content:

Both sides identified cooperation in trade and investment, digital public infrastructure and pharmaceuticals as priorities.

"They also discussed regional and international issues of mutual interest," Jaiswal said.

The consultations come as Secretary Ranganathan earlier undertook an official visit to Egypt, Palestine and Lebanon from August 16 to 21.

During her visit to Lebanon on August 21, the Indian Embassy in Beirut gave accounts of her engagements.

World.title: 'He called us Naxals': Rahul Gandhi hits back at PM Modi, renews debate challenge
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Monday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, and renewed his challenge to the Prime Minister for an open debate.

"Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies.

He called us Naxals," he wrote.

Reiterating his challenge, the Congress leader said the Prime Minister should debate him on who was anti-national and who was controlled by foreign forces.

"My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place," he said, adding, "My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won't have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again."

World.title: 'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

and the

traded barbs over AICC president

's description of

Diwali

as "khushiyon ka Eid", with the opposition party accusing the ruling party of deliberately misinterpreting his festive greeting.

The row began after Kharge used the phrase while wishing people on Diwali over the weekend. The BJP objected to the comparison, arguing that Diwali should be referred to by its own name and accusing the Congress of being anti-Sanatani.

BJP national media co-in-charge and spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari alleged that the Congress had brought vote-bank politics into Diwali celebrations by describing the festival as an "Eid of Happiness".



Congress hits back at BJP

Responding to the criticism, Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said the BJP leaders had misunderstood the meaning of the word Eid.

"Those making a big deal out of Kharge jiâs statement are semantically ignorant," Khera said as per news agency PTI.

"The word 'Eid' literally means 'festival'. Now go and listen to his statement again. It is perfectly normal -- unlike the Sanghi negativity that makes some people incapable of sparing even a festival," Khera said on X.





He also launched a sharp attack on those criticising Kharge, urging them to understand the meaning of the phrase rather than turn it into a controversy.

"In the spirit of Diwali and for the love of God, please light a bulb or two in your brain as well, and spare the rest of us the public display of your stupidity. Jaahil kahin ke (they are illiterates)," Khera added.

BJP questions comparison with Eid

BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia questioned why Kharge had compared Diwali, which he described as the biggest festival of Hindus, with Eid.

"Mr Kharge, what exactly is the problem with calling Diwali, the biggest festival of Hindus, by its own name?"

Bhatia said Eid and Diwali each had their own religious significance and distinct traditions. He also challenged Kharge and Rahul Gandhi to explain whether they would describe Eid as the "Diwali of joy".

"Respect Hindus' faith; don't change the identity of their festivals. Diwali was, Diwali is, and Diwali will remain Diwali," Bhatia said.

World.title: Delhi pollution sparks row: BJP alleges 'conspiracy'; AAP and Congress question AQI data
World.content:
BJP leaders blamed the previous Congress and AAP governments for failing to address the crisis

Kapil Mishra alleges conspiracy over Punjab farm fires

Pawan Khera questions missing pollution data

Praveen Khandelwal blames previous governments

AAP alleges manipulation of AQI readings

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A thick blanket of smog engulfed Delhi on Monday, with air quality deteriorating to the brink of the 'severe' category a day after Diwali celebrations. As several monitoring stations recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) above 400, a political war of words erupted between the BJP, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Congress.Delhi minister Kapil Mishra accused the AAP government in Punjab of orchestrating stubble-burning incidents on Diwali to deliberately worsen Delhi's air quality and target the festival. Congress leader Pawan Khera questioned the Delhi government's pollution data, alleging that readings from several monitoring stations had gone missing during the night.Delhi minister and BJP leader Kapil Mishra alleged that a sudden increase in stubble-burning incidents in Punjab on Diwali was a premeditated attempt to worsen pollution in the national capital. He demanded an investigation by Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and called for FIRs against those responsible.Speaking about the allegations, Mishra said he and BJP leader Sirsa had started receiving calls from farmers in Punjab reporting that their fields were being set on fire while they were celebrating Diwali at home.He said the claims initially appeared difficult to believe, prompting them to examine satellite data on stubble burning made available to the Government of India."We decided to find out the truth...We asked for data coming in through satellites for Govt of India on stubble burning. The data proves that this was a premeditated move, and fields in Punjab were set on fire," Mishra said.Citing the figures, he claimed that stubble burning was recorded at 125 locations on November 7, but the number jumped to 1,200 on November 8, coinciding with Diwali."How did it increase 10 times?...This is a really serious matter. This is a conspiracy against farmers, against Diwali, against Delhi, against Punjab," he said.Mishra also urged the Punjab chief minister to investigate the alleged fires and examine the phone records of AAP members from Delhi who were in Punjab, claiming that a campaign had been launched two days before the festival to blame the BJP government for rising pollution.Congress leader Pawan Khera took aim at the BJP government over the deteriorating air quality, alleging that pollution readings from several monitoring stations in Delhi were unavailable during the early hours of November 9.In a sharp attack, Khera congratulated Delhi for getting a "double-, triple- or whatever-engine Sarkaar", accusing the government of moving stealthily while allowing the city's residents to choke."There were no PM2.5 readings recorded at 25 of Delhiâs 39 monitoring stations between 2 and 3 a.m. on the night of November 8â9. WHY?" he asked.Khera questioned whether the government was suppressing pollution data, whether monitoring equipment had been deliberately switched off or whether pollution levels had exceeded the equipment's measuring capacity."Whatever the reason, the government owes the people of Delhi an explanation," he said.He further alleged that the absence of readings did not mean pollution had disappeared, warning that the toxic air continued to threaten people's health and life expectancy. He also accused the BJP of failing to acknowledge the severity of the crisis.BJP MP Praveen Khandelwal also accused the AAP of deliberately allowing stubble burning in Punjab to worsen Delhi's pollution during Diwali."This is a well-thought-out conspiracy. Aam Aadmi Party has a government in Punjab, and the people of Punjab are crying for help. Punjab decided to burn stubble vigorously so that Delhi remains polluted on Diwali and they can blame us for it," he said.Khandelwal also blamed successive Congress and AAP governments for failing to address the pollution problem, arguing that the BJP government would need time to reverse years of inaction.AAP Delhi unit president Saurabh Bhardwaj, meanwhile, accused the BJP government of manipulating pollution figures to present a better picture of Delhi's air quality.He alleged that monitoring stations had been shut down and that 20 new AQI stations had been installed in remote, green areas of the capital. He also claimed that water was being sprinkled directly over monitoring stations in polluted areas to influence readings."The government's data is based on fraud. We showed how monitoring stations were shut down, and how 20 new AQI stations were installed in remote, lush green areas of Delhi. Water is being sprinkled directly over the monitoring stations in polluted spots to manipulate the readings. People simply do not trust the government's AQI numbers; I certainly don't," Bhardwaj said.

World.title: Jaishankar extends national day greetings to Cambodia, hails strong civilisational ties

External Affairs Minister

on Monday extended National Day greetings to Cambodia, highlighting the strong civilisational linkages shared by the two countries.

In a post on X, Jaishankar said, âGreetings to DPM & FM Prak Sokhonn, the Government and people of Cambodia on their National Day.

Value our strong bonds built on shared civilizational linkages.

Jaishankar also highlighted the successful completion of the second edition of the Cambodia-India Bilateral Army Exercise (CINBAX-II) 2026, held in Cambodia from May 4 to 17.

The 14-day joint military exercise between the Indian Army and the Royal Cambodian Army was conducted at the Techo Sen Phnom Thom Mreas Prov Royal Cambodian Air Force Training Centre in Kampong Speu Province.



The exercise focused on joint planning and execution of tactical operations in a sub-conventional environment under the framework of Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate. It involved company-level joint training in a semi-urban setting.

The Indian Army contingent comprised 120 personnel, primarily from a battalion of the Maratha Light Infantry Regiment, while the Cambodian contingent included 160 personnel from the Royal Cambodian Army.





Training activities covered Command Post and Field Training Exercises, sniper training, mortar drills, tactical drone employment, combat first aid, urban operations, multi-domain operations and disaster relief.

The exercise aimed to enhance interoperability through the exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures, while providing both contingents an opportunity to share operational experiences and best practices.

World.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport, identity card to facilitate return to Bangladesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister

has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.

The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasinaâs lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.

Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities.

"In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.



The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".

According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power.





Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.

Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be

announced after the completion of various formalities.

Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.

âIf death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,â Hasina said.

Death sentence and legal proceedings

In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.

Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.

Political implications of her return

Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.

Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.

It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.

World.title: Reds gone, but 'dimagi Naxals' still instigating people: PM Modi
World.content:
RAIPUR:

on Sunday warned that the end of armed Maoist insurgency did not mean the threat had disappeared, alleging that what he called 'Dimagi Naxals' had infiltrated political parties and organisations and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy

Continuing his long-standing tradition of celebrating Diwali with security forces, this time at Karanpur camp in Chhattisgarh's Bastar - once the epicentre of Maoist insurgency and declared free of Naxalism on March 31 this year - he called for identifying and defeating such elements to safeguard the country.

Calling it a historic Diwali after nearly five decades of conflict, Modi said this was the first festival of lights when every district in the country was free from Maoist insurgency. "This is the first Diwali after the country has won its decades-long battle against Naxalism and Maoist terror. This is the first Diwali when every district is free from Naxalism," he said, attributing the achievement to the courage, sacrifices and dedication of security forces.



Modi asserted that for the first time in 47 years, the CRPF had completed a year without losing a single jawan in operational duty.

Political will since 2014 drove anti-insurgency success, says PM | page 6

He described the milestone as a victory of sound policies, political resolve and the bravery and restraint of security personnel. "More than 1,000 jawans sacrificed their lives in Chhattisgarh", he said, recalling the scale of Maoist violence, adding there was a time when more than 230 districts across 20 states were affected.





From Bihar and Odisha to Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, vast regions had lived under the shadow of violence, he said. "After sunset, life would come to a standstill. People could not step out of their homes. Naxals had even snatched away people's right to vote," he said.

Modi recalled the April 2010 Dantewada massacre in which 76 CRPF personnel were killed and another attack that year in which he said 44 civilians lost their lives.

He accused previous govts of treating the insurgency as an incurable problem and abandoning tribal communities to their fate. "Some had accepted that bullets would continue to fly, jawans would die and innocent people would suffer. No country can confront its enemies with an attitude that things will simply continue this way," he said.

He credited the change in India's counter-insurgency strategy to the political will demonstrated after his government assumed office in 2014.

"We gave our security forces the freedom to take every necessary decision," he said, adding the govt had taken several national security decisions, including measures not widely known to the public, to disrupt funding networks supporting Maoists and separatist organisations.

He also alleged that elements within the earlier political and administrative system had provided support to Left-Wing Extremism, which his govt worked to eliminate.

Linking the decline in insurgency to development, Modi said Maoists had prevented schools, hospitals, medical facilities, mobile towers and industries from coming up in areas under their influence. Modi said the govt had, therefore, pursued security operations alongside a special development campaign.

According to him, more than 15,000km of roads had been constructed in areas affected by Naxalism, along with over 9,500 mobile towers. Nearly 175 Eklavya residential schools had been opened for tribal students, while 50 industrial training institutes and approximately 50 skill development centres were established to improve employment opportunities. He also cited the establishment of thousands of post offices, bank branches and ATMs in previously underserved regions.

World.title: Watch: Diwali lights up Srinagar's Lal Chowk as tourists, locals celebrate at Ghanta Ghar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Thousands of earthen lamps lit up Srinagar's iconic Lal Chowk on Sunday evening as tourists and local residents came together to celebrate Diwali around the city's historic clock tower, popularly known as Ghanta Ghar.

Dozens of tourists gathered at the clock tower and lit diyas, illuminating the area around the landmark.

Local Hindus and Muslims also joined the celebrations, with people lighting firecrackers.

Ankush Chatterjee, a tourist from Kolkata, said he was delighted to celebrate the festival in Kashmir. "We are delighted to celebrate this year's Diwali in Kashmir. The atmosphere here is radiant," he told PTI.

Diwali celebrations at Ghanta Ghar have become a regular sight in recent years, with tourists and residents gathering at Lal Chowk to mark the festival.

Elsewhere in the Valley, security personnel celebrated Diwali by lighting lamps at their camps and distributing sweets.

World.title: Untangling Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s Chinese spy connection
World.content:
Nvidia is the world leader in making chips for AI data centres, and its role in providing the critical hardware for the development of large language models cannot be understated. Powerful AI tools like Anthropic’s Claude, Google’s Gemini, Meta’s Muse, and OpenAI’s GPT exist today because of Nvidia’s graphic processing unit (GPU) chips. So, it is only fair to say that if AI is the solar system, Nvidia is the sun powering American tech companies, plus those in China building competing AI models, that orbit around it. And CEO Jensen Huang is the sun maker.

Accessing Nvidia’s GPUs to build powerful AI models started becoming difficult for Chinese companies since 2022 as Washington doubled down on measures to tighten controls on who can access advanced chips.

World.title: Deepavali pollution spike: How does it affect lung function and respiratory health? | Explainer
World.content:
A few hours of exposure to firecracker smoke can be enough to trigger coughing, wheezing or breathlessness, particularly in people living with asthma or other respiratory conditions. The effects, however, are not limited to those with an existing diagnosis. High concentrations of particulate matter and gases can irritate the airways in anyone.

The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a numerical measure that converts the levels of different air pollutants into a single figure to indicate how polluted the air is and the likely health effects. India’s Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) calculates it using eight pollutants, including PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh tightens fireworks safety rules after fatal blasts
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has overhauled its fireworks safety, licensing and enforcement framework following explosions at fireworks manufacturing units in Rayavaram and Vetlapalem, introducing a system of centralised monitoring, risk-based inspections and stricter accountability for enforcement officials.

The reforms were notified through a government order dated November 7, 2026, issued by Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad, following the findings of inquiry committees, which pointed to fragmented enforcement and inadequate risk-based monitoring.

Under the new framework, the Director-General of the A.P. State Disaster Response and Fire Services has been designated as the State Nodal Authority to coordinate enforcement, conduct monthly inter-departmental reviews and submit compliance reports to the Home Department. District Collectors will function as nodal authorities at the district level, overseeing implementation and quarterly reviews.

The government has also ordered the establishment of a State Explosives and Fireworks Safety Cell within 30 days. It will maintain a digital register of fireworks manufacturing units, prepare risk-based inspection schedules, develop a Fireworks Risk Index and coordinate with the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO).

District Fireworks Safety Committees, headed by Collectors, will include officials from the police, fire services, revenue, factories, labour and pollution control departments. They will review licensed units and emergency preparedness at least once every quarter.

The licensing process for LE-1(a) units will be tightened through a two-stage system, involving provisional approval followed by a mandatory physical inspection after construction. The inspection must be supported by geo-tagged photographs and video evidence.

The government has set a six-month deadline for the RTGS and Information Technology, Electronics and Communications Department to operationalise an integrated online fireworks safety portal. It will track licences, approved layouts, CCTV feeds and stock movements, besides generating alerts on irregularities.

The new framework provides for immediate closure of units, seizure of materials and legal action in cases involving unlicensed operations, unauthorised chemical formulations, excess stock, unapproved equipment and obstruction of inspections.

The government has also made inspecting officers personally accountable for their certifications. Negligent inspections and suppression of violations will be treated as serious professional misconduct, inviting disciplinary and legal action.

The effectiveness of the new framework will depend on whether the prescribed inspections, digital monitoring and interdepartmental coordination translate into consistent enforcement on the ground.

CM reviews fire accidents in Rajam, Gannavaram and Tiruvuru

Meanwhile, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Monday (November 9) reviewed three separate fire accidents reported in Rajam, Gannavaram and Tiruvuru, and directed officials to remain alert and take preventive measures.

A major fire broke out at an automobile showroom in Rajam of Vizianagaram district after firecrackers, reportedly burst during Deepavali celebrations, accidentally fell on the premises. The showroom was gutted, resulting in extensive property damage. Senior Fire Services officials informed the Chief Minister that fire personnel rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control.

In Gannavaram of Krishna district, sparks from firecrackers being burst nearby landed on a furniture shop, triggering a fire. Another shop in Tiruvuru was gutted in a fire caused by an electrical short circuit.

Mr. Naidu expressed concern over the property losses and instructed officials to ensure adequate precautions to prevent such incidents.

World.title: 800-year-old Nandi sculpture lies neglected in Telangana’s Narayanapet
World.content:
An 800-year-old Nandi sculpture dating back to the Kakatiya period has been lying neglected amid bushes along the roadside in Jakkileru village, Maktal mandal of Narayanapet district in Telangana.

Archaeologist and Pleach India Foundation CEO E. Sivanagireddy, who inspected the site on Monday (November 9, 2026), said the black basalt sculpture, dating to the 13th century, was originally housed in the Rangamandapa of Trikutalaya (triple-shrine temple).

Acting on information provided by heritage activists K. Bhaskar Goud and G. Mahendar Reddy, Mr. Sivanagireddy visited the village and found that the sculpture was broken into two pieces by miscreants some time ago and lying unattended.

Nandi sculpture reflects the craftsmanship of Kakatiya artisans

Measuring five feet in length, three feet in width and 3.5 feet in height, the sculpture reflects the craftsmanship of Kakatiya artisans, particularly in its anatomical detailing and ornamental decorations, he said.

Mr. Sivanagireddy appealed to the villagers to shift the two pieces of the sculpture into the temple, restore them on a pedestal and install a plaque explaining their historical significance. He said the villagers responded positively and assured him that steps would be taken to preserve the sculpture for posterity.

Villagers Jayapal Reddy and Srinivasa Reddy, along with students, participated in the heritage awareness programme, ‘Preserve Heritage for Posterity’, organised by the Pleach India Foundation.

World.title: Two men arrested in Rajasthan, West Bengal for cybercrimes targeting Chennai residents
World.content:
The Cyber Crime Police, East Zone have arrested a 35-year-old man in Rajasthan for allegedly cheating a Chennai-based businessman of ₹12.99 lakh by promising high returns through an online trading platform advertised on the internet.

The complainant, Jeganathan Balaji (54), a resident of Triplicane, was exploring business opportunities related to electric vehicle charging stations on the internet. On May 28, 2026, he came across an  and contacted a business firm through his mobile phone.

The police said the people who spoke to him claimed to represent a Japanese company and persuaded him to register on a particular website to start trading, promising substantial profits. They also offered to provide online training before he began investing.

Believing their claims, Balaji transferred a total of ₹12.99 lakh in four instalments to bank accounts provided by them in August. Initially, the fraudsters paid him a small amount as profit but subsequently stopped communicating with him and deactivated the website.

Following this, Balaji lodged a complaint with the Cyber Crime Police, East Zone seeking the identification of those behind the fraud. A special team of Cyber Crime Police analysed the bank account details and mobile phone numbers linked to the fraud and found that one of the suspects was hiding in Rajasthan.

The team travelled to Rajasthan and, with the assistance of personnel from the Ramgarh Pachwara Police Station, traced and arrested Rajendra Kumar Meena (35) of Hemliwala, Dausa district. The police seized two mobile phones including an iPhone, from him.

He was brought to Chennai after completing the necessary legal formalities. Following interrogation, Meena was produced before a court in Chennai and remanded to judicial custody.

Man arrested in West Bengal for cheating Chennai resident by promising premium credit card

In a separate development, the Cyber Crime Police have arrested a 26-year-old man in West Bengal for allegedly cheating a Chennai resident of ₹17.6 lakh by promising to provide him with a premium credit card with attractive benefits.

Police said the complainant, Keerthivasan (34), a resident of Nungambakkam, was contacted by an unidentified person over the phone on April 23. The caller claimed that, based on his credit score, he was eligible for a premium credit card offering several benefits.

The caller sent him a link through WhatsApp and asked him to enter his bank account and other personal details, promising that the premium credit card would be issued shortly. Believing the offer, Keerthivasan entered the requested details on the link.

The following day (April 24), the fraudster sent him a mobile phone and instructed him to insert his SIM card into it for a two-step verification process. Shortly after Keerthivasan inserted his SIM card into the new phone, ₹10 lakh was transferred from his bank account, while another ₹7.6 lakh was fraudulently debited through online transactions using his credit card. The total loss amounted to ₹17,60,440.

Keerthivasan subsequently lodged a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and approached the Cyber Crime Police Station, East Zone seeking action against the fraudster and recovery of his money. The police registered a case and launched an investigation.

After analysing the bank account details and mobile phone numbers linked to the transactions, the police found that one of the suspects was hiding in West Bengal.

The team travelled to West Bengal and, with the assistance of local police personnel, traced and arrested the suspect Abul Hussain Sheikh (26) of Nawda in Murshidabad district on November 6. He was arrested and brought to the city.

Following interrogation, Sheikh was produced before the Saidapet Metropolitan Magistrate Court on November 8 and remanded to judicial custody.

World.title: Fire breaks out in two shops; LPG blast in Krishna district house, no casualties reported
World.content:
A fire broke out in two shops in the NTR and Krishna districts on Deepavali festival day, and property worth several lakhs of rupees was gutted by the fire. However, no casualties were reported.

The fire accident occurred in a photo frame workshop near Jai Bhavani Centre in Tiruvuru town, NTR District. Fire personnel rushed to the spot and extinguished the flames.

In another accident, a fire broke out in a household appliances shop at Gannavaram in Krishna district. The reasons for the mishap were not known immediately, and valuable material was damaged in the fire, locals said.

Cylinder exploded

An LPG cylinder exploded in a house in Koduru in Krishna district on Monday (November 9, 2026). The family members had a narrow escape as the mishap occurred when they went out.

Fire Services personnel put off the flames, the villagers said.

World.title: In pictures: Smog blankets Indian cities after Deepavali as firecrackers push air quality to ‘severe’
World.content:
Thick smog enveloped several Indian cities on Monday (November 9, 2026), after firecrackers were burst late into Deepavali night on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Delhi’s air quality touched the ‘severe’ category, while Mumbai, Lucknow, Chennai and Hyderabad also recorded ‘poor’ or worse readings.

Here’s a collection of pictures of the haze from across the country:

A thick layer of toxic haze engulfs Delhi as people commute near Rashtrapati Bhavan, shrouded in thick smog during the early morning of November 9, 2026, a day after Deepavali. The city’s 24-hour average AQI was 370, in the “very poor” category, at 9 a.m.

People jog near India Gate, shrouded in thick smog, as Delhi’s AQI touched 404 in the ‘severe’ category at 4 a.m. on November 9, 2026, according to the CPCB’s live dashboard.

Burari Crossing recorded Delhi’s highest AQI on November 9, 2026, at 441, followed by Vivek Vihar at 437 and Delhi Technological University at 434. People walking near India Gate.

Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) is in force across Delhi and adjoining districts of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, following the CAQM’s decision. A view of the Rashtrapati Bhavan, shrouded in thick smog during the early morning hours after Deepavali night.

The Supreme Court had allowed only green firecrackers in specified time windows on November 7 and 8, 2026, but the more polluting traditional crackers were also available in Delhi markets.

PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable particles 2.5 micrometres or smaller, which can enter deep into the lungs and the bloodstream and cause respiratory and other health problems. People commute near Rashtrapati Bhavan, shrouded in thick smog.

Kherwadi-Bandra East in Mumbai recorded an AQI of 264 on November 9, 2026, followed by Sewri at 226, Ghatkopar at 221 and Chembur at 216. Byculla recorded an AQI of 193, Mindspace-Malad West 191, Kandivali West 187 and Worli 148 in Mumbai on November 9. Kurla was the lowest at 96.

Chennai’s AQI slipped to the ‘poor’ category at 213 on the morning of November 9, 2026, according to the CPCB’s Sameer app.

A private sensor at the Chennai home of weather blogger K. Srikanth recorded an AQI of around 1,000 for nearly four hours between 6 p.m. and 10 p.m. on November 8, 2026. Chennai residents said smoke from firecrackers lingered in cramped residential communities, with visibility so poor at one point that people could barely see one another.

As of 9 a.m. on November 9, 2026, Manali Village recorded Chennai’s highest AQI at 296, followed by Arumbakkam at 265, Kodungaiyur at 215, Royapuram at 184 and Velachery Residential Area at 142.

Hyderabad woke up to a grey, smoggy morning on November 9, 2026, after Deepavali celebrations that went on until 3 a.m. in localities such as Banjara Hills, Panjagutta, S.R. Nagar, Ameerpet and Somajiguda.

Smog shrouds the historic Golconda Fort, PM2.5 in Hyderabad reached 392 μg/m³ at 9.30 p.m. on November 8, 2026, with the city’s AQI averaging 509. Ravi Colony near Masjid Banda in Hyderabad logged an AQI of 995 on November 8, 2026, and Serilingampally recorded 666 at 11.30 p.m., when the city average was 442.

Telangana Pollution Control Board monitors in Hyderabad were out of order as pollution rose on November 8, 2026, with the University of Hyderabad station offline by 10 p.m. The figures come from publicly available monitors. Hyderabad’s AQI was still 178 on November 9, morning, with PM10 at 113 μg/m³.

World.title: Firecracker explosion kills 10-year-old boy in Delhi’s Narela
World.content:
A 10-year-old boy in outer North Delhi’s Narela died after being injured by a firecracker on Deepavali night, police officials said on Monday (November 9, 2026). The boy, identified as Rishi, was hit by an ‘anar’ (flower pots or fountain) that exploded near his chest, causing severe burn injuries. He was later declared brought dead at a nearby hospital.

The boy was bursting firecrackers in front of his home in outer North Delhi’s Narela with his elder brother and friends. While trying to burst an ‘anar’ in his hand, the firecracker exploded near his chest. He was immediately taken to the Satyawadi Raja Harish Chandra hospital where the doctors declared him dead, the officials said.

“We received the information from the hospital at around 10.50 p.m. that the child was brought dead due to burn injuries caused by a firecracker. The incident took place around 9.45 p.m. as per family of the victim,” said Shobhit Saxena, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Outer North).

The child’s body has been sent for post-mortem examination, while further legal proceedings are underway, the officer said. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident and examining the details of the firecracker explosion. Police are also investigating the kind of material used in the firecracker.

A number of firecracker-related incidents were reported widely across the city.

As per the data shared by AIIMS, as many as 42 burn cases were received on Monday (November 9, 2026) including six children under the age of 10, and 12 children between ages 10 and 18. While 11 of the 42 are major burn cases, 31 are minor injuries. Out of 42, 37 were firecracker related burns.

Among the children, one eight-year-old child is critical with 45% burns, the hospital administration said. Several persons also reported eye injuries at the Dr RP. Eye Centre.

Similarly, Safdarjung Hospital hospital received 127 patients on November 8 due to Deepavali-related burns. Of these, 122 were firecracker injuries. At least seven persons had to undergo surgeries.

Delhi Fire Service received 257 calls on November 8, of which 24 were firecracker related calls.

World.title: Protective bund of Tarbela Dam tunnel collapses, triggering water surge
World.content:
SWABI: A rock mass collapsed at the Tarbela Dam 5th Extension Project construction site on Monday, causing a surge of water to enter downstream work areas.

An emergency was declared following the collapse, construction work was suspended and workers were directed to move to safer areas.

The Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) said in a statement that water entered the under-construction power house area and a tunnel of the Tarbela Dam 5th Extension Project after a weak rock mass collapsed during excavation work, prompting the evacuation of workers.

In a statement, Wapda said the incident occurred during excavation of the 2nd Bench Connecting Tunnel, when the collapse allowed water from the Intake Pit to enter the tunnel and power house area.

“All workers were immediately evacuated safely,” the statement said, adding that the water from the Intake Pit had been completely drained and no further water was entering the downstream work sites.

Wapda said dewatering work at the under-construction power house had also started.

Senior Wapda officers, the project engineer and the contractor were assessing the situation to address any challenges to the T-5 project, the statement added.

The authority also dismissed reports circulating about the collapse of the T-5 tunnel, saying the main tunnel, under-construction power house, tailrace culvert and switchyard had not been damaged.

It further said there had been no injuries or loss of life among the workforce.

More to follow.

World.title: PM directs foreign ministry to urgently ‘escalate humanitarian assistance’ for rain-hit Gaza
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said on Monday he had directed the foreign ministry to pursue all possible means to urgently “escalate humanitarian assistance” to Gaza, where heavy rains have flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

The Gaza government media office said on Sunday that at least 70,000 tents had been flooded in the past 12 hours, affecting tens of thousands of displaced people and causing injuries, although no fatalities had been reported. The rains and subsequent flooding has also washed away shelters, according to authorities.

Gaza’s civil defence service said it had received 1,500 distress calls from displaced residents.

Municipal and civil defence officials ​said they were unable to cope with the storm because of fuel shortages and damage to equipment. They said Israel had destroyed hundreds ​of vehicles, including bulldozers and others used to pump water, during its assault on the territory.

PM Shehbaz said photos from Gaza had been “heart rending”, with tents being flooded and Gazan children, with nowhere to go, being trapped and subject to starvation and extreme cold.

“I have directed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to pursue all possible means to escalate humanitarian assistance urgently,” he posted on X.

The premier added that he was also “deeply concerned about continued Israeli illegal actions to deny basic humanitarian assistance to the brave Palestinian people of Gaza”.

“I strongly condemn these violations of the ceasefire and international law, and this continued aggression toward the Palestinian people.”

Gaza has been subjected to Israeli assault for long, particularly following an attack by Hamas on Israel on Oct 7, 2023. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since Israel began its assault on the territory.

Last year’s US-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for ​the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal and Israel continues to violate the ceasefire.

Israeli forces still hold more than 60 per cent of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where more than two million Palestinians live, ​mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies.

A majority of Gazans are dependent on aid supplies, following three years of Israeli assault, repeated ​displacement and severe restrictions imposed by Israel on aid deliveries.

Heavy rains and flooding has worsened their condition.

On Sunday, at a tent encampment in Gaza City, some people tried to repair their tents, while others ​used sand to reinforce them and prevent water from entering. Some were busy getting their children out ⁠of flooded tents.

Olfat Magdoub, a Gaza resident, tried in vain to sweep water away from her tent.

“This is the first day of ​rain, and of course we are already flooded. What will happen if it rains again the next day? This is only the ​first day and we’re already overwhelmed,” said the woman.

“Two weeks ago when it rained, I swear to God, I spent four days sleeping on blankets spread on the floor because the rainwater had flooded the bedding. Same now, the mattresses are wet so we sleep on the ground.”

Another resident, Rafiq Ghattas, standing barefoot in the middle of ​a large pool of rainwater, said: “We have no resources, no tarpaulins, no tents and no one is ⁠checking on ​us.”

World.title: Security forces neutralise terrorists’ hideouts in North Waziristan’s Mir Ali: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Muzak village, on the southern outskirts of Mir Ali in North Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, neutralising two terrorist hideouts, the military’s media wing said on Monday.

During the operation, troops “sanitised” the hideouts belonging to the India-sponsored Fitna al-Khawarij, the military’s media wing said.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces recovered a huge cache of prepared improvised explosive devices (IEDs), explosive preparation material, weapons, and ammunition from hideouts, which were established inside mosques.

The statement added that the terrorists had “deliberately established hideouts in Masajid to store explosive materials and also were running torture cells there,” observing that, “this reprehensible desecration of places of worship by Indian proxy Fitna Al Khwarij serves yet another clear evidence of their utter disregard of fundamental teachings of Islam.”

ISPR maintained that the terrorists, who it had said were facilitated by the Afghan Taliban, had no connection with Islam and their “perverted interpretation and misuse of our great religion is unacceptable and fully rejected by proud and righteous people of KP and Pakistan”.

Moreover, a sanitisation operation was “being conducted by brave soldiers of Pakistan security forces to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorist hideouts in the area,” ISPR said.

“Relentless counter-terrorism campaign under vision Azm-i-Istehkam by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out [the] menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.”

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for the successful IBO, praising their “professionalism”.

“Using mosques to store explosives and as centres of violence is a blatant violation of Islam’s fundamental teachings,” he said on X.

“Terrorist elements operating with the support of the Afghan Taliban have no connection to Islam. Arbitrary interpretations and misuse of religion are unacceptable,” the president stressed.

Meanwhile, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi described the incident as “deeply distressing” while also praising the security forces for the successful IBO, Pakistan TV reported.

The governor also called for “intensified” IBOs to restore peace across KP and reaffirmed his support for security forces in their efforts to bring lasting peace to the province, Pakistan TV stated.

KP and Balochistan have been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time.

The country’s security environment continued to show considerable volatility from October 30 to November 5, 2026, with renewed terrorist activity in parts of KP and the former tribal districts, alongside intensified counterterrorism operations and changing patterns of militant violence, according to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) .

Per the latest PICSS Weekly Insight, 49 militant attacks were recorded nationwide during the reporting period, compared with 31 in the preceding week. These incidents resulted in 25 fatalities and 21 injuries.

On October 8, security forces killed nine terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan, while a day earlier, 18 terrorists were eliminated in separate engagements in KP and Balochistan.

World.title: Iran war 'highly unlikely' to resume but decision depends on whether Tehran signs 'very strong' deal: Trump
World.content:
US President Donald Trump cast doubt on renewed fighting with Iran, telling CNN it was “highly unlikely”, ahead of a meeting with mediator Qatar’s prime minister on Monday.

Trump has threatened to resume strikes in recent weeks, with US media reports suggesting that hostilities could restart after last Tuesday’s midterm elections.

The president told CNN in an interview on Sunday that renewed fighting was “highly unlikely,” but warned that his decision “depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement.”

“I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don’t know how hard I hit them,” he said.

Trump is scheduled to meet Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who is also the country’s foreign minister, at the White House on Monday.

The meeting will be Trump’s first with a foreign leader since a massive midterm loss that saw his Republican Party lose control of Congress.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested on Sunday that peace talks had been paused while the political fallout of the vote was being assessed.

“For the past few days, there has been no more travel (by mediators), and the reason for this is the shock that the election results in the United States have caused to everyone,” Araghchi told state television.

“We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward,” he added.

‘They had enough’

Trump has acknowledged that the highly unpopular war on Iran — which began with US-Israeli strikes in late February — was at least partially responsible for the Republicans’ defeat.

Araghchi said on Monday that the US president “clearly recognises that the vast majority of Americans are disgusted with Israel.”

“Americans are evidently sick and tired of Israel bamboozling US administrations into forever wars,” Araghchi said on X. “They had enough. So has our region.”

In Sunday’s CNN interview, Trump once again suggested that the economic pressure Iran is under will force its leaders into accepting the United States’ terms.

“They’re a failing nation. It just came out, you saw this year, 301 per cent inflation,” Trump claimed.

“They’re withering away financially. We’ve hit them militarily. We could finish them off.”

Iran’s official figures put inflation at nearly 90pc year-on-year in September.

Iranian state television said the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz was attacked overnight on Sunday, hours after the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions there.

Various regional powers, including Qatar and Pakistan, have been trying for months without success to bring a definitive halt to the war.

Outright fighting has largely subsided, but Iran continues in its efforts to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, vital to global energy supplies, while the US Navy maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

World.title: TV anchor's killing: Rawalpindi court grants police 2-day physical remand of victim's husband
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: A local court on Monday granted police two-day physical remand of Ahsan, the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at home in the Gulshanabad area a day earlier.

Rabia, who previously co-hosted a current affairs show alongside senior journalists Amir Mateen and Rauf Klasra, was found with a gunshot wound below her neck, City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Sukhera told reporters on Sunday. Her husband was taken into custody following a complaint filed by her brother.

A first information report was registered at Saddar Beruni police station under Section 302 (premeditated murder) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) and Section 2-A of the Punjab Arms Amendment Ordinance, 2015 on Sunday.

On Monday, the suspect was presented before Area Magistrate Talat Waheed by police, who sought physical custody for further investigation.

After hearing the police request, the magistrate approved a two-day physical remand of the suspect, allowing investigators to interrogate him and pursue further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the anchorperson’s death.

Following the court’s order, police took the suspect into custody for further investigation. Ahsan, who is the primary suspect in the case, will remain in police custody for two days.

The judge directed police to produce the suspect at the expiry of the remand period.

A day earlier, police said that a male domestic worker at their house informed them that the victim’s husband claimed the gunshot had been fired accidentally.

First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari had “exp­ressed deep sadness over the killing” and called for a thorough, impartial and transparent investigation to establish the facts and ensure that those responsible were held accountable.

World.title: Lahore remains world’s most polluted major city as AQI crosses 600
World.content:
LAHORE: Lahore was ranked the world’s most polluted major city on Monday as its Air Quality Index (AQI) reached 590, according to IQAir. A separate historical reading on the platform, however, showed an hourly index of 647, placing the city in the hazardous category.

The IQAir live global major city ranking for 9am to 10am on Nov 9 placed Lahore at the top, followed by Ulaanbaatar with an AQI of 177, Delhi with 174, Kolkata with 173 and Sarajevo with 170.

The ranking showed Lahore’s pollution level to be more than three times that of the second-ranked city. The platform’s historical air quality graph separately displayed an hourly reading of 647 for Lahore during the same period.

IQ Air rankings for the most polluted cities on Nov 9. — Screengrab IQAir

According to global health statistics, air pollution, both outdoor and indoor, is the second-leading risk factor for deaths worldwide, claiming an estimated 8.1 million lives annually. Outdoor particulate matter alone accounts for 4.7 million deaths.

Within Lahore, air pollution is affecting several neighbourhoods. IQAir’s station ranking for the city shows multiple areas experiencing extremely poor air quality. Allama Iqbal Town recorded an AQI of 1,033, while CERP Office (864) and Burki Road Paragon (748) also reported hazardous levels. Hourly historical graphs indicate that pollution levels rise sharply during the early morning and late-night hours, creating dense smog that forces residents to remain indoors.

The crisis is not confined to Lahore. Other parts of Punjab are also experiencing hazardous air quality. IQAir’s real-time Pakistan city ranking showed Raiwind (688), Multan (655), Lahore (639) and Faisalabad (600) all recording air quality levels in the hazardous category.

The deterioration came a day after the Punjab government warned that smoke from Diwali fireworks in neighbouring Indian Punjab, crop-residue burning and easterly winds could aggravate air pollution in Lahore and adjoining districts.

A special report issued by the provincial government on Nov 8 had predicted that smoke from Diwali fireworks could reach Lahore within five to 13 hours. It forecast an increase in pollution levels in Lahore, Kasur and border areas on the morning of Nov 9, as easterly winds were expected to carry polluted air from Indian territory towards Pakistan.

The report identified fireworks, crop-residue burning and stagnant air during the night as factors that could contribute to a deterioration in air quality.

Amritsar, located around 50 kilometres from Lahore, was identified as a potential source of cross-border pollution. However, a measurement-based assessment would be required to establish how much of Lahore’s pollution could be attributed to fireworks and other sources across the border.

Indian media reports also highlighted deteriorating air quality after Diwali celebrations in Amritsar, Ludhiana, Jalandhar and Patiala. The AQI in Mandi Gobindgarh reportedly reached 445, while New Delhi also experienced a sharp increase in pollution following the fireworks.

The Punjab government’s report recorded 2,347 incidents of crop-residue burning in Indian Punjab up to Nov 4. Of these, 1,081 were reported in three districts — Tarn Taran, Ferozepur and Amritsar — located opposite Lahore and Kasur. These accounted for 46 per cent of the reported incidents in Indian Punjab.

Daily-wage labourers wait along a roadside for customers amid dense smog in Lahore on November 9, 2026.

However, satellite-based fire detections indicate that agricultural fires are also a major concern in Pakistan. An analysis by Hamari Hawa using NASA’s VIIRS satellite data recorded 13,241 fire detections in Pakistani Punjab, compared with 3,158 in Indian Punjab, between Oct 1 and 29, 2026, showing more than four times as many detections on the Pakistani side. The analysis found that 92 per cent of the detections in Pakistani Punjab were on farmland.

A separate analysis covering Oct 15 to Nov 1 identified 7,130 crop-associated fire detections within a 100-kilometre radius of Lahore on both sides of the border, including 781 within 40 kilometres of central Lahore.

The district-wise figures included 322 detections in Sheikhupura, 149 in Tarn Taran, 106 in Amritsar, 77 in Nankana Sahib, 62 in Lahore and 50 in Kasur. These satellite detections indicate fire activity and should not be treated as individually verified crop-burning incidents.

The Environment Protection Agency (EPA) Punjab, meanwhile, reported 679 agricultural fire incidents across the province, of which 650 had been extinguished through coordinated surveillance and firefighting operations. The agency said it had intensified its crackdown on stubble burning by deploying specialised night squads, drones, tractor-mounted fire bowsers and Quick Response Units in agricultural hotspots.

According to the EPA, the Punjab Climate Watch Hub was using satellite-based fire-anomaly detection to identify vulnerable locations and alert district field formations for on-ground verification and firefighting. The campaign was being conducted in districts including Hafizabad, Sheikhupura, Nankana Sahib, Faisalabad, Kasur, Sialkot, Sargodha and Gujranwala.

EPA Director General Abdullah Nayyar Sheikh has directed regional directors and field formations to prioritise anti-stubble-burning operations and personally monitor enforcement. He has also conducted surprise inspections along motorway corridors and GT roads to assess surveillance and firefighting arrangements.

The EPA said its operations against agricultural burning were being reinforced through coordination with district administrations and Agriculture Department officials, while legal action was being taken against those involved in illegal crop-residue burning.

The provincial government’s report also noted that Lahore’s nighttime PM2.5 concentration had already reached 202 micrograms per cubic metre before Diwali. It said prevailing weather conditions had increased the likelihood of pollution from fireworks and agricultural fires accumulating and spreading.

The government had forecast that pollution levels would remain high on Nov 9 and 10, with a slight improvement expected from Nov 11.

The Environment Protection Department is expected to release comparative findings on Nov 10 to assess the contributions of different pollution sources and weather conditions. Such an assessment would be important in establishing the extent of cross-border pollution and distinguishing it from emissions generated within Punjab.

World.title: President, PM say Iqbal’s vision continues to serve as a 'guiding beacon' for Pakistan
World.content:
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday paid tribute to Allama Muhammad Iqbal — the poet of the East — on his 149th birth anniversary, stressing that his message of unity and peaceful coexistence continued to serve as a “guiding beacon” for the country.

Born in Sialkot in 1877, Iqbal was a distinguished poet, a scholar, a gifted philosopher and Pakistan’s ideological founder. It was at the Allahabad session of the Muslim League in 1930 that Iqbal became the first politician to articulate the two-nation theory that ultimately led to the creation of Pakistan on August 14, 1947.

Last week, the federal government announced November 9 as a public holiday on account of Iqbal Day. A Change of Guards ceremony was held at Iqbal’s mausoleum in Lahore on Monday morning, Radio Pakistan reported.

In his message, the prime minister said that Iqbal was responsible for awakening political consciousness among the Muslims of the subcontinent, inspiring them to recognise and assert their distinct national identity.

“This consciousness of a separate identity played a pivotal role in their historic struggle for the creation of an independent homeland,” the premier wrote.

“Allama Iqbal was a person of exceptional intellectual stature and profound wisdom. The enduring thought of this eminent philosopher and visionary continues to broaden intellectual horizons and foster the intellectual growth of our youth and future generations.”

PM Shehbaz further stated that Iqbal, as a distinguished philosopher of Islam, explored the intellectual dimensions of Islamic teachings.

“His Islamic thought continues to offer meaningful and practical guidance to Muslims in their individual and collective lives.”

The premier also announced that the government will be holding a year-long commemoration of the 150th anniversary of Iqbal, culminating on November 9, 2027.

“A comprehensive programme of national and international events is being formally launched, featuring international conferences, academic and research seminars, literary festivals, exhibitions, educational competitions and cultural activities.

“These commemorative initiatives aim to preserve and transmit Iqbal’s rich intellectual legacy to future generations.”

He further added that the government remained committed to ensuring that Iqbal’s philosophy was a part of the education system and national discourse as well as development priorities.

“Intellectual awakening, character building and collective renewal must, undoubtedly, form an essential part of our national objectives.”

Speaking of Iqbal’s concept of Khudi (selfhood), the prime minister said that it taught that “Individuals and nations can transform their destinies through self-realisation, purposeful endeavour and spiritual emancipation.”

PM Shehbaz further stated that Iqbal had regarded youth as “architects of the nation’s future.”

“His concept of the Shaheen (falcon) embodies courage, independence, lofty aspirations and an unwavering pursuit of excellence.”

PM Shehbaz said that Iqbal’s thoughts spoke of peace, social harmony, tolerance, and justice as “indispensable pillars of sustainable national development.”

“His philosophy of life categorically rejects hatred, extremism, sectarianism and discrimination.”

He also noted that Iqbal’s message of “muslim unity, universal brotherhood and peaceful coexistence” held relevance on an international level. He added that Pakistan will continue to work on developing unity and solidarity among the Muslim ummah and the resolution of international disputes.

“Allama Iqbal’s timeless message, rooted in individual, national and universal values, continues to illuminate our path and serve as a guiding beacon for the nation.”

Concluding his statement, the prime minister pledged to renew resolve to deepen the understanding of Iqbal’s message, promote “rigorous” scholarly research into his thought, foster creative thinking and strengthen our national character.

Must take inspiration from Iqbal’s poetry to boost ‘spirit of inquiry, develop critical faculties’

President Zardari also spoke of Iqbal’s role in developing political consciousness among the Muslims of the subcontinent as he paid tribute to the poet, urging the country’s youth to take inspiration from Iqbal’s poetry “as a catalyst to boost the spirit of inquiry, develop critical faculties.”

“Iqbal gave intellectual direction to the aspirations of the Muslims of the Subcontinent. His poetry also spoke to a wider human struggle: the pursuit of freedom, equality and a life of self-respect,” a statement issued by the president’s office quoted him as saying.

He continued: “Iqbal envisioned a society in which wealth, privilege and inherited status would no longer determine a person’s worth or opportunities.”

The statement added that Iqbal’s poetry sought to challenge exploitation, awaken the poor, and uphold the dignity of labour.

President Zardari stressed that Iqbal’s vision called to “build a Pakistan where the worker receives a fair wage, the farmer enjoys the fruits of his labour, and every child can learn and advance, regardless of family circumstances, gender or faith”.

He also spoke of Khudi, stressing that “national self-respect demands the capacity to make independent decisions, develop our own strengths and engage with other countries on the basis of equality and mutual respect.”

“For me, fidelity to Iqbal’s vision means building a Pakistan where no citizen’s dignity is diminished by poverty, no child’s future is limited by birth, and our nation stands among others with confidence and self-respect,” the president was quoted as saying.

He further stated that Iqbal’s vision had gained renewed significance as the region looked towards the “dawn of an Asian century”.

“The promise of that century must reach beyond economic growth to embrace freedom from hunger, access to knowledge and opportunity, and respect for the sovereignty of nations. Pakistan must help realise this promise through education, scientific progress, regional cooperation and peace.”

President Zardari urged the youth to translate Iqbal’s concept of Khudi into “confidence rooted in knowledge, national self-respect into hard work to transform Pakistan into a developed and strong nation, and the ideal of equality into justice in everyday life.”

“This is how we can honour Iqbal and fulfil the promise of Pakistan.”

World.title: Drap urges public to verify authenticity and prices of medicines via new app
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (Drap) has urged consumers to use its Mehfooz Dawa application to verify the authenticity and prices of medicines as part of its efforts to curb the sale of counterfeit drugs.

About 800 pharmaceutical companies and more than 90,000 medicines were registered with Drap, Sajid Shah, a spokesperson for the Ministry of National Health Services, told Dawn.

Shah said Drap had set up a 2D barcode system that allows consumers to scan medicine packs and ensure they receive safe, high-quality and effective products.

The centralised track-and-trace system for pharmaceutical products distributed across Pakistan became operational on October 9, he added.

Furthermore, according to the spokesperson, the system will enable authorities to track medicine supply chains and make it easier to recall products in case of complaints or quality issues. People with smartphones will also be able to scan barcodes to view product details and prices.

The idea of introducing a barcode system was first proposed in 2015. It was approved by the federal cabinet in 2017; however, bureaucratic delays prevented its implementation.

Earlier, Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, taking notice of the delay, announced that the system would be launched as soon as possible.

Earlier this year, Drap had set October 1 as the cut-off date for launching the barcode system to curb the sale of counterfeit and expired medicines and eradicate black marketing.

Shah said the Ministry of National Health Services was “dedicated” to ensuring that citizens had access to high-quality and effective therapeutic products.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment.
